findings.refined_fix: Add `Control::reserve_object_bytes(name, size, max_total) -> ApiResult<bool>` running `UPDATE repos SET object_bytes = object_bytes + ?2 WHERE name = ?1 AND (?3 = 0 OR object_bytes + ?2 <= ?3)` and returning rows_affected > 0 (use `sql_params![name, size as i64, max_total as i64]`). In the closure, once `!existed`, call it and return QuotaExceeded on false. Replace the later `add_object_bytes(+size)` with a compensating `add_object_bytes(name, -(size as i64))` if `put` fails. Test with N concurrent uploads against a small quota.

findings.excerpt:
max_changeset_ops: 100_000,
max_changesets_per_publication: 10_000,
findings.problem: Negotiate advertises two limits as literals instead of the values the engine enforces (ag_types::limits::Limits::default() / Repository::limits(): max_ops 100_000, max_changesets_per_publication 10_000). They agree today by coincidence and will drift silently as soon as the engine limit changes or is made configurable, making the advertised protocol contract false.
findings.proposed_fix: Fill them from ag_types::limits::Limits::default() (or the server's configured Limits) and add a test asserting the advertised values equal the engine's.
reasons: session.rs negotiate advertises `max_changeset_ops: 100_000` and `max_changesets_per_publication: 10_000` as literals. They equal ag_types::Limits::default() (max_ops, max_changesets_per_publication), which the engine uses (repo.rs:140 `Limits::default()`), so they agree only by coincidence and can drift.

The two literals equal ag_types::limits::Limits::default() (100_000 and 10_000), and the server never customizes engine limits (repo.rs:140 uses Limits::default() and nothing in config changes it). The advertised values are therefore correct today and cannot drift through configuration. Replacing the literals would only be a refactor.
findings.refined_fix: In negotiate: `let engine = ag_types::Limits::default();` then `max_changeset_ops: u32::try_from(engine.max_ops).unwrap_or(u32::MAX), max_changesets_per_publication: u32::try_from(engine.max_changesets_per_publication).unwrap_or(u32::MAX),`. Note the export path is `ag_types::Limits`, not `ag_types::limits::Limits`. Add a test comparing the advertised values with `Repository::limits()` of a fresh repository.

findings.problem: `ag-server admin ...` ignores the real configuration file: there is no --config flag, so `admin create-repo` always creates a SQLite + filesystem repository even when the deployment uses [repos.storage] PostgreSQL/S3, with a hardcoded Quota::default() (main.rs:245) instead of the configured defaults. `admin mint` has a hardcoded `--ttl` default of 3600 (main.rs:78) and does not enforce auth.max_ttl_secs/max_agent_ttl_secs; `admin repos` silently truncates at 10_000 (main.rs:250); `--default-stream` default "main" duplicates config.
findings.proposed_fix: Give Admin the same --config/AG_SERVER_CONFIG option as Serve and build App from the loaded config; apply the configured TTL caps, default quota, default stream and storage template; page through all repos. Test create-repo against a Postgres/S3 config.
reasons: The headline claim is stale. `Admin` now has `--config`/AG_SERVER_CONFIG and copies `repos`, `control` and `server.data_dir` from the loaded config (main.rs ~237-246), so create-repo uses the configured PostgreSQL/S3 template. One real residual remains: only those three sections are loaded, so `CreateRepo` calls `repos.create(..., v1::Quota::default())` (unlimited) while the API uses `App::default_quota()` from `limits.max_total_object_bytes` and `limits.max_open_proposals`. Admin-created repos therefore get no default quota. This is narrowed to low severity.

The headline is refuted. main.rs:55-62 gives Admin a --config/AG_SERVER_CONFIG option, and the Admin branch (about line 201) loads [repos] (so [repos.storage] PostgreSQL/S3), [control] and data_dir. The container images set it. Hardcoded mint ttl and the 10_000 repos cap are acceptable for an offline operator tool. One narrow gap remains: `create-repo` passes v1::Quota::default() and the admin config loading ignores [limits], so repos created through the documented README bootstrap path lack the configured max_open_proposals and max_total_object_bytes defaults that the API applies in default_quota().
findings.refined_fix: In the Admin branch also copy `cfg.limits = loaded.limits;`. Make `App::default_quota` `pub` (repository.rs) and in `AdminAction::CreateRepo` call `app.default_quota()` instead of `v1::Quota::default()`. Make `--default-stream` an `Option<String>` falling back to `app.cfg.repos.default_stream`. Test that an admin-created repo carries the configured default quota.

findings.problem: Deduplication is a linear scan of only the 1000 newest jobs (existing_validation_jobs at line 167 scans 500), although tx.job_enqueue already dedupes by an indexed dedupe_key. Beyond that window an existing job is missed, so a duplicate 'job.enqueue' audit entry and 'enqueued' metric are produced and prepare() under-reports existing jobs. Worse, a hit returns the existing job in ANY state: after a job failed permanently (e.g. a runner infrastructure failure) or was cancelled, request_validation / prepare(enqueue_validations) keeps returning that dead job and never queues a new one for the same (proposal, check, tree, policy_version), so validation cannot be retried until the tree changes.
findings.proposed_fix: Look the job up by dedupe_key with a Tx::job_by_key (public) instead of scanning; if the existing job is failed/cancelled, re-queue it (new Tx::job_requeue) or enqueue a fresh job with a generation suffix in the key; make existing_validation_jobs query by payload/dedupe prefix. Test: exhaust attempts, call request_validation again, expect a queued job.
reasons: enqueue_validation_jobs dedupes with `tx.job_list(None, 1000).find(dedupe_key == key)` and existing_validation_jobs scans `job_list(None, 500)`, both newest-first windows. Beyond them an existing job is missed: the code increments the 'enqueued' metric and appends a duplicate 'job.enqueue' audit row (job_enqueue_with itself returns the existing row via ON CONFLICT), and prepare() under-reports existing jobs. The 'failed job is returned forever' part is documented behaviour (docs/guides/workers.md: 'asking again returns the same job', 'after that it stays failed'), so it is dropped from the fix.

Confirmed at jobs.rs:133: dedupe scans only the newest 1000 jobs (job_list(None,1000)) and existing_validation_jobs (about line 167) scans 500. job_enqueue then dedupes through an indexed lookup, so no duplicate job is created. However a repeat request for an older job still records an extra job.enqueue audit entry and increments the 'enqueued' metric, and prepare under-reports existing jobs once the table is larger than the window. Tx::job_by_key already exists but is private. Re-queuing permanently failed jobs is a design choice (workers.md says a failed job 'stays failed'), so I exclude it.
findings.refined_fix: Make `Tx::job_by_key` public (ag-storage/src/meta/jobs.rs) and in enqueue_validation_jobs use `match tx.job_by_key(&key)? { Some(j) => Ok(j), None => { let j = tx.job_enqueue(...)?; events...inc(); tx.audit_append(...)?; Ok(j) } }`. In existing_validation_jobs look up each required check by `dedupe_key(&proposal, &check, &tree, pv)` through job_by_key instead of `job_list(None, 500)`. Test with more than 1000 later jobs in the repo and assert exactly one 'job.enqueue' audit row.

findings.problem: Only worker-driven transitions are counted/audited. When a worker dies, Tx::job_claim silently reaps expired claims inside the claimer's transaction (requeue, or state 'failed' when attempts are exhausted) with no audit entry, no 'retried'/'failed' metric increment and no event in the feed. The shipped alert AgentGitJobsFailing (increase(agwp_job_events_total{event="failed"}[1h]) > 5) and the documented metric semantics therefore never see jobs that fail permanently because their runner crashed - the most common failure mode.
findings.proposed_fix: Have job_claim (and a periodic reaper) return the list of reaped jobs with their new state; in try_claim increment job_events{retried|failed} and append a 'job.expire' audit entry for each. Add a test: claim with a tiny lease, let it expire with attempts=max, claim again, assert failed metric and audit entry.
reasons: Tx::job_claim (ag-storage jobs.rs) reaps expired claims with two bulk UPDATEs (state 'failed' when attempts >= max_attempts, else requeue) and returns nothing about them. try_claim in jobs.rs only increments the 'claimed' label and appends 'job.claim', so lease-expiry failures never reach the 'failed'/'retried' metric labels or the audit feed. The AgentGitJobsFailing alert (deploy/observability/alerts.yml:66) therefore misses them.

Confirmed. Tx::job_claim (ag-storage jobs.rs) silently UPDATEs expired claims to 'failed' or 'queued' inside the claimer's transaction, and the server's try_claim only counts and audits 'claimed'. The only 'failed'/'retried' metric increments and job.fail audit entries are in fail_job. A runner that crashes five times produces no failed metric, so the shipped AgentGitJobsFailing alert (event="failed") never sees it. workers.md documents the lease-expiry path but lists job.fail as the failure topic.
findings.refined_fix: Add `Tx::job_reap_expired(&self) -> Result<Vec<JobRow>, MetaError>` that selects ids with `state='claimed' AND claimed_until < now` first, applies the two UPDATEs and returns the rows with their new state. In try_claim call it just before `tx.job_claim`, and for each reaped job increment `events.with_label_values(&["retried"|"failed"])` by new state and `tx.audit_append("system:jobs", "job.expire", &j.id, &json!({"state": j.state.as_str(), "attempts": j.attempts}))`. Test: claim with a tiny lease at attempts=max, let it expire, claim again, assert the failed metric and the audit row.

findings.excerpt:
after_seq: q.get("after_seq").and_then(|v| v.parse().ok()).or(last_event_id).unwrap_or(u64::MAX),
heartbeat_ms: q.get("heartbeat_ms").and_then(|v| v.parse().ok()).unwrap_or(0),   (replay: line 1246 `.unwrap_or(0)`, 1247 limit; line 1239/1285 `serde_urlencoded::from_str(...).unwrap_or_default()`)
findings.problem: Malformed query parameters on the two hand-parsed event routes are silently replaced by defaults instead of rejected. `?after_seq=abc` (or a malformed query string) on the SSE route becomes u64::MAX = 'follow from now', so a client that thinks it is resuming silently skips all missed events; on replay it becomes 0 = replay the whole log. All other routes return invalid_argument for bad input.
findings.proposed_fix: Parse with serde_html_form into v1::SubscribeRequest / ReplayRequest like the generic handler (path params win), returning ApiError::invalid for unparsable values; keep Last-Event-ID as an explicit fallback. Test that after_seq=abc yields 400.
reasons: http.rs events routes: `serde_urlencoded::from_str(...).unwrap_or_default()` and `.and_then(|v| v.parse().ok()).unwrap_or(...)`. On SSE a malformed after_seq falls back to Last-Event-ID or u64::MAX ('follow from now'), so a resuming client silently skips missed events; on replay it becomes 0 (whole log). Every other route returns invalid_argument for bad input.

Confirmed at http.rs:1294-1300 and 1245-1247. In the hand-written events routes, `after_seq=abc` or a malformed query string silently becomes u64::MAX ('follow from now') for SSE or 0 (replay from the start), and `serde_urlencoded::from_str(...).unwrap_or_default()` drops the whole query. A client that thinks it is resuming (for example `after_seq=undefined`) silently skips all missed events, which contradicts the guarantee that a returning subscriber loses nothing. Every other route rejects bad input as invalid_argument.
findings.refined_fix: Define `#[derive(serde::Deserialize, Default)] struct EventsQuery { after_seq: Option<u64>, limit: Option<u32>, heartbeat_ms: Option<u32>, topics: Option<String> }` and parse with `serde_urlencoded::from_str::<EventsQuery>(query)`. On Err return `ApiError::invalid(format!("query: {e}")).with_request_id(&id).into_response()` (SSE route) or `finish(Err(..), &id)` (replay). Also reject an unparsable Last-Event-ID header with invalid_argument. Build the requests from the typed struct (`after_seq.or(last_event_id).unwrap_or(u64::MAX)` stays for the absent case). Test that `?after_seq=abc` returns 400.

findings.excerpt: `X-Request-Id` and in every error. `traceparent` is propagated into logs and traces.
findings.problem: Only traces use the traceparent (trace.rs Tracer::begin). The request log span (app.rs:207 info_span!("request", op, request_id, transport)) carries no trace/span id, Ingress.traceparent's doc ('passed through to logs', app.rs:44) is false, SpanContext::traceparent() (trace.rs:251, 'to hand to downstream calls') is never called, and no response header or downstream call (JWKS fetch, jobs handed to workers) carries a traceparent, so there is no propagation beyond continuing an inbound trace.
findings.proposed_fix: Add trace_id/span_id fields to the request log span when a span is recorded, optionally return a `traceparent` response header and store it in job payloads so worker spans link; otherwise correct the docs and the Ingress comment and delete the unused SpanContext::traceparent.
reasons: app.rs dispatch creates the log span as `info_span!("request", op, request_id, transport)` with no trace or span id, so docs/protocol/agwp-v1.md:66 ('traceparent is propagated into logs and traces') and the Ingress.traceparent doc ('passed through to logs') are false for logs. Ingress.traceparent is consumed only by `Tracer::begin`, which yields nothing when OTLP is off. SpanContext::traceparent() (trace.rs:251) has no caller.

The doc claim is false. agwp-v1.md:66 says 'traceparent is propagated into logs and traces', but only Tracer::begin uses it. The request log span in app.rs (info_span! with op, request_id, transport) carries no trace id. Ingress.traceparent's doc ('passed through to logs') is untrue, and SpanContext::traceparent() is never called. observability.md:55 describes only continuing the trace, and correlates logs by request_id.
findings.refined_fix: In dispatch declare `trace_id = tracing::field::Empty` on the request span and, when `span` is Some, call `log_span.record("trace_id", hex::encode(ctx.trace_id).as_str())`. Correct the doc line in agwp-v1.md and the Ingress comment to say the trace id is logged only when OTLP export is enabled, or parse the inbound header independent of the tracer. Delete `SpanContext::traceparent` unless it is used for a response header.

findings.excerpt: .map(|h| h.meta().read(|tx| tx.job_list(Some(JobState::Queued), 1000)).map(|v| v.len() as i64).unwrap_or(0))
findings.problem: agwp_jobs_queued is computed by loading up to 1000 full JobRow records (with JSON payloads) per known repository just to take len(): it saturates at 1000 per repo (documented in metrics.rs:34 and observability.md, but the cap is arbitrary), errors are swallowed to 0, and only repositories in the in-memory job_repos hint are counted, so a backlog on a repo the hint lost is invisible to the AgentGitJobsBacklog alert. server.rs:167 also maps a join error to 0.
findings.proposed_fix: Add Tx::job_count(state) (SELECT COUNT(*)), count across all repositories (or maintain per-repo counters), and propagate errors as a scrape failure/an error counter instead of reporting 0.
reasons: jobs.rs count_queued_jobs loads up to 1000 full JobRow records (with JSON payloads) per repo only to take `.len()`, silently maps errors to 0 (`unwrap_or(0)`), and counts only repos in Local.job_repos, which claim_job prunes whenever a claim returns None. The /metrics handler in server.rs also does `unwrap_or(0)` on a join error. It runs on every Prometheus scrape (production path) and feeds the AgentGitJobsBacklog alert.

The cap is explicitly documented in metrics.rs:34 and observability.md:24 ('at most 1000 counted per repository; computed at scrape time'), and the shipped alert threshold is 50, far below it. The hint-based repo set and error-to-0 behaviour are bounded by the documented rescan design (ADR 0007). Not a hidden placeholder.
findings.refined_fix: Add `Tx::job_count(state: JobState) -> Result<u64, MetaError>` (`SELECT COUNT(*) FROM jobs WHERE state = ?1`). Make `count_queued_jobs` return `Result<i64, ApiError>` using it, and in the `metrics` handler set the gauge only on success, otherwise log a warning and increment a new `scrape_errors` counter instead of reporting 0. Rebuild the hint (rebuild_job_index) before counting so repos pruned from the hint are not invisible.

findings.excerpt: const MAX_MESSAGE: usize = 16 * 1024 * 1024;
findings.problem: gRPC encode/decode limits are fixed at 16 MiB regardless of limits.max_request_bytes / max_object_bytes that Negotiate advertises (session.rs:40-41) and that the HTTP transport honours. Raising limits.max_request_bytes above 16 MiB works over HTTP but is rejected over gRPC while negotiate says otherwise; lowering has no effect on gRPC.
findings.proposed_fix: Derive max_decoding/encoding_message_size from cfg.limits (max_request_bytes for unary, chunk size for streams) and add a test that both transports reject at the same size.
reasons: grpc.rs:31 `MAX_MESSAGE = 16 MiB` is applied unconditionally in `router()` via max_decoding/encoding_message_size, while HTTP enforces cfg.limits.max_request_bytes (http.rs:100) and Negotiate advertises that value. Raising max_request_bytes above 16 MiB works over HTTP but is rejected over gRPC; lowering it has no effect on gRPC.

Confirmed at grpc.rs:31 and 608: encode/decode limits are a fixed 16 MiB while negotiate advertises the configurable cfg.limits.max_request_bytes and config.validate() does not bound it. With the default 8 MiB there is no problem, but an operator who raises max_request_bytes above 16 MiB gets requests that HTTP accepts and gRPC rejects, contradicting the advertised limit.
findings.refined_fix: In `router()` compute `let max_in = (g.app.cfg.limits.max_request_bytes as usize).max(ag_protocol::limits::CHUNK_BYTES + 64 * 1024);` and use `.max_decoding_message_size(max_in).max_encoding_message_size(max_in.max(MAX_MESSAGE))` in `svc!`, so the decode limit follows the configuration while chunked object streams still fit. Add a test that HTTP and gRPC reject a unary request of the same size.

findings.excerpt: let size = repo.blob(&e.content).map(|b| b.len() as u64).unwrap_or(0);   (also line 40 `repo.blob_len(&e.content)?.unwrap_or(0)`, line 125 `e.size = repo.blob_len(&id)?.unwrap_or(0);`)
findings.problem: resolve_path reads the entire blob (up to 256 MiB) just to learn its size and turns any error (corrupt or missing object) into size 0, while the sibling paths use the metadata-only blob_len. A missing/corrupt blob is reported as an empty file of size 0 in resolve, tree and directory listings instead of an error, hiding repository damage that fsck/verify would flag.
findings.proposed_fix: Use repo.blob_len everywhere; treat None (missing object) as ObjectMissing/ObjectCorrupt and propagate it; add a test deleting a blob from the object store and asserting the listing errors.
reasons: tree.rs resolve_path reads the whole blob (`repo.blob(&e.content).map(|b| b.len()).unwrap_or(0)`, up to 256 MiB) just to learn its size and turns any error into 0, while tree_page and list_directory use the metadata-only blob_len. Those two also map a missing object (`None`) to size 0 via `unwrap_or(0)`. A missing or corrupt blob is therefore reported as an empty file.

Confirmed at tree.rs:76: resolve_path computes the size with `repo.blob(&e.content).map(|b| b.len() as u64).unwrap_or(0)`. This reads and hash-verifies the entire blob (up to 256 MiB) just to get its length, and turns a missing or corrupt blob into size 0. The sibling paths use the metadata-only blob_len, but still `.unwrap_or(0)` on None (missing object), so a damaged repository lists as empty files instead of an error.
findings.refined_fix: Add a helper in tree.rs: `fn blob_size(repo: &Repository, id: &ag_types::BlobId) -> ApiResult<u64> { repo.blob_len(id)?.ok_or_else(|| ApiError::new(ag_protocol::ErrorCode::ObjectMissing, format!("blob {id} is missing from the object store"))) }`. Use it in resolve_path (replacing `repo.blob(..)`), tree_page and list_directory. Test: remove a blob from the store and assert resolve, tree and list return object_missing.

findings.excerpt:
let verified = verify(tx, &row).ok();
out.push(convert::provenance_entry(&row, verified.as_ref()));
findings.problem: Any error from provenance verification (bad signature, unknown key, but also a database error) is swallowed into verified = false, and convert::provenance_entry then drops the record body (record: None) so the caller cannot tell tampering from an I/O fault and loses the stored data. Integrity results should never degrade silently.
findings.proposed_fix: Distinguish AgentError::Verification (return the stored record with verified=false and a reason field) from infrastructure errors (propagate). Extend ProvenanceEntry with `verification_error`.
reasons: agents.rs list_provenance does `verify(tx, &row).ok()`, and convert::provenance_entry sets `record: None` and `verified: false` for None. ag_agent::provenance::verify returns AgentError::Verification for tamper/unknown key but also propagates metadata (database) errors through the same Result. A DB fault is thus reported as an unverified record with its body dropped.

Failing closed is the intended behaviour: the proto field is `verified` and agents.rs reports verified=false whenever verification cannot be established, and convert::provenance_entry withholds the record body of an unverified (untrusted) record on purpose. An I/O error inside the read transaction that also runs provenance_for would normally have failed that call first. The unverified result is the safe direction, so this is deliberate, not silent degradation.
findings.refined_fix: Collect `(row, verify(tx,&row))` pairs inside `repo.meta().read`, then outside it: `let rec = match v { Ok(r) => Some(r), Err(ag_agent::AgentError::Verification(_)) => None, Err(e) => return Err(e.into()) };` (ApiError already converts from AgentError, error.rs:140) before calling `convert::provenance_entry(&row, rec.as_ref())`. Optionally add a `verification_error` string to v1::ProvenanceEntry.

findings.excerpt: pub fn ingress_from_headers(headers: &HeaderMap, remote: Option<String>) -> Ingress {   (every call site passes `None`; app.rs:47 `pub remote: Option<String>` is never read)
findings.problem: The peer address is collected only for gRPC and never for HTTP (all HTTP handlers pass None although the server is built with into_make_service_with_connect_info::<SocketAddr>()), and Ingress.remote ('Peer address, for logs') is not read anywhere - not in the request log span, not in auth-failure logs, not in the audit log. Source IPs of failed authentications are therefore unavailable.
findings.proposed_fix: Extract axum::extract::ConnectInfo<SocketAddr> (and trusted X-Forwarded-For via config) in the HTTP handlers, add `remote` to the request tracing span and to auth-failure log lines.
reasons: Ingress.remote is filled only by gRPC (grpc.rs:68 `req.remote_addr()`); every HTTP handler calls `ingress_from_headers(&headers, None)` although server.rs serves with `into_make_service_with_connect_info::<SocketAddr>()` and nothing reads `Ingress.remote` (grep shows only the definition and the gRPC assignment). Source IPs are never logged for HTTP or failed authentications.

Confirmed: ingress_from_headers is always called with None for the remote on HTTP (http.rs and server.rs call sites), and Ingress.remote (documented 'for logs') is never read anywhere, including on gRPC where it is filled in. The server is already built with into_make_service_with_connect_info::<SocketAddr>(), so the information is available. Failed authentications cannot be tied to a source address.
findings.refined_fix: Add `axum::extract::ConnectInfo<SocketAddr>` to the HTTP handlers (and the generic route! macro) and pass `Some(addr.to_string())` instead of `None`. In `App::dispatch` add `remote = ing.remote.as_deref().unwrap_or("")` to the `request` info_span and include it in the auth-failure log line. Honour X-Forwarded-For only behind an explicit `server.trusted_proxies` option.

findings.problem: 'Runs create at most once per (scope, key)' is only true within one healthy process: create() and the idempotency record are two separate transactions, so a crash or write error between them leaves the object created but unrecorded and a retry with the same key creates it again; the guard is a single process-wide mutex that serializes every keyed creation across all repositories and does nothing across processes. Records are never expired.
findings.proposed_fix: Record the key inside the same repository transaction as the creation (as propose_idempotent does), or use a UNIQUE(scope,key) row inserted first; scope locking per repository; add a TTL/cleanup for idempotency rows.
reasons: api/mod.rs idempotent_create runs `create()` and the idempotency `meta_set` in two separate transactions, so a crash or write error between them leaves the object created without a record and a retry with the same key creates it again. A single process-wide `static KEYED_CREATE` mutex serialises all keyed creations across repositories, protects nothing across processes, and records are never expired. It is used by run.start, task.create and lease.acquire (agents.rs), against the docs' idempotency promise.

Confirmed at api/mod.rs:34-69: create() and the idempotency record are two separate transactions, and the only guard is a process-wide static Mutex that also serializes all keyed creations across all repositories. A crash between them, or a retry that lands on another replica while the first is still running (shared PostgreSQL+S3 repositories), creates the object twice. That contradicts ADR 0007's invariant that a killed replica 'double-applies nothing; clients retry against another replica'. Used by start_run, create_task and acquire lease.
findings.refined_fix: Make the record part of the creation transaction: change the three creators to take a closure that runs inside the same `repo.meta().write(|tx| ...)` and call `tx.meta_set(&slot, ...)` there (as propose_idempotent does). Replace the global mutex with a per-`(repo, slot)` lock (e.g. a sharded `[Mutex<()>; 64]` indexed by hash) and add a periodic TTL cleanup of `idem:` meta keys.

findings.excerpt: if Authorizer::roles(p, std::slice::from_ref(b), &b.repo.replace('*', "x")).contains(&b.role) {
findings.problem: whoami decides which role bindings apply to the caller by substituting 'x' for '*' in the binding's repository glob and matching that invented repository name. It is wrong for globs with ?, [..] or {a,b} (the substituted name does not match its own pattern, so a held role is not reported) and for patterns where 'x' is excluded by a more specific sibling. The reported roles are a guess, not the real authorization result.
findings.proposed_fix: Add Authorizer::bindings_for(principal, bindings) that evaluates only the subject match and returns the binding's own repo pattern, and use it here (and in list_roles).
reasons: session.rs whoami checks each binding with `Authorizer::roles(p, [b], &b.repo.replace('*', "x"))`. Bindings use globset patterns (authz.rs glob_match -> `Glob::new`), which support `?`, `[..]` and `{a,b}`; the substituted name `x` need not match its own pattern, so a held role is then not reported.

Documented binding patterns are `*` globs only (acme/web, acme/*, *), and for those the substitution `*` -> `x` always matches its own pattern, so whoami lists the correct bindings. The 'excluded by a sibling' scenario cannot occur because roles() is called with a single-binding slice. Patterns with ?, [..] or {a,b} are outside the documented syntax, and the roles list is informational (authorization itself uses Authorizer::check).
findings.refined_fix: In authz.rs split the subject test out of `Authorizer::roles` into `pub fn subject_matches(principal: &Principal, b: &Binding) -> bool` (the `glob_match(&b.subject, ident) || glob_match(&b.subject, base) || groups` expression). In whoami iterate `bindings.iter().filter(|b| Authorizer::subject_matches(p, b))` and push `format!("{}:{}", b.repo, b.role.as_str())` using the binding's own pattern. Test with a `{a,b}/web` binding.

findings.excerpt: let mut rows = repo.meta().read(|tx| tx.proposals_list(state, 100_000))?;   (also line 28 `proposals_list(Some("open"), 100_000)`)
findings.problem: list_proposals loads up to 100_000 rows into memory, filters in Rust and then slices an offset page (paginate); proposals beyond the cap are silently invisible and the open-proposal quota check counts at most 100_000 rows (loading all of them on every create). Offset tokens over an in-memory snapshot also shift when proposals are created between pages.
findings.proposed_fix: Push state/stream/author filtering and keyset pagination (created_at,id) into the meta store (proposals_page) and use SELECT COUNT(*) for the quota.
reasons: proposals.rs list_proposals calls `tx.proposals_list(state, 100_000)`, filters stream/author in Rust, and paginates by offset over that in-memory snapshot. Proposals beyond the cap are invisible, offsets shift as proposals are created, and the open-proposal quota check in create_proposal loads up to 100_000 rows on every create just to take `.len()`.

The 100_000-row cap is far above any realistic proposal count per repository and the page tokens are plain offsets, which is a common documented pagination style here (paginate() in api/mod.rs). The quota check loading open proposals is an efficiency detail, not a placeholder. Proposal volumes of this size would first hit other limits, so this is not a defect worth fixing.
findings.refined_fix: Add `Tx::proposals_count(state: &str) -> Result<u64,_>` (`SELECT COUNT(*)`) and use it in create_proposal's quota check. Add `Tx::proposals_page(state, stream, author, after: Option<(i64,&str)>, limit)` with `WHERE ... AND (created_at, id) < (?, ?) ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC LIMIT ?`, and encode `(created_at,id)` in the page token instead of an offset.

findings.excerpt: app.cfg.server.cors_origins.iter().filter_map(|o| HeaderValue::from_str(o).ok()).collect();
findings.problem: Invalid CORS origins from the operator's configuration are silently dropped; if every entry is invalid CorsLayer is installed with an empty allow-list and the Web UI on another origin fails with no server-side message. config.validate() does not check cors_origins.
findings.proposed_fix: Validate cors_origins in ServerConfig::validate (scheme://host[:port], no path, or *) and fail startup; remove the filter_map.
reasons: server.rs cors() builds the allow-list with `filter_map(|o| HeaderValue::from_str(o).ok())`, silently dropping invalid origins, and installs the CorsLayer even when the list ends up empty. ServerConfig::validate (config.rs ~361) validates many sections but not server.cors_origins, so a typo gives a broken Web UI with no server message.

HeaderValue::from_str only rejects strings with control or non-ASCII bytes, so the filter_map drops almost nothing in practice. An origin that is merely wrongly formatted (such as a trailing slash) is a valid header value and is kept, so the claimed silent-empty-allow-list scenario is practically unreachable. Validating origin syntax in config.validate() would be a nicety, not the defect described.
findings.refined_fix: In `ServerConfig::validate` add: `for o in &self.server.cors_origins { let host = o.strip_prefix("https://").or_else(|| o.strip_prefix("http://")); if host.is_none_or(|h| h.is_empty() || h.contains('/')) || axum::http::HeaderValue::from_str(o).is_err() { return bad(&format!("server.cors_origins entry '{o}' must look like https://host[:port] without a path")); } }`. Keep the filter in cors() but add a `tracing::warn!` for any dropped entry.

findings.problem: agwp_integrations_total is documented as integrations by outcome (integrated, blocked, conflict, denied, invalid) but run_queue only counts successes; blocked/rejected/failed queue entries are never counted, so the error-ratio dashboards under-report non-integrations from the queue. Outcomes are also inferred from the queue-entry state string.
findings.proposed_fix: Map every processed entry to its Outcome status (the queue entry stores the outcome) and increment the matching label; test blocked-in-queue increments blocked.
reasons: integration.rs run_queue increments `integrations{outcome="integrated"}` only for processed entries with state "done". docs/operations/observability.md:20 documents the outcomes integrated, blocked, conflict, denied and invalid, and metrics.rs describes the counter as 'Integration attempts by outcome', so blocked or rejected queue entries are never counted.

Confirmed at integration.rs:210-214: run_queue increments agwp_integrations_total only for processed queue entries in state "done". Blocked, rejected and failed queue entries are never counted, although the metric is documented as 'Integration attempts by outcome' with blocked/conflict/denied/invalid labels (observability.md:20) and the dashboard shows 'integrations by outcome'. The integrate() path counts every outcome, so the queue path under-reports.
findings.refined_fix: Replace the loop with a mapping over `p.state`: `"done" => "integrated", "blocked" => "blocked", "rejected" => "conflict", _ => "invalid"` (confirm the exact label per queue state against ag-integrate/src/queue.rs, and use `QueueRow.outcome` when present) and `.with_label_values(&[label]).inc()`. Test that a blocked proposal in the queue increments `outcome="blocked"`.

findings.excerpt: .map(|i| v1::FsckIssue { kind: i.kind.clone(), object: String::new(), detail: i.detail.clone() })
findings.problem: FsckIssue.object is part of the protocol but is always the empty string because the engine's FsckIssue has no object field, so API clients and the Web UI cannot tell which object is corrupt.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `object: Option<String>` to ag_integrate::FsckIssue, fill it where fsck detects corrupt/missing objects, and map it here.
reasons: admin.rs fsck maps every issue to `v1::FsckIssue { object: String::new(), .. }`, and ag_integrate::FsckIssue (fsck.rs:13) has only `kind` and `detail`. The protocol field is therefore always empty, although fsck.rs knows the object id at most sites (e.g. `info.id` for corrupt_object/missing_object) and currently embeds it only in the free-text detail.

The engine's FsckIssue has no object field, but every issue's `detail` already starts with the object or changeset id (fsck.rs: "{id}: {why}", "missing_object" detail is the id). Clients can identify the object from detail. The empty `object` field is a minor unused protocol slot, not misleading data.
findings.refined_fix: Add `pub object: Option<String>` to ag_integrate::FsckIssue, change `Report::issue` to take it (`issue(kind, object: Option<String>, detail)`), fill it for corrupt_object, missing_object, bad_blob, index_mismatch, dangling_parent and unreadable_changeset, and map `object: i.object.clone().unwrap_or_default()` in admin.rs.

findings.problem: An empty branch that evaluates a condition and does nothing; a reader assumes a check exists. The same pattern at lines 283-286 (`if out.is_empty() && ... { return Ok(ListCredentialsResponse { credentials: out }); }` followed by the identical return) is a branch that cannot change the result, with a comment about hiding existence that nothing implements.
findings.proposed_fix: Delete both dead branches (the narrowing is already enforced by `me.scope.contains(&wanted)` above); keep the comment on the actual check.
reasons: admin.rs mint_credential has an empty `else if me.scope.is_unrestricted() && ... { // Self-minting is always allowed ... }` branch (no statements), and list_credentials has `if out.is_empty() && subject != "*" && subject != me { return Ok(ListCredentialsResponse { credentials: out }); }` followed by the identical return. Both are dead code with misleading comments in an authorization path.

The empty `else if` branch and the redundant early return are dead code with no behavioural effect: scope containment is enforced by `me.scope.contains(&wanted)` above, and list_credentials already hides credentials the caller cannot manage by filtering through may_manage_credential, so nothing is leaked. It is harmless clutter, not a stub that misleads about a missing check.
findings.refined_fix: Delete the empty `else if` block and the redundant `if out.is_empty() ... { return ... }` in list_credentials, keeping a one-line comment that self-minting only narrows (enforced by `me.scope.contains(&wanted)` above).

findings.excerpt: repo.meta().read(|tx| tx.leases_all(500))?
findings.problem: list_leases with active_only=false returns at most the newest 500 leases with no indication of truncation or paging.
findings.proposed_fix: Add page_size/page_token to ListLeasesRequest (keyset by acquired_at,id) or return a `truncated` flag.
reasons: agents.rs list_leases with active_only=false calls `tx.leases_all(500)`: a fixed cap, no request field to raise it or page, and no truncation indicator in ListLeasesResponse, unlike runs/jobs, which accept `limit`. Older leases are silently unreachable.

list_leases(active_only=false) returning the 500 newest leases is an administrative history view, and the default active_only listing (the operational one) is not capped. A fixed cap on a history listing is an acceptable documented-by-code limit, not a hidden placeholder.
findings.refined_fix: Add `uint32 limit = 3;` to ListLeasesRequest and `bool truncated = 2;` to ListLeasesResponse in proto/agwp/v1/agwp.proto. In the handler use `let limit = if req.limit == 0 { 100 } else { req.limit.min(1000) } as usize;`, fetch `leases_all(limit + 1)`, truncate to `limit` and set `truncated = fetched.len() > limit`.

findings.problem: The job index rebuild (startup and the 5 s rescan) silently returns on a control-DB error, ignores repositories it cannot open and treats read errors as 'no jobs', so work in a temporarily unreadable repository is invisible to claim_job (with an empty `repo`) until a later rescan - with no log line. It also opens every repository (up to the max_open pool, evicting hot ones) on each rescan and caps at 100_000 repos.
findings.proposed_fix: Log failures with the repository name, count them in a metric, iterate with paging instead of a 100_000 literal, and prefer a control-plane table of repos-with-queued-jobs updated on enqueue/claim so no repository needs opening.
reasons: jobs.rs rebuild_job_index (startup plus the periodic rescan) does `let Ok(repos) = self.control.repos("", "", 100_000) else { return };` and `if let Ok(h) = self.repos.handle(..) && h.meta().read(..).map(..).unwrap_or(false)`, so any control-DB, open or read error is silently treated as 'no jobs' with no log line. Queued work in an unreadable repo stays invisible to claim_job until a later rescan, and the 100_000 cap is silent.

This is the documented polling safety net (ADR 0007: 'job claimers rescan every 5 s', 'costs latency, never correctness'). Transient errors only delay discovery until the next rescan, and cluster notices announce new work immediately. Scaling concerns about opening many repositories per rescan are a design trade-off, not a hardcoded placeholder, and a logging nicety does not make the finding a defect.
findings.refined_fix: Page through repos (`let mut after = String::new(); loop { let rows = match self.control.repos("", &after, 500) { Ok(r) => r, Err(e) => { tracing::warn!(error = ?e, "job index rescan: cannot list repositories"); return; } }; let Some(last) = rows.last().map(|r| r.name.clone()) else { break }; for row in &rows { match self.repos.handle(&row.name) { Ok(h) => match h.meta().read(|tx| tx.job_list(Some(JobState::Queued), 1)) { Ok(v) if !v.is_empty() => self.note_jobs_queued(&row.name), Ok(_) => {} Err(e) => tracing::warn!(repo = %row.name, error = ?e, "job index rescan: cannot read jobs") }, Err(e) => tracing::warn!(repo = %row.name, error = ?e, "job index rescan: cannot open repository") } } after = last; }`).

findings.problem: claim_job removes a repository from the in-memory hint when its claim returned None; a job enqueued between that claim and the removal (note_jobs_queued ran first) is dropped from the hint and only found by the 5 s rescan, which is triggered only inside an ongoing long-poll after a timeout and only when the hint is entirely empty. Short-poll workers (wait_ms=0) may not see the job for a long time, and jobs queued by another server process are discovered only through this scan.
findings.proposed_fix: Re-check the repo after removal (or remove only if job_list(Queued,1) is still empty in the same transaction), and make the rescan independent of long-polling (background interval task).
reasons: claim_job (empty `repo`) removes the repo from Local.job_repos whenever try_claim returns None. A job announced between that claim and the removal (note_jobs inserts the hint) loses its hint. A retry-delayed job (fail_job with retry_after_ms: queued but run_after in the future) also loses the hint at the first None claim, so nothing re-adds it when run_after passes. `rescan_jobs_if_due` runs only inside a long-poll loop after the deadline check, so wait_ms=0 workers never trigger it.

The race window is tiny (between a None claim and the hint removal) and the delay is bounded: ag-worker long-polls (wait_ms) and claim_job calls rescan_jobs_if_due on every wait iteration, so the repo is rediscovered within about 5 s. ADR 0007 documents this rescan as the correctness floor. It is a latency effect, not lost work.
findings.refined_fix: After removing the hint in claim_job, re-check cheaply and restore it: `if req.repo.is_empty() { self.local.job_repos.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()).remove(&repo); let (app, r) = (self.clone(), repo.clone()); let still = tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || app.repos.handle(&r).ok().is_some_and(|h| h.meta().read(|tx| tx.job_list(Some(JobState::Queued), 1)).map(|v| !v.is_empty()).unwrap_or(true))).await.unwrap_or(true); if still { self.local.job_repos.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()).insert(repo.clone()); } }`. This keeps repos that only have delayed or just-enqueued jobs in the hint.

findings.problem: The stored error is truncated to a literal 2000 characters but the audit entry written in the same transaction (and hash-chained forever) receives the full, untrusted req.error, which can be up to max_request_bytes (8 MiB) - an unbounded write amplification into the append-only audit log.
findings.proposed_fix: Truncate once (named constant, ideally configurable) and use the truncated string for both the job row and the audit entry.
reasons: jobs.rs fail_job stores `req.error.chars().take(2000)` in the job row but appends the audit entry with the full `json!({"error": req.error, ..})`. req.error is bounded only by max_request_bytes (8 MiB), so an authenticated runner can write multi-MiB entries into the append-only, hash-chained audit log.

Confirmed at jobs.rs:423-431: the job row stores `req.error` truncated to 2000 chars, but the audit entry written in the same transaction receives the full `req.error`. The error comes from a runner (limited only by max_request_bytes, 8 MiB over HTTP and 16 MiB over gRPC), and audit entries are append-only, hash-chained and delivered to event subscribers. complete_job also writes the unbounded worker result into its audit entry.
findings.refined_fix: Before `with_repo_mut` add `const MAX_JOB_ERROR_CHARS: usize = 2000; let error: String = req.error.chars().take(MAX_JOB_ERROR_CHARS).collect();`, move it into the closure, pass `&error` to `tx.job_fail(&req.job_id, &worker, &error, retry)?` and use `json!({"error": error, "state": j.state.as_str()})` for the audit entry.

findings.excerpt: ing.deadline_ms = Some(u64::MAX / 4);   (same in grpc.rs:487)
findings.problem: A magic sentinel is used to disable the deadline for streams; app.rs:221-223 then exports it as the span attribute agwp.deadline_ms (~4.6e18) and as the Request-deadline of the trace, and the `events.subscribe` span/latency histogram only measure stream setup.
findings.proposed_fix: Model 'no deadline' explicitly (Ingress.no_deadline: bool or Option<Option<u64>>) and omit the attribute.
reasons: http.rs:1319 and grpc.rs:487 set `ing.deadline_ms = Some(u64::MAX / 4)`, and app.rs dispatch exports any Some deadline as the span attribute `agwp.deadline_ms` (clamped to i64::MAX), so every events.subscribe span carries ~4.6e18. This is bogus telemetry, though cosmetic and low severity.

u64::MAX/4 is a deliberate sentinel for 'no deadline' on long-lived streams, and the only effect is an unusual value in the agwp.deadline_ms span attribute of the events.subscribe span. This is a cosmetic telemetry detail, not a misleading or harmful placeholder.
findings.refined_fix: Add `pub const NO_DEADLINE_MS: u64 = u64::MAX / 4;` in app.rs, use it in http.rs and grpc.rs, and in dispatch only push the attribute when `d < NO_DEADLINE_MS` (`if let Some(d) = ing.deadline_ms.filter(|d| *d < NO_DEADLINE_MS)`).

findings.problem: The 'chunked streaming' of object and file downloads is a stream::iter over a fully materialised Vec: the whole object (up to 256 MiB) is read into memory by get_object/file_content, then copied again chunk by chunk (2x). Uploads (ObjectSink, HTTP PUT collect()) likewise buffer the whole object before store_object. With max_concurrent_requests = 512 the memory bound is 512 x 256 MiB. The advertised objects.chunked feature does not reduce server memory.
findings.proposed_fix: Expose a streaming reader from the object store (get_stream/put_stream with incremental hashing) and wire both transports to it; at minimum bound total in-flight object bytes with a semaphore.
reasons: grpc.rs `chunks()` slices an already materialised Vec and ObjectSink buffers each object, which is true. But objects.chunked only promises wire framing under the 16 MiB message cap, and verification (RawObject::decode_envelope/verify) needs the whole envelope. No document promises bounded server memory, so this is a scalability limitation, not a false claim.

Only partly valid. The 'chunking' does materialize whole objects (stream::iter over a Vec in grpc.rs chunks(), full buffering in ObjectSink and HTTP PUT), but that follows from verifying the hash before storing and the docs never claim a memory bound. The real exposure is in http.rs:421-437: the PUT handler collects the body (up to 256 MiB) BEFORE app.dispatch, so it happens before authentication, rate limiting and the concurrency semaphore. Any unauthenticated client can therefore make the server buffer 256 MiB per connection, while the 512 x 256 MiB bound the finding cites does not even apply to this path.
findings.refined_fix: Do not rewrite the object store for streaming. In the PUT /objects/{id} handler move the `Limited::new(...).collect()` into the dispatch closure (so it runs after the concurrency permit, authentication and rate limit). Additionally bound in-flight object bytes with a weighted tokio Semaphore (new `limits.max_inflight_object_bytes`, default for example 1 GiB) acquired per upload, and document in agwp-v1.md that `objects.chunked` is framing, not a memory bound. Test: unauthenticated PUT with a large body returns 401 without being buffered.

findings.excerpt: s.split(',').filter_map(|kv| { let (k, v) = kv.split_once('=')?; ... (!k.is_empty() && k.bytes().all(...) && !v.is_empty()).then(...)
findings.problem: Malformed entries in OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS (e.g. a header whose value contains a comma, or a bad name) are silently discarded, so an authentication header for a hosted collector can vanish and the only symptom is 401s counted in trace_export_failures.
findings.proposed_fix: Return an error from parse_headers and fail start-up (or log the offending name, never the value).
reasons: app.rs parse_headers drops any `name=value` entry that fails the `split_once('=')`, name-charset or non-empty-value checks, without logging, so a mistyped auth header for a hosted collector disappears and the only symptom is 401s in trace_export_failures. Low severity.

parse_headers follows the OTLP header-list convention, where malformed entries are ignored, and a wrong or missing header shows up as export failures counted in agwp_trace_export_failures_total and the warning log naming the endpoint and collector status. The format is documented in observability.md. Failing startup for a lenient optional telemetry setting would be a policy choice, not a defect.
findings.refined_fix: In parse_headers replace the silent `filter_map` rejection with a `tracing::warn!(entry = i, name = %k_or_placeholder, "ignoring malformed entry in the OTLP headers variable")` for each rejected entry (log the index and the name, never the value), keeping the return type unchanged.

findings.excerpt:
WHERE (?1 IS NULL OR subject = ?1) AND (?2 IS NULL OR repo = ?2) ORDER BY subject, repo, role LIMIT 5000
... .filter_map(|b| Some(Binding { ..., role: Role::parse(&b.role)? }))
findings.problem: (Adjacent area.) all_bindings, which feeds every authorization decision, silently drops bindings beyond 5000 and any row with an unknown role string; credentials listing is capped at LIMIT 1000 (line 248). Authorization data is truncated without a warning.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove the LIMIT for the authorizer query (paginate only API listings), and log/count rows with unknown roles.
reasons: control/mod.rs `roles()` ends with `ORDER BY subject, repo, role LIMIT 5000`, and `all_bindings()` (the only source for authorization, cached in App::bindings) builds on it and silently drops rows with an unknown role via `filter_map(.. Role::parse(..)?)`. Beyond 5000 bindings, those sorted last (by subject) silently lose access. It fails closed, so the severity is low.

Truncation fails closed: dropping bindings beyond 5000 (or with an unknown role string) can only remove access, never grant it, and the code comment states the design assumption that bindings are few and cached. 5000 explicit bindings is far beyond the documented usage (pattern bindings like agent:* / acme/*), and the 1000 credentials cap is an API listing limit.
findings.refined_fix: Give `all_bindings` its own query without LIMIT (`SELECT subject, repo, role FROM roles`) and log `tracing::warn!(subject, repo, role, "ignoring role binding with unknown role")` for each unparsable row instead of dropping it silently. Keep `LIMIT 5000` plus a page token only for the listing API `roles()`.

findings.excerpt: timeout: Some(std::time::Duration::from_secs(120)),   (same literal again at line 355 in `clone`)
findings.problem: Every remote call, including the single client-streaming `upload_objects` of an entire push and each object download, gets a fixed 120 s deadline that an operator cannot change by flag, env var or remote config. A large initial push over a slow link is cut off by the client with a deadline error. `clone` (line 351-357) builds its own Options by hand with `..Default::default()`, so it also drops AG_RUN and the ag/<version> user agent that `connect()` sets, a divergent duplicate of the connection logic.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `timeout` (and `connect_timeout`) to the Remote config and to clone/remote-add flags plus an AG_TIMEOUT env override. Use a much larger or no overall deadline for bulk transfer (upload/get_object) and keep per-call deadlines for unary calls. Make clone call the same `connect()` helper. Verify with an ag-server integration test that pushes a multi-hundred-MB history through a throttled proxy with a short and a long configured timeout.
reasons: Verified. connect() in remote.rs calls connect_with_timeout(.., 120s), and there is no flag, env var or config to change it. push sends every missing object in one upload_objects client stream under that single deadline (remote.rs ~552-558), so a slow link can hit the deadline. clone (remote.rs ~401) builds Options by hand with a second 120s literal and ..Default::default(), which drops AG_RUN and the ag/<version> user agent that connect() sets.

remote.rs connect() hard-codes 120 s, and clone() repeats the literal with its own Options (no AG_RUN, no user agent). Nothing overrides it: only `ag doctor --timeout` exists. push() sends every object in one client-streaming upload_objects call built with client.req(), so the whole push must finish inside 120 s and a large first push over a slow link fails.
findings.refined_fix: In crates/ag-cli/src/cmds/remote.rs add `fn call_timeout() -> Duration` that reads AG_TIMEOUT (seconds, >0) and falls back to 120s. Use it in connect(). Extract one `fn options_for(r: &Remote, token: String, timeout: Duration) -> Options` that sets run from AG_RUN, user_agent `ag/<version>` and ca_file. Use it in connect_with_timeout and in clone (replace the hand-built Options at ~line 396-403). For the bulk calls (Client::upload_objects and get_object) either skip set_timeout or send the objects in size-bounded batches, so the unary-call deadline does not cap a whole push.

findings.excerpt: page_size: 200,   // remote proposals;  `limit: 500,` (line 967, remote events replay);  `page_size: 1000,` (line 230, fetch);  `heartbeat_ms: 15_000,` (line 949);  `max_commits: 0` (line 1043, remote blame)
findings.problem: `ag remote proposals` requests one page of 200 and never follows `next_page_token`, so any repository with more than 200 proposals is silently truncated with no indication. `ag remote events` replays at most 500 events and does not report that more remain (the response carries latest_seq, which is ignored). `ag remote log -n` is clamped by the server to 1000 without notice. Page sizes are magic numbers that duplicate ag_protocol::limits::MAX_PAGE_SIZE, the follow heartbeat is hard-wired, and `remote blame` cannot pass --max-commits although local `ag blame` can (it sends 0 = server default).
findings.proposed_fix: Loop on next_page_token until exhausted (or until an explicit --limit), print a `(more: use --after <seq>)` hint or loop for events based on latest_seq, derive page sizes from ag_protocol::limits / negotiated Limits, expose --max-commits and --heartbeat flags. Verify against a real ag-server holding >1000 proposals and >5000 audit events that `--json` returns every row.
reasons: Verified. RemoteCmd::Proposals sends page_size: 200 and prints a single page, and ListProposalsRequest has a page_token that the CLI never uses. RemoteCmd::Events replay hardcodes limit: 500 and ignores ReplayResponse.latest_seq. Blame hardcodes max_commits: 0, and `remote log -n` is passed straight to the server's clamp. In text mode the truncation is silent. In --json mode next_page_token is visible but the CLI has no way to pass it back.

`remote proposals` sends page_size 200 once and never follows next_page_token, and the CLI has no way to pass a page token, so repositories with more than 200 proposals are silently truncated, in --json mode too. `remote events` replays at most 500 events and prints nothing when latest_seq shows more remain. The other points (blame --max-commits, heartbeat value, duplicated 1000 page size) are cosmetic.
findings.refined_fix: In the Proposals arm, loop with `page_size: ag_protocol::limits::MAX_PAGE_SIZE` and `page_token: token.clone()`, accumulate `page.proposals` until `next_page_token` is empty, then print `v1::ListProposalsResponse{ proposals: all, next_page_token: String::new() }`. In the Events replay arm, repeat the call with `after_seq = last.seq` while `last.seq < latest_seq`, merging the events. Add `--max-commits` to `remote blame` and pass it instead of 0. Optionally add `--limit/--all` to `remote proposals`.

findings.excerpt: let list = ctx.repo.meta().read(|tx| tx.proposals_list(state.as_deref(), 200))?;   (also agents.rs:126 `tx.runs(name.as_deref(), 50)` and agents.rs:331 `tx.leases_all(200)`)
findings.problem: Local `ag proposal list`, `ag agent runs` and `ag lease list --all` have fixed result caps (200 / 50 / 200) with no --limit flag and no truncation notice, unlike `ag log -n`, `ag op list -n` and `ag stream reflog -n`. Output on a busy repository is silently incomplete, which is dangerous for scripts consuming --json.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `-n/--limit` (default documented, `0` or `--all` for unlimited) to these three commands, and emit a stderr notice or a `truncated: true` JSON field when the cap is hit. Verify with a CLI e2e test that creates >200 proposals and >50 runs.
reasons: Verified. flow.rs:189 calls proposals_list(state, 200), agents.rs:129 calls runs(name, 50), and agents.rs:340 calls leases_all(200). proposals_list is `ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT n`. None of the three commands has a limit flag, and none prints a truncation notice. The --json output is silently cut to the newest N rows.

flow.rs:189 (proposals_list, 200), agents.rs:129 (runs, 50) and agents.rs:340 (leases_all, 200) are fixed newest-first LIMITs with no flag and no notice, unlike `ag log -n` and `ag op list -n`. No docs mention the caps, so scripts reading --json from a busy repository get incomplete data without being told.
findings.refined_fix: Add `#[arg(short = 'n', long, default_value_t = 200)] limit: usize` to `ProposalCmd::List`, with defaults of 50 for `AgentCmd::Runs` and 200 for `LeaseCmd::List --all`. Pass it to proposals_list, runs and leases_all, with 0 meaning usize::MAX/i64::MAX. When `rows.len() == limit`, call `ctx.note("showing the newest N; use -n 0 for all")`, which goes to stderr and is skipped in JSON mode.

findings.excerpt: let _ = std::fs::remove_file(root.join(".ag").join("credentials").join(name));
findings.problem: `ag remote remove` reports 'Removed remote' even when the stored credential file could not be deleted; the secret silently stays on disk.
findings.proposed_fix: Ignore only NotFound; propagate or warn (exit non-zero) on any other error so the user knows a token file remains.
reasons: Verified at remote.rs:771. `let _ = std::fs::remove_file(.ag/credentials/<name>)` runs after save_remotes and before the 'Removed remote' output, so a PermissionDenied or other I/O failure leaves the token file on disk and the command still exits 0.

remote.rs:771 `let _ = std::fs::remove_file(...)` runs after remotes.json has already been saved without the remote. On a permission error or locked file the command still prints 'Removed remote', the token stays on disk, and a retry fails with 'no remote named'.

findings.excerpt: print(cli, &ev, || format!("{:>6}  {}  {}", ev.seq, ev.topic, ev.payload_json))?;   (docs/guides/remote.md: '`--json` works everywhere'; main.rs:27 'Machine-readable JSON output.')
findings.problem: `--json` is documented as working everywhere, but `ag cat`, `ag remote cat` and `ag policy example` ignore it, and `ag remote events --follow --json` emits a stream of concatenated multi-line pretty-printed JSON objects (serde_json::to_string_pretty), which is not NDJSON and cannot be parsed line by line by a consumer.
findings.proposed_fix: Emit one compact JSON object per line for streaming output (to_string), make `--json` on cat-style commands either wrap content (base64 + metadata) or be rejected explicitly, and narrow the doc claim. Verify by piping `ag --json remote events --follow` into `jq -c .` in an e2e test against a real server.
reasons: Only partly valid. `ag cat`, `ag remote cat` and `ag policy example` are documented raw-output exceptions in help/json.md and in the golden RAW list, so that part is refuted. docs/guides/remote.md:55 saying '--json works everywhere' is a minor over-claim. Still real: `remote events --follow` goes through print() -> emit(), which uses to_string_pretty, so the stream is concatenated multi-line objects rather than line-delimited JSON, and that is not documented.

Only the streaming part holds. `ag remote events --follow --json` prints each event through emit(), which uses to_string_pretty, so the output is a stream of multi-line objects rather than one JSON document per line. The cat, remote cat and policy example complaints are legitimate: golden.rs RAW lists them deliberately as commands whose output is the data itself, and tests enforce that.
findings.refined_fix: In the follow loop of RemoteCmd::Events (remote.rs ~1000), replace the print(...) call with: `if cli.json { crate::ui::print_line(&serde_json::to_string(&ev)?); } else { print(cli, &ev, || format!("{:>6}  {}  {}", ev.seq, ev.topic, ev.payload_json))?; }`. Then in docs/guides/remote.md:55 and help/json.md say that `events --follow --json` prints one compact JSON object per line and that `cat` prints raw content.

findings.excerpt: None => ctx.repo.resolve_rev("@").or_else(|_| ctx.repo.resolve_rev(ctx.repo.default_stream().as_str())).map_err(|_| anyhow!("the repository has no history yet; create files and run `ag snapshot -m ...`")),
findings.problem: Any error from resolving the workspace head or stream (corrupt metadata, I/O or locking failure, database error) is discarded and replaced by the canned message 'the repository has no history yet', hiding real failures behind a plausible but wrong diagnosis for log/show/blame/ls/propose/diff.
findings.proposed_fix: Distinguish 'not found / no head' from other errors (match on the engine's NotFound variant) and propagate everything else unchanged. Verify with a test that corrupts .ag metadata and expects the real error.
reasons: Verified at repo.rs:284-292. rev_or_default's `.map_err(|_| anyhow!("the repository has no history yet..."))` replaces every error from resolve_rev (Meta, Store, Io and so on) with the canned message. Only Error::NotFound from resolve_base means there is no head.

repo.rs:287-291 rev_or_default maps every error from resolve_rev("@") and the default-stream lookup (Meta/Store/Io failures, not only NotFound) to 'the repository has no history yet; create files and run ag snapshot'. A locked or corrupt metadata database therefore gets a wrong diagnosis. resolve_base returns Error::NotFound for the genuinely empty case, so the cases can be told apart.

findings.problem: An invalid run id is silently dropped (`.ok()`), so the client keeps talking to the server WITHOUT the `ag-run` header and acts as the bare credential instead of the agent run the caller asked for. `connect()` correctly rejects the same input with ClientError::Invalid("bad run id"); `with_run` swallows the error and changes attribution/permissions instead.
findings.proposed_fix: Return Result<Self> and propagate ClientError::Invalid for a header-unsafe run id (share the validation with connect()). Verify with a unit test that with_run("bad\nid") is an error and a real-server test that the header is present on every call.
reasons: Dead code. `with_run` has no caller anywhere in the Rust workspace (grep over *.rs finds only the definition). ag-cli and ag-worker never call it, ag-client is publish = false, and the Python SDK has its own unrelated with_run. connect() already validates the run id for every real path.

lib.rs:173-175 `MetadataValue::try_from(r).ok()` drops an invalid run id, so the client silently sends no ag-run header. effective_actor in ag-server/src/app.rs then falls back to the bare principal (agent:name instead of agent:name#run), changing attribution, while connect() rejects the same input with ClientError::Invalid. There are no callers in the workspace today, so the risk is latent, but it is a public API.
findings.refined_fix: Extract fn run_header(r: &str) -> Result<AsciiMetadataValue> that returns ClientError::Invalid("bad run id"), use it in connect(), and change with_run to `pub fn with_run(&self, run: Option<&str>) -> Result<Self>`. Add a unit test that with_run(Some("bad\nid")) is an Err.

findings.problem: `get_file` returns whatever it received when the stream ends, even if the `last` marker never arrived, so a cleanly truncated response is returned as a complete file (`ag remote cat` writes it to stdout with exit 0). Unlike `get_object`, there is no content-hash check to catch it, and there is no use of total_size.
findings.proposed_fix: Track whether a chunk with last=true was seen (and compare total_size if provided) and return ClientError::Transport/Invalid otherwise; ideally verify the file's blob id against the tree entry. Verify with a test server that ends the stream early.
reasons: Refuted by tonic 0.14.6. A stream that ends without a grpc-status trailer (proxy truncation or RST_STREAM(NO_ERROR)) is turned into Status::unknown('missing grpc-status trailer ... possible truncation'), which `stream.message().await?` propagates. The server's chunks() always sends at least one chunk with last=true. Silent truncation would need a server bug. A missing `last` check would be defense-in-depth only.

lib.rs:312-319 get_file ends its loop on stream end and returns the bytes whether or not a chunk with last=true arrived. The server always sets last and puts total_size in the first chunk. A response that ends early therefore comes back as a complete file, and `ag remote cat` prints it with exit 0. get_object is protected by its hash check; get_file has no check at all. The trigger is unlikely, but the protocol provides the marker precisely for this.
findings.refined_fix: In get_file, track `done` (set when chunk.last is seen) and record the first chunk's total_size. After the loop return ClientError::Transport("the server ended the file stream before its last chunk") if !done, or if the first chunk's total_size != bytes.len() as u64. Add a test with a stream that stops early.

findings.excerpt:
let out = Command::new("git")
        .arg("-C")
        .arg(dir)
        .args(args)
        .env("GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT", "0")   (export.rs:66 and import.rs:49 spawn `git` directly with no environment hardening at all)
findings.problem: Git is invoked with the caller's ambient environment and the user's/system git config. GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE or GIT_INDEX_FILE exported in the environment (for example when `ag git export` runs from a git hook) override `-C <dir>` and make the bridge read or write the wrong repository; `log.showSignature=true` injects gpg output into the `git log --format=...` stream the importer parses; `i18n.logOutputEncoding` re-encodes %B before it is read with from_utf8_lossy. The binary name `git` and its location are also fixed (no AG_GIT/--git override). The three spawn sites are inconsistent with each other.
findings.proposed_fix: Route all three spawns through one helper that env_removes GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE/GIT_INDEX_FILE/GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY/GIT_CONFIG*, sets GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 and GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null (or passes -c log.showSignature=false -c i18n.logOutputEncoding=UTF-8 -c core.quotePath=false), and allows an `AG_GIT`/`--git-bin` override. Verify with roundtrip tests run with GIT_DIR pointing elsewhere and with a global config enabling showSignature.
reasons: Verified. run.rs git() sets only GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT and GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS. GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE and GIT_INDEX_FILE in the caller's environment still override `-C`, for example when run from a git hook. import.rs list_commits runs `git log --format=...` without --no-show-signature, so log.showSignature=true injects gpg lines into the parsed stream. The cat-file spawn in import.rs and the fast-import spawn in export.rs build `Command::new("git")` themselves with no env handling at all, so the three spawn sites are inconsistent.

run.rs git() sets only GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT and GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS, and the cat-file spawn in import.rs and the fast-import spawn in export.rs use no hardening at all. I reproduced it with git 2.43: `git -c log.showSignature=true log --format='%H%x1f%an%x1e'` prepends 'No signature' (and verifier error text) to the record, so parse_log would read a garbage sha and the import of a signed repository would fail. An exported GIT_DIR (for example from a git hook) also overrides `-C`.
findings.refined_fix: In crates/ag-git/src/run.rs add `pub(crate) fn git_command(dir: &Path) -> Command` that does Command::new("git").arg("-C").arg(dir), calls env_remove for GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE, GIT_INDEX_FILE, GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY, GIT_COMMON_DIR, GIT_NAMESPACE, GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES and GIT_PREFIX, and sets GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 and GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0. Use it in git(), CatFile::start and the fast-import spawn in export.rs. In list_commits add `--no-show-signature` and `--encoding=UTF-8` to the `git log` arguments.

findings.excerpt:
git(dir, &["log", "--topo-order", "--reverse", "--format=%H%x1f%P%x1f%an%x1f%ae%x1f%at%x1f%B%x1e", rev, "--"])?;
    let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(&out);
findings.problem: Commit metadata is parsed from `git log` text using in-band 0x1e/0x1f control-character separators and decoded with from_utf8_lossy. A commit message containing U+001E breaks parsing with 'unexpected log record', and non-UTF-8 author names/messages are silently replaced by U+FFFD with no report, so imported content differs from the source without any warning (only skipped paths and submodules are reported).
findings.proposed_fix: Read raw commit objects via `git cat-file --batch` (already used for blobs) and parse the header/message bytes, honouring the `encoding` header and reporting any lossy conversions in ImportReport, or at least use `git log -z` with NUL-delimited fields (NUL cannot occur in a commit). Verify with fixtures containing a latin1-encoded commit and 0x1e in a message.
reasons: Verified. list_commits frames git log with in-band U+001F/U+001E separators and decodes with String::from_utf8_lossy. A commit message containing U+001E is split into extra records. That fails with 'unexpected log record with N fields', or can inject a fabricated record. Invalid UTF-8 in author or message bytes becomes U+FFFD with no warning in ImportReport. git re-encodes commits that carry an `encoding` header, so the latin1-header case is mostly fine, but raw invalid bytes are still silently altered.

An in-band U+001E in a message makes parse_log fail loudly ('unexpected log record') rather than corrupt data. Git already re-encodes commits that carry an encoding header to UTF-8 in `git log`, so lossy decoding only touches genuinely invalid bytes. A crafted message cannot do more than the repository author already can, since author and message are untrusted input anyway. parse_log is covered by the fuzz targets.
findings.refined_fix: Use NUL framing: `git log -z --topo-order --reverse --format=%H%x00%P%x00%an%x00%ae%x00%at%x00%B --encoding=UTF-8 <rev> --`, split the whole output on b'\0' and take chunks_exact(6), keeping empty fields. Decode with String::from_utf8 first; on failure use the lossy value and add `lossy_commits: usize` to ImportReport, then print it in cmds/gitbridge.rs. Update parse_log and the fuzz target fuzz/fuzz_targets/git_parse.rs (it is re-exported via ag_git::fuzzing) to match.
