.stdout(Stdio::piped())
            .stderr(Stdio::null())
findings.problem: git cat-file's stderr is discarded, so when it fails (missing/corrupt object, shallow or partial clone) the user only sees the secondary error "cat-file said '' for <sha>" with the real cause thrown away.
findings.proposed_fix: Capture stderr (pipe and read it on failure, or inherit it) and include it in GitError::Parse/Failed. Verify by importing a shallow/partial clone.
reasons: Verified. CatFile::start uses `.stderr(Stdio::null())`. When `git cat-file --batch` dies (corrupt or unreadable object, partial-clone fetch failure) it writes the reason only to stderr and nothing to stdout. blob() then reads an empty header and reports 'cat-file said '' for <sha>', so the real cause is lost. (A merely missing object is reported on stdout as '<sha> missing', which is fine.)

cat-file's stderr is discarded, but a missing object is reported on stdout as '<sha> missing' and is included in the error text. Failures are therefore loud, and only the underlying git message for exotic cases such as a failing promisor fetch in a partial clone is lost. That is a minor error-message nicety, not a misleading result.
findings.refined_fix: In crates/ag-git/src/import.rs use `.stderr(Stdio::piped())` in CatFile::start. In blob(), when the header is empty or malformed, call `self.child.kill()`, read `self.child.stderr.take()` to a string, and return `GitError::Failed { args: "cat-file --batch".into(), stderr }` (or add the text to the GitError::Parse message).

findings.excerpt:
if opts.branch.is_empty()
        || opts.branch.starts_with('-')
        || opts.branch.contains(['\n', ' ', '~', '^', ':', '?', '*', '[', '\\'])
        || opts.branch.contains("..")
findings.problem: Hand-rolled approximation of git's ref-name rules. It accepts names git rejects (`x.lock`, `a/`, `.hidden`, `a@{b}`, `@`, `a//b`, control characters other than newline), which then fail later inside fast-import with a less helpful message, after a repository may already have been created by `git init`. The real validator (git itself) is a required dependency of the bridge anyway.
findings.proposed_fix: Validate with `git check-ref-format --branch <name>` (or `refs/heads/<name>`) before touching the destination, and do the check before `git init`. Verify with a table test of invalid names.
reasons: Verified. In export() the `fresh` branch runs create_dir_all and `git init -q` before the hand-rolled branch-name check, so an invalid name leaves a freshly initialised empty repository behind. The check also accepts names git rejects (`x.lock`, trailing `/`, `a//b`, `@`, `a@{b}`, a leading `.` component, control characters), and those only fail later inside fast-import.

export.rs creates the destination and runs `git init` before it validates the branch name. A rejected name (including ones the pre-check does catch), or a name git later refuses such as x.lock, leaves an initialised empty repository behind. On the next run `fresh` is computed from the existing .git, so the `symbolic-ref HEAD` and `reset --hard` steps are skipped and the destination is left unchecked-out with HEAD on another branch.
findings.refined_fix: In crates/ag-git/src/export.rs, move the branch validation above the `if fresh { create_dir_all; git init }` block. Keep the `starts_with('-')` and empty checks, then validate with `git(Path::new("."), &["check-ref-format", &format!("refs/heads/{}", opts.branch)])`, mapping failure to GitError::Unsupported(format!("'{}' is not a usable branch name", opts.branch)). Add a table test of invalid names.

findings.excerpt:
//! Submodules (gitlinks), paths AgentGit refuses to record ..., tags, notes, signatures,
//! committer identity and timezone offsets. Skipped paths are reported.   (docs/guides/git-bridge.md:27: 'Not carried over, and reported when it happens: ... tags, notes, signatures, committer identity and timezone offsets')
findings.problem: The guide says everything in the 'not carried over' list is reported when it happens, but ImportReport only contains skipped paths and a submodule count. Signed commits, committer != author, non-UTC offsets, annotated tags and refs other than the single --rev are dropped silently, so a user migrating from Git gets no signal that provenance data was lost.
findings.proposed_fix: Either add counters/warnings to ImportReport and CLI output (signed commits dropped, committer differs, non-zero tz offset, other refs/tags not imported) or rewrite the sentence to say only paths and submodules are reported. Verify with a fixture containing a signed commit and a differing committer.
reasons: Verified. ImportReport has only skipped_paths and skipped_submodules, and cmds/gitbridge.rs prints only those. Signatures, committer differences, timezone offsets, tags, notes and other refs are dropped silently. lib.rs says only 'Skipped paths are reported', which is accurate. docs/guides/git-bridge.md:27 says all of 'tags, notes, signatures, committer identity and timezone offsets' are 'reported when it happens', which overclaims.

docs/guides/git-bridge.md:27 says the items not carried over are 'reported when it happens', including tags, notes, signatures, committer identity and timezone offsets, and that the command prints each skipped path. ImportReport and gitbridge.rs only report skipped paths and a submodule count; the rest is dropped silently. lib.rs:21 is worded accurately ('Skipped paths are reported'); the guide over-promises.
findings.refined_fix: In docs/guides/git-bridge.md replace the 'Not carried over, and reported when it happens: ...' paragraph with: '**Not carried over:** submodules (gitlinks), paths AgentGit refuses to record (...), tags, notes, signatures, committer identity and timezone offsets. Only skipped paths and submodule entries are reported (`ag git import` prints each skipped path and the submodule count); the rest is dropped without a message.' Optionally add counters (signed_commits, committer_differs, non_utc_offsets) to ImportReport and print them.

findings.problem: The whole OCI backend (the one the docs recommend for hostile/multi-tenant workloads, and which the README advertises as 'or a container') is verified only against a shell script that echoes canned replies ('inspect' prints a file, 'kill' touches a file, exit 125 is scripted). Nothing proves that docker/podman accept the generated flags (--memory-swap, --ulimit cpu, --pids-limit, --tmpfs, --mount type=bind, --entrypoint), that read-only/cap-drop/no-new-privileges/network none are actually enforced, that OOMKilled/exit-125 mapping works with real output, that cleanup removes real containers, or that bind-mounted /work is writable. The real components are feasible: GitHub ubuntu-latest runners ship Docker (and Podman), and .github/workflows/ci.yml:35-42 already runs the sandbox suites on Linux. src/oci.rs:8-10, docs/architecture/sandbox.md:251-256, ROADMAP.md:47 and CHANGELOG.md all admit it is untested against a real runtime.
findings.proposed_fix: Add tests/oci_real.rs that runs against a real runtime (docker, and a second matrix leg with podman) using a small digest-pinned image pulled in CI (e.g. busybox@sha256:...). Assert from inside the container what the kernel shows (NoNewPrivs=1, Seccomp=2, CapEff=0, read-only root EROFS, no network, pids/memory limits hit -> PidsLimit/MemoryLimit via real OOMKilled, timeout leaves no container in `docker ps -a --filter label=ag-sandbox=1`). Make the job fail (like AG_REQUIRE_SANDBOX) when the runtime is missing in CI (AG_REQUIRE_OCI=1). Keep a tiny argv-construction unit test only; delete the FAKE script and the 'untested' disclaimers once green.
reasons: crates/ag-sandbox/tests/oci.rs drives only a /bin/sh FAKE script; oci.rs:8-10 and docs/architecture/sandbox.md:251-256 admit the OCI backend (reachable via `ag-worker run --sandbox oci`, app.rs:260) was never run against docker/podman. ci.yml already uses docker on ubuntu-latest (the `images` job), so a real-runtime test is feasible.

The fake-runtime limitation is accurate and documented in oci.rs:8-10, tests/oci.rs:5-6, sandbox.md:251-256, ROADMAP.md:47, CHANGELOG.md:70 and README.md:401. OCI reports are marked verified:false with a 'requested, not observed' note, and a flag the runtime rejects surfaces as SandboxError::Runtime and a retry, not a wrong verdict. Nobody is misled, and real-runtime verification is already a tracked roadmap item.
findings.refined_fix: Add crates/ag-sandbox/tests/oci_real.rs, #![cfg(target_os="linux")]. It skips when no docker/podman is on PATH, and panics if AG_REQUIRE_OCI=1 and none is found. Because the sandbox hard-codes `--pull never`, add a CI step on the Linux leg that runs `docker pull busybox@sha256:<pinned>` first, then `AG_REQUIRE_OCI=1 cargo test -p ag-sandbox --test oci_real`. In the test, `chmod 0777` the workdir and use `--entrypoint sh`. Assert the kernel's view from inside via /proc/self/status (`NoNewPrivs: 1`, `Seccomp: 2`, `CapEff: 0000000000000000`). Assert that a write to / gives EROFS and that /proc/net/dev shows only lo. Assert that a fork bomb gives PidsLimit and that a memory hog gives MemoryLimit via the real OOMKilled. Assert that after a timeout `docker ps -a -q --filter label=ag-sandbox=1` is empty, and that a missing image gives SandboxError::Runtime. Keep the FAKE-script tests only for argv construction and supervision, and drop the 'untested' disclaimers once green.

findings.excerpt:
let isolation = IsolationReport {
    verified: false,
    user_ns: false,
    mount_ns: true,
    pid_ns: true, ... seccomp: true, rlimits: true,
    host_root: false,
    memory: Enforcement::Runtime,
    tasks: Enforcement::Runtime,
    cgroup: Some(CgroupReport { memory: true, pids: true }),
findings.problem: Every isolation flag of an OCI run is a constant, not an observation. They feed environment_digest (digest.rs:40-56) and therefore what a signed attestation states about the environment. They can be false claims: a Docker daemon started with seccomp unconfined or a permissive default profile still reports seccomp: true; rootless Podman or userns-remap reports user_ns: false; `--oci-user 0:0` (a legal worker flag) runs the check as kernel-uid 0 yet reports host_root: false; cgroup limits are reported as set although the runtime may have silently ignored --memory (no cgroup swap accounting, cgroup v1 without memory controller) or --pids-limit. The 'requested, not observed' note exists but the digest still hard-asserts the boolean values.
findings.proposed_fix: Before `rm -f`, run `<runtime> inspect --format '{{json .HostConfig}}' <name>` and `<runtime> info --format json`; derive each flag from what the runtime reports (ReadonlyRootfs, CapDrop, SecurityOpt contains no-new-privileges/seccomp profile, NetworkMode, PidsLimit, Memory/MemorySwap, Ulimits, User, rootless/userns info) and set host_root from the effective uid. If an observed value differs from the request, return SandboxError::Runtime instead of running with weaker isolation; set verified: true only for flags actually read back. Cover with the real-runtime tests from the previous finding.
reasons: oci.rs:294-311 builds the IsolationReport from constants (user_ns false, seccomp true, host_root false, cgroup Some(true,true)). environment_digest hashes these flags (digest.rs:40-60), so an attestation asserts them without observing them. `--oci-user 0:0` is a legal worker flag (app.rs:104) and still yields host_root:false. The `verified:false` field and the note only partly mitigate this.

outcome.rs:112-115 says that for OCI the flags describe what was requested and verified is false. oci.rs:315-318 adds a note saying the same, and verified is hashed into the digest (digest.rs:41), so a pinned digest cannot be mistaken for an observed one. Observing HostConfig via inspect/info would be a feature. The odd edge case (--oci-user 0:0 still reports host_root:false) is small and covered by the documented 'requested' semantics.
findings.refined_fix: 1) Set `host_root` from the configured user: parse the uid part of `cfg.user`, and treat non-numeric as unknown (fail closed or true). 2) Replace the OOM-only inspect at oci.rs:288 with one inspect call before `cleanup`, using a Go template so no JSON dependency is needed: `{{.State.OOMKilled}}|{{.HostConfig.ReadonlyRootfs}}|{{.HostConfig.NetworkMode}}|{{.HostConfig.PidsLimit}}|{{.HostConfig.Memory}}|{{.HostConfig.MemorySwap}}|{{json .HostConfig.CapDrop}}|{{json .HostConfig.SecurityOpt}}|{{.HostConfig.Privileged}}|{{.Config.User}}`. 3) Set each report flag only if the observed value matches the request, and set `verified:true` only when all of them were read back. 4) If a value differs, or the inspect cannot be read, return SandboxError::Runtime after cleanup so the job is retried instead of signed. Seccomp and user-namespace state need `<runtime> info`. Until that is done, leave those two flags false rather than true.

findings.excerpt: push(&["run", "--name", container_name, "--label", "ag-sandbox=1", "--pull", "never"]);
findings.problem: The sandbox always passes `--pull never`, and neither ag-sandbox nor ag-worker ever pulls or verifies the image. docs/guides/workers.md:108 and README advertise policies that name a digest-pinned `image` for container workers, but a job whose image is not already in the local store fails with 'Unable to find image' (mapped to SandboxError::Runtime -> Failure::retry in worker.rs:376-380) until the server's attempt limit is hit; the docs never tell the operator to pre-pull. `ag-worker run --sandbox oci --oci-image X` also does not validate X at start-up: a tag-only image is only rejected per job in Backend::sandbox_for (profile.rs:83-88), and the runtime/daemon reachability is never checked (see doctor finding). The label `ag-sandbox=1` is set so stale containers could be found, but nothing in the repository ever uses it (no reaper).
findings.proposed_fix: Add an explicit, digest-only ensure step in the OCI path: if `<runtime> image inspect <image@sha256:...>` fails, run `<runtime> pull <image@sha256:...>` (bounded by a configurable timeout, subject to a worker flag such as --oci-allow-pull and network policy), verify the resulting RepoDigests contains the pinned digest, and cache per image. Validate --oci-image (pinned, present or pullable) and the runtime/daemon (`info`) at worker start-up. Add a startup reaper that removes containers with label ag-sandbox=1 left by a crashed worker. Document the image-provisioning contract in docs/guides/workers.md and test it against a real registry-less local image.
reasons: oci.rs:148 always passes `--pull never`, and nothing pulls or checks the image. app.rs backend() (lines 260-264) does not validate --oci-image or the runtime at start-up, so a tag-only image is rejected per job in Backend::sandbox_for (profile.rs:83-88). workers.md and sandbox.md never tell the operator to pre-pull. The only `ag-sandbox=1` use in the repo is the label itself (oci.rs:148), so no reaper exists.

--pull never is deliberate (sandbox.md:244), but workers.md:58,108 never tells the operator that images must be pre-pulled. app.rs:260-264 builds Backend::Oci with no check of the runtime, the daemon or --oci-image. An unpinned or absent image is only refused per job (profile.rs:83-88, oci.rs:108) and then retried via Failure::retry, so a misconfigured worker starts fine and fails every job. The ag-sandbox=1 label is never used anywhere in the repo.
findings.refined_fix: Keep `--pull never`, because pulling is a deliberate security choice, and fix the contract instead. (a) In workers.md and sandbox.md state that the digest-pinned image must already be in the local store (`docker pull name@sha256:...`). (b) In app.rs `backend()` for Oci, build `OciSandbox::with_config` once when `--oci-image` is set so unpinned or malformed references fail at start-up. (c) Add a bounded start-up probe, `<runtime> image inspect <image>` with a 10 s timeout, that bails with the runtime's message. (d) Optionally add an opt-in `--oci-pull` that runs `<runtime> pull <image@sha256:...>` and then verifies it with `image inspect`. (e) Add a reaper that lists `ps -a --filter label=ag-sandbox=1 --format {{.Names}}` and removes only containers whose name `ag-sandbox-<pid>-…` has a dead pid.

    oci_user: String,
 ... crates/ag-worker/src/profile.rs:96-106  Backend::Oci { user, .. } => parse_numeric_user(user), ... checkout.rs:220 fs::set_permissions(&target, ... if entry.executable { 0o755 } else { 0o644 })
findings.problem: For container workers the check runs as container uid 65534 but the checked-out tree is only chown'ed to that uid when the worker is root (tree_owner returns None for any non-root worker, and for a non-numeric --oci-user, silently). A non-root worker (the recommended deployment, also every rootless Podman setup, where container uid 65534 maps to a subuid and not to the host uid) leaves /work owned by the worker's uid with mode 0755/0644, so the container user cannot write to /work and any check that writes (cargo target/, npm install, test artifacts) fails or - worse - fails as a signed `fail` verdict for a tree that is fine. Nothing detects the mismatch at start-up and parse_numeric_user failure is ignored. This is exactly the class of bug the missing real-runtime test (finding 1) would have caught.
findings.proposed_fix: Derive the container user from the runtime/worker: for non-root workers default --oci-user to the worker's own uid:gid (rootful docker) or `0:0` under rootless podman (maps to the host user), expose the choice explicitly, and refuse to start (Profile::check) when a root worker's --oci-user is non-numeric. Verify with a real-runtime e2e test that a check can create files in /work under rootful docker, rootless podman and non-root docker client.
reasons: The code is in crates/ag-worker/src/app.rs:104 (main.rs is a 20-line shim). `Backend::tree_owner()` (profile.rs:96-106) returns None for any non-root worker, so write_tree never chowns, and files and dirs are 0644/0755 owned by the worker uid (checkout.rs). The container runs as 65534 (or the rootless-podman subuid), so /work is not writable. `scratch_problem()` only runs when tree_owner is Some, and `parse_numeric_user` failure silently yields None.

profile.rs:96-106 returns tree_owner() == None for any non-root worker. checkout.rs:220,249 creates files 0644 and dirs 0755 owned by the worker. app.rs:104 defaults --oci-user to 65534:65534, and oci.rs:514 forbids --userns, so the container user is 'other' and cannot write /work. Writing checks (cargo target/, etc.) then exit non-zero and become a signed fail. workers.md only describes the chown for the root/namespace case, and a root worker with a non-numeric --oci-user silently skips the chown (profile.rs:109-112).
findings.refined_fix: In app.rs `backend()` or `profile()` for SandboxChoice::Oci, validate the user. 1) Bail if `--oci-user` is not numeric `uid[:gid]`. 2) If the worker is non-root and the uid differs from the effective uid, do one of two things. If `--oci-user` was left at its default (use `Option<String>` for the flag), substitute `format!("{euid}:{egid}")` for rootful Docker. If the user passed it explicitly, `bail!` with a message that rootless Podman needs `--oci-user 0:0` (container root is the host user) or the `keep-id` mapping. Expose `parse_numeric_user` as `Backend::user_problem()` so Profile can report it at start-up alongside `scratch_problem`. Add a worker e2e leg for Backend::Oci that creates a file under /work.

findings.problem: The cgroup v2 path (exact memory.max / pids.max / oom.group / memory.peak / cgroup.kill, the Enforcement::Cgroup claims in the IsolationReport and the digest) is only tested against a temp directory that merely stores written strings (cgroup.rs:126-172). Nothing shows the kernel accepts those writes, that cgroup.procs migration works from a user namespace, that OOM kills are classified as MemoryLimit, or that Drop's `cgroup.kill` + rmdir loop actually cleans up. A real delegated cgroup v2 is feasible in CI (ubuntu-latest runs systemd on cgroup v2: `systemd-run --user --scope -p Delegate=yes`, or a privileged container with a writable cgroup2 mount). docs/architecture/sandbox.md:214-217, ROADMAP.md:47 and CHANGELOG.md admit it is untested.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a Linux integration test (and a CI step that provides a delegated cgroup2 subtree with memory+pids controllers, failing when it cannot - AG_REQUIRE_CGROUP=1) that runs a memory hog and a fork bomb and asserts isolation.cgroup == Some({memory:true,pids:true}), Enforcement::Cgroup, ExitStatus::MemoryLimit from oom_kill, max_rss_bytes from memory.peak, and that no ag-sandbox-* cgroup directory remains. Keep the fake-directory unit tests only for parsing.
reasons: cgroup.rs is on the production path: namespace.rs:429 calls delegated_base()/Cgroup::create on every run. Its kernel-facing behaviour (memory.max, pids.max, cgroup.procs, memory.events oom_kill, cgroup.kill+rmdir) is covered only by the fake-directory unit tests, and the module header (cgroup.rs:9-11) says it was never exercised on a real cgroup v2.

cgroup.rs:1-12, sandbox.md:214-217, ROADMAP.md:47 and CHANGELOG.md:70-71 all state plainly that the kernel-facing part is untested. The code is best effort: Cgroup::configure only reports memory/pids as true if the write succeeded (cgroup.rs:73-79), and otherwise the sampled and rlimit limits stay in force with cgroup:None. The limitation is accurate, documented and fail-safe, and a delegated cgroup v2 test would be new CI infrastructure, not a defect fix.
findings.refined_fix: Add crates/ag-sandbox/tests/cgroup_real.rs that runs only when `/proc/self/cgroup` is v2 and the delegated subtree is writable with the memory and pids controllers, and panics if AG_REQUIRE_CGROUP=1 and it is not. In CI, run that one test binary under `sudo systemd-run --scope -p Delegate=yes --uid=$(id -u) ...`, or as root in a created subtree with `+memory +pids` written to `cgroup.subtree_control`. Assert `isolation.cgroup == Some({memory:true,pids:true})`, `Enforcement::Cgroup`, and `ExitStatus::MemoryLimit` from a memory hog (via `oom_kills()`). Assert `max_rss_bytes` comes from memory.peak, that a fork bomb stops at `pids.max`, and that no `ag-sandbox-*` directory remains afterwards.

findings.problem: `..Limits::default()` silently fixes `open_files = 1024` (RLIMIT_NOFILE) and `file_size_bytes = 1 GiB` (RLIMIT_FSIZE, spec.rs:96-108) for every check on every worker. Neither the policy RunSpec, the worker CLI nor Profile can change them, although they are part of the environment digest and real builds hit them (linkers/test runners with many fds; artefacts or debug info over 1 GiB end with SIGXFSZ and a signed `fail` for a healthy tree). They are also the only two limits with no ceiling check in sandbox_spec.
findings.proposed_fix: Add open_files and file_size_bytes to Ceilings/Defaults (flags --max-open-files, --default-open-files, --max-file-size-mb, --default-file-size-mb with ceiling validation like the other four) and, if the policy should control them, to RunSpec in proto/ag-protocol; reject (Refusal) when the request exceeds the ceiling; cover with a worker e2e test that a check writing a 2 GiB sparse file passes when allowed and is refused/failed when not.
reasons: plan.rs:96-103 uses `..Limits::default()`, which fixes open_files=1024 and file_size_bytes=1 GiB (spec.rs:96-108). Neither appears in Ceilings, Defaults, any app.rs flag or the RunSpec (grep finds no open_files or file_size in ag-worker or the proto), and both are hashed into the environment digest. They are the only two limits with no ceiling check in sandbox_spec.

The 1024 fds and 1 GiB RLIMIT_FSIZE are the conventional Linux defaults, documented in spec.rs Limits and in the sandbox.md limits table, and they are part of the environment digest. No evidence is given that realistic checks hit them. A signed fail from SIGXFSZ or EMFILE is the correct report for exceeding a stated limit. Adding worker flags or RunSpec fields is a feature request.
findings.refined_fix: Add `open_files: u32` and `file_size_mb: u32` to both `Defaults` and `Ceilings` in profile.rs. Add flags `--max-open-files`, `--default-open-files`, `--max-file-size-mb` and `--default-file-size-mb` in app.rs `profile()`. In plan.rs set `open_files` and `file_size_bytes` from the defaults and refuse above the ceiling, exactly as for the other four limits. Only if the policy should control them, add the fields to RunSpec in proto and ag-protocol and use `0` to mean the worker default. Add a plan.rs unit test and extend the limits table in workers.md.

findings.excerpt:
output_bytes: 8 << 20,
            tmp_mb: 512,
            tail_bytes: 8 * 1024,
            max_checkout_bytes: 4 << 30,
