findings.problem: Profile::new hard-codes the per-stream output cap (8 MiB), the sandbox /tmp size (512 MiB per check, held in RAM) and how much output is stored (8 KiB tail), and `main.rs::profile()` never exposes them: there is no --output-limit, --tmp-mb, --tail-bytes or --default-cpu-secs flag (Defaults.cpu_secs is copied from the default). An operator cannot size /tmp for a machine running N lanes or for builds that need a bigger /tmp (rust, node), nor keep more log tail for debugging, without recompiling. docs/guides/workers.md:79,169 present these as 'by default' as though they were adjustable.
findings.proposed_fix: Add --output-mb, --tmp-mb, --result-tail-kb and --default-cpu-secs flags (with env equivalents) wired into Profile/Defaults, validate sane ranges, and update docs/guides/workers.md. Consider letting the policy request /tmp size within a ceiling because it is already part of the environment digest.
reasons: Profile::new hard-codes output_bytes 8 MiB, tmp_mb 512 and tail_bytes 8 KiB (profile.rs:187-190). `profile()` in crates/ag-worker/src/app.rs, not main.rs, exposes none of them, and `cpu_secs: d.cpu_secs` (app.rs:300) is copied from the default, so there is no way to set it. workers.md:79,169 describe them as 'by default'. A build needing more than 512 MiB of RAM-backed /tmp ends as a signed `fail`.

Profile fields output_bytes, tmp_mb and tail_bytes are pub, and the defaults (8 MiB per stream, 8 KiB tail, 4 GiB checkout) are stated in workers.md:79,169-170. Embedders can override them, and the CLI exposes max_checkout_mb and the ceilings. Missing CLI flags for the rest are a convenience gap, not a defect that misleads or harms an operator.
findings.refined_fix: In app.rs `RunArgs` add `--output-mb` (default 8), `--tmp-mb` (default 512), `--result-tail-kb` (default 8) and `--default-cpu-secs` (default 0). In `profile()` assign them to `p.output_bytes`, `p.tmp_mb`, `p.tail_bytes` and `p.defaults.cpu_secs`. Reject 0, because SandboxSpec::validate requires non-zero limits. Update workers.md at lines 79 and 169 and add a flag-parsing test.

findings.excerpt: ro_mounts: ag_sandbox::standard_system_mounts(),  // spec.rs:326 "they carry no [`Mount::identity`]" ; digest.rs:96 None => put(b'h', m.host.to_string_lossy().as_bytes()),
findings.problem: By default every sandbox mounts the host's /usr, /bin, /lib*, /etc/ssl/certs with no identity, so environment_digest binds only the host path string. Two workers with entirely different /usr contents (different compiler, libc, Python) produce the same digest, and the same worker produces the same digest before and after `apt upgrade`. The product feature 'a policy can pin required_environment_digest so only workers in that exact configuration can satisfy the check' (docs/guides/workers.md:127-136, ADR 'environment' binding) is therefore not backed unless the operator manually replaces the default mounts via --no-system-mounts and --mount HOST=IDENTITY; the worker neither warns at start-up nor derives an identity.
findings.proposed_fix: Derive a real content identity for the default mounts (e.g. hash of /etc/os-release plus the package database digest - dpkg status / rpm db / apk installed - or a Merkle hash of the mounted tree, cached at start-up) and attach it via Mount::with_identity; at minimum log a warning and report `environment_identity: path-only` in result_json when any mount lacks an identity, and make `ag-worker doctor` print the identities that will enter the digest. Add an e2e test that changing a mounted tree's content changes the digest.
reasons: standard_system_mounts() (spec.rs:324-340) returns mounts with no identity, and Profile::new uses them by default. digest.rs:94-97 then hashes only the host path string. app.rs only warns about the process sandbox and never about mounts lacking an identity. workers.md:127-136 presents `required_environment_digest` pinning as binding the worker's exact configuration, with the identity caveat only in the Toolchains section.

This is exactly the documented behavior. spec.rs:321-323 says the standard mounts carry no Mount::identity. digest.rs:18-20 and sandbox.md call path-only a weaker statement. workers.md:121-125 tells the operator to give each mount an identity via --mount HOST=IDENTITY (with --no-system-mounts) because the digest otherwise says nothing about content. Overrides exist and are documented.
findings.refined_fix: 1) In app.rs `run()`, after building the profile, `tracing::warn!` listing each `ro_mount` whose `identity` is None, with text such as 'environment digest binds only the host path of these mounts'. 2) Print the same in `doctor()`. 3) Add a `--system-mounts-identity <ID>` flag that maps `standard_system_mounts()` through `Mount::with_identity(id)` (for example `debian-12.5` or an image digest). 4) Optionally, auto-derive the identity from a sha256 of /etc/os-release plus /var/lib/dpkg/status when present. Add a test that the digest changes when the identity changes.

findings.excerpt: let oci = ["docker", "podman"].iter().find_map(|rt| { std::env::split_paths(...).map(|d| d.join(rt)).find(|p| p.is_file()) }).map(|_| Availability::Available)
findings.problem: `detect()` and `ag-worker doctor` (main.rs:185-190) report the OCI sandbox as `available` merely because a file named docker/podman exists on PATH; the daemon, permissions on the socket, rootless setup, the configured `--oci-runtime` (any other name or path is never looked at) and the image are not probed. An operator is told 'oci available' on a host where every job will fail. `best_available()` (detect.rs:53-56) additionally returns the limits-only ProcessSandbox silently, and `doctor` prints `best_available()` which ignores OCI altogether.
findings.proposed_fix: Probe like the namespace sandbox does: run `<runtime> version --format '{{.Server.Version}}'`/`podman info` with a short timeout, and (when --oci-image is set) `image inspect`; honour the worker's configured runtime path; make doctor print the exact failure. Tests must run against a real runtime (see finding 1).
reasons: detect.rs:35-44 reports `oci: Available` when any file named docker or podman exists on PATH. `ag-worker doctor` (app.rs:184-195) prints that as plain 'available' and knows nothing of --oci-runtime. The rustdoc discloses the limitation, but the operator-facing CLI output does not.

detect.rs:35-44 reports oci Available if a docker/podman file exists on PATH. app.rs:190-195 prints a bare 'oci  available', yet workers.md:23 says `ag-worker doctor` 'tells you which work on this machine'. The library docs disclose the caveat, but the doctor output drops it, and doctor has no way to name the configured --oci-runtime. The 'not probed because it can hang' reason does not hold, since oci.rs already has a timeout-bounded capture().
findings.refined_fix: In `doctor()`, print the oci line as 'runtime executable found (daemon and image not probed)'. Add `OciSandbox::probe(&self, timeout: Duration) -> Availability` that runs `<runtime> version --format '{{.Server.Version}}'` through the existing `capture()` helper with a 5 s limit, and call it from `doctor` and from `backend()` for SandboxChoice::Oci using `--oci-runtime`, including the error text. Leave detect() cheap.

findings.problem: The comment above says 'Decide whether this worker can and will run it before spending bandwidth', but the pinned-environment check runs only after the complete check has executed (up to the full timeout). A worker that can never match the pinned digest claims the job, runs it for up to an hour, throws the result away and returns it to the queue, again and again until the server's attempt limit; it can also starve workers that could match.
findings.proposed_fix: Compute the digest before executing: add `Sandbox::environment_digest(&self, spec) -> Result<String>` that builds the IsolationReport the same way as run() (namespace: probe cgroup/sampler availability; oci: the observed HostConfig) and compare with required_environment_digest before checkout; keep the post-run comparison as a safety net.
reasons: worker.rs:383-390 compares `outcome.environment_digest` with `task.required_environment_digest` only after `sandbox.run`. A worker that can never match runs the whole check, drops the result and fails with retry. ClaimJobRequest carries no digest, so the server cannot route around it. The server also re-checks at completion (jobs.rs:385), so this is wasted work and not a correctness hole.

The digest is a property of the run, built from the IsolationReport (cgroup, enforcement, host_root) that the sandbox produces while running (namespace.rs run_plan, oci.rs:294). Checking it after the run is by design, and workers.md:91 documents the outcome (job fails, returned to the queue, message shows both digests). The attempt limit bounds the waste to a few runs. A pre-run predictor would have to duplicate the sandbox's runtime decisions, and a mismatch would wrongly refuse runnable jobs. The comment at worker.rs:338 refers to the sandbox_for/isolation checks that follow it, not to the digest.
findings.refined_fix: Add a defaulted `fn predicted_environment_digest(&self, _spec: &SandboxSpec) -> Option<String> { None }` to the Sandbox trait. Implement it for OciSandbox, whose IsolationReport is a pure function of the config and spec, by factoring the report construction out of `run`. Call it in worker.rs `run_job` right after `sandbox_spec(..)`, before `fetch_manifest`, and return `Failure::retry` on a mismatch. Keep the post-run comparison for namespace and process sandboxes.

findings.excerpt:
if lost.load(Ordering::SeqCst) {
            return Disposition::Abandoned("the claim was lost while the check ran ...")  // docs/guides/workers.md:172  "the check is not interrupted: it runs to its own time limit and its result is discarded" ; main.rs:354 std::process::exit(130);
findings.problem: There is no cancellation path: Sandbox::run (lib.rs:100-109) takes no cancel token, so when the lease is lost (another worker already runs the job) or the operator sends the second signal, the check keeps burning CPU for up to its timeout and, on the second signal, `std::process::exit(130)` leaves OCI containers running (the docker client is in its own process group and is not killed; nothing runs `<runtime> kill/rm`). The `ag-sandbox=1` label that would let a reaper find them is never used.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a cancellation handle to the Sandbox trait (e.g. `run_cancellable(&spec, &AtomicBool)` checked in supervise()'s poll loop and wired to the lease-lost flag and to shutdown), have OciSandbox's on_kill hook run on cancel, and add a start-up/shutdown reaper for label ag-sandbox=1 containers. Test with a real runtime.
reasons: There is no cancellation path: `Sandbox::run(&self, &SandboxSpec)` (lib.rs:100-109) takes no cancel token, and `lost` is checked only after the job (worker.rs:271). The second signal calls `std::process::exit(130)` (crates/ag-worker/src/app.rs:359, not main.rs), leaving OCI containers running. workers.md:172 documents the lost-claim part. The `ag-sandbox=1` label is never used for cleanup.

The lost-lease part is documented (workers.md:172) and acceptable. The OCI part is not: the container is only killed by the supervisor's on_kill hook (oci.rs:262-267), the docker client runs in its own process group, and the namespace sandbox's PR_SET_PDEATHSIG protection (spawn.rs:439) has no OCI counterpart. The second-signal path `std::process::exit(130)` (app.rs:359), which workers.md:156 advertises, or a worker crash or kill -9, therefore leaves the container running with no wall-clock bound, and nothing ever uses the ag-sandbox=1 label.
findings.refined_fix: Add `fn run_cancellable(&self, spec: &SandboxSpec, cancel: &AtomicBool) -> Result<Outcome, SandboxError>` to the Sandbox trait, defaulting to `run`. Poll `cancel` in the supervise() loop and add a `Verdict::Cancelled` that triggers the existing kill path (including OCI's `on_kill`). Pass `lost.clone()` into the spawn_blocking closure in run_job. On the second signal, set a shared cancel flag and wait briefly instead of an immediate exit(130). Add the reaper from finding 2, restricted to containers named `ag-sandbox-<pid>-*` whose pid is dead.

findings.excerpt: const RETRY_AFTER_MS: i64 = 10_000;  ...  let mut backoff = Duration::from_secs(1);  ...  backoff = (backoff * 2).min(Duration::from_secs(30));   // main.rs:316 timeout: Some(Duration::from_secs(120)),   // main.rs:342-343 lease: Duration::from_secs(args.lease_secs.max(5)), wait: Duration::from_secs(args.wait_secs.min(30)),
findings.problem: Operational timings an operator would tune are fixed: the retry delay for jobs a worker cannot run (10 s, documented as a fact in workers.md:89), the claim-error backoff (1 s..30 s), and the gRPC client request timeout (120 s, also applies to large blob downloads). `--lease-secs 1` and `--wait-secs 100` are silently rewritten to 5 and 30 with no message.
findings.proposed_fix: Expose --retry-after-secs, --client-timeout-secs and --backoff-max-secs; reject (or log a warning for) out-of-range --lease-secs/--wait-secs instead of silently clamping; document the defaults.
reasons: The constants exist as quoted: RETRY_AFTER_MS=10_000 (worker.rs:24), backoff 1 s to 30 s (worker.rs:179,204), and the client timeout of 120 s at crates/ag-worker/src/app.rs:321 (not main.rs). `--lease-secs` is silently raised to a minimum of 5 (app.rs:347) with no mention in its help text. `--wait-secs` is clamped to 30, but its help text does say 'at most 30'.

RETRY_AFTER_MS is a documented fact (workers.md:89). The backoff and the 120 s client timeout are ordinary internal tuning constants. The --wait-secs clamp is stated in its help text ('at most 30', app.rs:86), and the server caps it at 30 s anyway (worker.rs:36). The silent 5 s lease minimum is trivial and not harmful.
findings.refined_fix: In app.rs `run()`, `bail!` on `--lease-secs < 5` instead of using `.max(5)` (or emit `tracing::warn!` when clamping `--wait-secs`). Add `--retry-after-secs` (default 10, passed through `Options`), `--client-timeout-secs` (default 120) and `--backoff-max-secs` (default 30). Replace RETRY_AFTER_MS with `opts.retry_after`. Document the defaults in workers.md:89.

findings.problem: Resource-limit statuses are guessed: any non-zero exit (including an ordinary test failure) whose sampled peak happened to reach 90% of the memory limit is reported as MemoryLimit, and a SIGKILL near the CPU budget as CpuLimit (the +50 ms slack and the 90% threshold are magic numbers). The status goes into result_json/summary that humans use to debug and docs call 'best effort'. The signed verdict is fail in both cases, so correctness of the attestation is unaffected, but the reported cause can be wrong.
findings.proposed_fix: Report the cause only when observed: with cgroup v2 use memory.events oom_kill / pids.events; for the sampled path return MemoryLimit only when the supervisor itself killed it (verdict) and otherwise return the natural exit status with a separate `near_memory_limit: true` note; name the thresholds as documented constants.
reasons: supervise.rs:380-383 sets `abnormal = !natural.success()`, and ExitStatus::success() is true only for Exited(0) (outcome.rs:33). So an ordinary Exited(1) whose sampled peak reached 90% of the limit becomes MemoryLimit. docs/architecture/sandbox.md:212 states that a merely non-zero exit is never reclassified, so the code contradicts its documentation. Both namespace.rs:484 and process.rs:119 call classify(). The signed verdict is unaffected, only the reported cause.

sandbox.md:208-212 documents that classification is best effort, and the finding itself concedes that the signed verdict is fail in every case. The heuristic is deterministic and bounded (reclassify only when abnormal and the sampled peak is at least 90% of the limit, or SIGKILL near the CPU budget). It only affects the unsigned status label, and a program that dies of an allocation failure (Python MemoryError, exit 1) is exactly what it targets.
findings.refined_fix: In supervise.rs `classify`, restrict the sampled heuristic to signal deaths: replace `let abnormal = !natural.success();` with `let abnormal = matches!(natural, ExitStatus::Signaled(_));`. Name the thresholds as `const NEAR_MEMORY_NUM/DEN` (9/10) and `const CPU_KILL_SLACK_MS: u64 = 50`. Add a unit test: Exited(1) with peak_sampled at 95% stays Exited(1), and Signaled(SIGKILL) at 95% becomes MemoryLimit.

findings.excerpt:
report.seccomp,
        report.rlimits,
        report.host_root,   // DOMAIN = b"agentgit.sandbox.environment.v1\0"
findings.problem: The environment digest says 'attestations bound to this digest state which protections their check ran under', but protections are booleans: `seccomp: true` is identical whether the deny-list has 60 or 10 syscalls, across ag-sandbox releases, and the digest contains no kernel release, no sandbox/crate version, no hostname/INNER_ID/SHM_MAX/root-tmpfs constants. A release that weakens the filter or /proc masking yields the same digest, so a policy pin cannot detect it.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a versioned `profile` identifier (e.g. sha256 of the built seccomp program and the PROC_MASKED/PROC_READONLY/DEVICES lists, plus a SANDBOX_PROFILE_VERSION constant) and the kernel release to the digest (domain v2, documented), and cover it with the existing 'every ingredient changes the digest' test.
reasons: digest.rs:36-98 hashes only OS, arch, sandbox name, boolean flags, cgroup bits, network, image, runtime, limits, env and mounts. There is no seccomp-program or profile version, so weakening the filter or the /proc masks keeps the digest unchanged. In addition, the digest.rs:14-15 doc says it covers every IsolationReport field except notes, but `memory` and `tasks` (Enforcement) are not hashed.

digest.rs:6-26 defines the digest as covering the sandbox name, OS/arch, every report flag, the limits, the env and the mounts. It never claims to cover filter contents, sandbox version or kernel release, and the domain string is versioned for format changes. Booleans stating which protections were in force match the documented 'protections' claim. Adding profile hashes or kernel release would be a design extension, and it would make pinned digests churn on every kernel update.
findings.refined_fix: Add `pub const SANDBOX_PROFILE_VERSION: u32` in ag-sandbox, bumped whenever the seccomp deny-list, PROC_MASKED, PROC_READONLY or DEVICES change. Hash it with a new tag (`put(b'V', ..)`) together with a sha256 of the built seccomp program for the current arch. Also hash `report.memory` and `report.tasks` as small integers. Bump DOMAIN to `agentgit.sandbox.environment.v2\0`, document it, and extend `every_ingredient_changes_the_digest`. Do not add the kernel release: it would make digests churn on every host kernel update and defeat pinning across nodes.

findings.excerpt:
const RUNTIME_ERRORS: [&str; 8] = ["Error response from daemon", "Cannot connect to the Docker daemon", "Unable to find image", "pull access denied", "invalid reference format", "unknown flag", "unknown shorthand flag", "Error: "];
        let from_runtime = stderr.starts_with(&format!("{runtime}:")) || RUNTIME_ERRORS.iter().any(|m| stderr.contains(m));
findings.problem: Whether exit code 125 is a runtime failure or the check's own exit status is decided by substring-matching the (untrusted, check-controlled) stderr; a check that exits 125 after printing 'Error: ' is reclassified as an infrastructure failure (job retried instead of a signed fail), and runtimes with other message texts/locales are mismatched. Only verified against the fake script.
findings.proposed_fix: Distinguish by observation instead of text: after the run, `inspect` the container: if it never existed or `.State.ExitCode`/`.State.Status` shows it never started, it is a runtime failure; otherwise the exit code is the command's. Verify against real docker and podman.
reasons: oci.rs:392-409 treats exit 125 as a runtime failure if stderr starts with `<runtime>:` or contains any of RUNTIME_ERRORS, including the generic 'Error: '. That stderr is the client's merged stream and so includes the check's own stderr. A check that exits 125 after printing 'Error: ' becomes SandboxError::Runtime, which the worker turns into Failure::retry (worker.rs:380) instead of a signed fail. Only the fake script covers this.

oci.rs:380-382 documents the trade-off: a command that really exits 125 cannot be told apart by code alone, so the runtime's stderr decides. The worst case (a check that exits 125 with a matching string such as 'Error: ' in stderr) is retried and then ends in a failed job, which is fail-safe. It can never produce a false pass, and exit 125 is rare. It is also exactly the kind of runtime behavior that needs real-runtime verification, which is already tracked.
findings.refined_fix: Reuse the container inspect that already runs at oci.rs:288. Change its format to `{{.State.Status}}|{{.State.ExitCode}}|{{.State.OOMKilled}}`, return the parsed tuple, and pass it into `map_status`. Treat exit 125 as a runtime failure only if the inspect failed (no such container) or `State.Status` is `created`, meaning the command never started. If the container ran, `Exited(125)` is the command's own status. Keep the substring list only as a fallback when inspect is unreachable. Container removal is explicit (`cleanup`, no `--rm`), so inspect is reliable at that point. Add a test using the fake script's `inspect` branch.

findings.problem: The results of `kill` and `rm -f` are discarded and the 10 s/20 s timeouts are fixed. If the daemon hiccups the container (and its tmpfs/memory) leaks silently with a still-running check, and the worker reports success; ag-sandbox has no logging so nobody learns about it. `inspect` for OOMKilled likewise degrades to `false` on any failure (line 288-289), turning an OOM kill into a plain exit status.
findings.proposed_fix: Return/propagate cleanup failures (SandboxError::Runtime or a note in IsolationReport.notes and a tracing event), retry with backoff, make the timeouts part of OciConfig, and fail the run when `inspect` cannot be read instead of assuming OOMKilled=false.
reasons: oci.rs:266 discards the result of `kill`, oci.rs:376-378 discards the result of `rm -f -v`, and oci.rs:288-289 degrades any inspect failure to OOMKilled=false. The 10 s and 20 s timeouts are fixed, and ag-sandbox has no logging dependency. The impact is bounded, since `rm -f` also force-kills, so a leak needs the daemon to be failing at the time.

Best-effort cleanup is standard. oci.rs:262-267 and 375-378 retry nothing, but a failing `docker kill` or `rm -f` needs a daemon fault, and then the job's own run would also be failing. The 10 s and 20 s bounds are sensible. The OOM read defaults to false only when `inspect` fails, and the natural exit status is still reported. The orphan-container exposure that matters is covered by finding 11.
findings.refined_fix: Make `cleanup` return `bool`, and make `capture` return `Option<(bool,String)>` as it does now. In `run`, if the `rm -f` result is false, push a note onto `IsolationReport.notes` (the digest ignores notes), for example 'container <name> could not be removed; label ag-sandbox=1'. If `inspect` returns None and the natural status is Exited(137) or a signal, return `SandboxError::Runtime("cannot read the container state")` so the job is retried instead of signed with a guessed cause. Move the 10 s and 20 s values into OciConfig fields with those defaults.

findings.excerpt: let nonce = ag_crypto::random_id("d").unwrap_or_else(|_| format!("d_{}", std::process::id()));  ... fn prepare_dir(dir: &Path) -> std::io::Result<()> { if dir.exists() { return Ok(()); } ... from_mode(0o755)
findings.problem: If the system RNG fails the job directory name silently becomes a predictable `d_<pid>`, and prepare_dir() accepts an already-existing directory without checking owner/mode, so a local attacker who pre-creates `<scratch>/<job>-<attempt>-d_<pid>` (or any pre-existing dir) gets the worker to write the checkout into attacker-controlled storage; new job dirs are always 0755/0644 even when the worker is not root, so other local users can read every checked-out tree.
findings.proposed_fix: Propagate the RNG error (fail the job) instead of falling back; create the job dir with `create_dir` (EEXIST is an error) and mode 0700 unless a root worker needs to map to another uid, in which case 0711/0755 only on the path components required; verify ownership of the scratch root at start-up.
reasons: worker.rs:457 falls back to `d_<pid>` if random_id fails, and `prepare_dir` (worker.rs:469-476) returns Ok for any pre-existing directory without checking owner or mode. New dirs are always 0755 and files 0644 (checkout.rs), and the default scratch dir is under the shared temp dir, so other local users can read checked-out trees and a pre-created scratch root is trusted. The RNG-failure path is a minor trigger. The main exposure is the unvalidated scratch root and the world-readable trees.

The predictable-name fallback only happens if the OS RNG fails, which would break key generation and signing too. In normal operation job_dir() uses a random_id nonce. prepare_dir() deliberately leaves existing directories alone (documented at worker.rs:466-468, since the scratch parent can be /tmp). The 0755/0644 modes are needed so the sandbox user can reach the tree. workers.md:142-146 says to run the worker as a dedicated user on a host that does not run unsandboxed untrusted code.
findings.refined_fix: 1) In `job_dir` return a `Result` and fail the job on a random_id error (a `Failure::retry`). 2) Create `job_dir` and `workdir` with `std::fs::create_dir` so that EEXIST is an error. 3) Add a check at start-up, in `Profile::scratch_problem` or a new Profile method, that an existing `scratch_dir` is owned by the effective uid and has `mode & 0o022 == 0`, and bail otherwise. 4) For the Namespace and Process backends when the worker is non-root, create the job dirs with mode 0700. Keep 0755 for a root worker, and for OCI with a different container uid, where the container user must be able to traverse.

findings.problem: The test `what_the_command_leaves_in_the_namespace_dies_with_its_init` computes the list of host processes that match the sandbox's leftover `sleep` commands and then throws it away; the remaining assertion inspects only direct children of the test process, which the sandbox's processes never are, so it passes even if the sandbox leaked daemons (the real coverage lives in limits.rs). A similar weak assertion is at isolation.rs:253 (`assert!(!o.stdout_lossy().is_empty())` for the mount/remount attempt).
findings.proposed_fix: Use unique_marker()/sleep_marker() like limits.rs and assert host_processes_matching(marker).is_empty() after the run, or delete the test; assert the exact error text of the remount attempt.
reasons: The vacuity is real (isolation.rs:647 `let _ = sleepers;`, and `children_of_this_process` cannot see namespace members), but the code is test-only and the same property is genuinely asserted in limits.rs (lines 52-67 and 466-490 check `host_processes_matching(...).is_empty()`). The weak assertion at isolation.rs:253 sits in a test that otherwise has exact EPERM/EROFS checks. It is a redundant-test nit, not a coverage gap.

isolation.rs:643-649 computes `sleepers` and discards it with `let _ = sleepers;`. The only assertion checks children_of_this_process(), and the sandbox's processes are never children of the test process, so the test cannot fail if the sandbox leaked daemons, despite its name. The assertion at isolation.rs:253 (`!o.stdout_lossy().is_empty()`) is similarly vacuous. limits.rs:52,67 already shows the unique-marker pattern.
findings.refined_fix: In what_the_command_leaves_in_the_namespace_dies_with_its_init, start the background sleepers with a per-run unique duration or marker, as limits.rs:52 and :67 do (`sleep {id}`). After sh() returns, poll briefly (up to about 2 s) and assert `host_processes_matching(&format!("sleep {id}")).is_empty()`. Delete the `let _ = sleepers` and children_of_this_process lines. At isolation.rs:253 replace the non-empty check with an assertion that the combined output contains the kernel's refusal text (for example 'Operation not permitted' or 'Read-only file system' for the remount and write attempts).

findings.problem: Every checkout error is classified retryable, including deterministic ones for the tree itself (CheckoutError::Bad: a symlink with an absolute or `..`-escaping target, invalid path, wrong object kind). Such a candidate can never be validated by any worker: the job bounces through the queue until the attempt limit and the proposal stays 'blocked' with no signed verdict; legitimate repositories containing e.g. an absolute symlink are permanently unvalidatable.
findings.proposed_fix: Classify CheckoutError::Bad for tree-content violations as Failure::permanent with a clear reason surfaced to the author (or materialise such symlinks safely - dangling links are harmless inside the sandbox, which cannot see host paths - and reserve the rejection for real traversal risks); keep size-over-limit as retry.
reasons: worker.rs:362 and :368 map every CheckoutError to Failure::retry, including `CheckoutError::Bad` from check_link_target (checkout.rs:261-282) for absolute or escaping symlinks. That outcome is deterministic for the tree, so every worker fails it until the server's attempt limit and no signed verdict is produced. A repository with e.g. `link -> /usr/bin/x` is permanently unvalidatable.

worker.rs:364-368 retries all checkout errors, but checkout.rs:261-282 rejects absolute or escaping symlinks on purpose, and workers.md:69-71 states the rule. Not attesting a tree that cannot be materialized safely is correct, and the failure reason is visible via GET jobs. The CheckoutError::Bad variant is mixed (server inconsistency, size limits another worker may allow), so blanket-permanent would be wrong. The extra retries are bounded by the attempt limit.
findings.refined_fix: In checkout.rs add `CheckoutError::Unsafe(String)` and use it for tree-content violations: check_link_target failures, non-UTF-8 symlink target, 'exists and is not a directory', and unknown file type. Keep `Bad` for server inconsistencies (hash mismatch, wrong object kind) and the size limit, and keep both as retry. In worker.rs, at lines 362 and 366-368, map `Unsafe` to `Failure::permanent(format!("the candidate cannot be checked: {e}"))` and everything else to `Failure::retry`. Add a unit test for the mapping.

findings.excerpt: const form = ref({ name: '', description: '', stream: 'main' })  // :111 same literal in openCreate(); :123 default_stream: form.value.stream.trim() || undefined
findings.problem: The create-repository form prefills the default stream with the literal 'main' and then sends it explicitly, so the server's configurable default (cfg.repos.default_stream, used in create_repo when default_stream is empty) can never apply. An operator who configures a different default (e.g. trunk) gets 'main' from every repository created via the UI.
findings.proposed_fix: Leave the field empty with a placeholder, and send default_stream only when the user typed one so the server default wins. Better: have the server expose its default stream in /v1/capabilities (or a repos-defaults field) and show that as the placeholder. Verify with a real ag-server started with repos.default_stream='trunk': create a repo from the UI with the field empty and assert Repo.default_stream === 'trunk' (Playwright e2e against the real server).
findings.severity_note: configurable server value overridden by the client
reasons: ReposView.vue:105/111 prefill form.stream='main' and :123 sends it as default_stream. ag-server create_repo (api/repository.rs:54) only falls back to cfg.repos.default_stream (config.rs:285, configurable) when the field is empty, so the UI always overrides it.

ReposView.vue seeds form.stream with 'main' (in the ref and in openCreate) and create() sends it explicitly. The server only falls back to cfg.repos.default_stream when default_stream is empty (api/repository.rs:54-57; config.rs:284 'Default stream for new repositories'). A configured default such as trunk therefore never applies to repositories created from the UI.
findings.refined_fix: Initialise and reset form.stream to '' (lines 105 and 111), keep line 123 as `default_stream: form.value.stream.trim() || undefined`, and give the TextField a neutral placeholder/hint such as "Leave empty to use the server default". Optionally show the real default after creation from the returned Repo.default_stream.

findings.excerpt: const rev = computed(() => qRev.value || board.repo?.default_stream || 'main')  // HistoryView.vue:47 effectiveRev uses the same || 'main'; stores/board.ts:205 stream.value = value.default_stream || 'main'
findings.problem: While the repository record has not loaded (board.repo is null) or when default_stream is empty, Files, History and the board request the stream literally named 'main'. On a repository whose default stream is anything else this issues a wrong request (404 or the empty-state 'no changesets yet') and can flash or keep wrong data. The fallback hides the missing real state.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove the 'main' fallbacks. Gate the first list/log/resolve request on board.repo being loaded (useResource already supports enabled(); the History/Files watchers need the same guard) and show the skeleton until default_stream is known. Verify in e2e with a repo whose default stream is not 'main' and assert the first network request carries that stream.
reasons: RepoLayout renders RouterView immediately while board.start() loads the repo asynchronously, and board.stop() nulls board.repo. FilesView.vue:34 and HistoryView.vue:47 therefore request rev='main' first; on a repo whose default is not main this gives a transient 404/error or, if a non-default 'main' stream exists, briefly shows the wrong tree. The server already resolves an empty rev to the default stream (api/mod.rs:123, tree.rs:55, history.rs:69), so the literal is unnecessary.

RepoLayout.vue renders <RouterView> immediately while board.start() is still loading, so board.repo is null on a deep link. FilesView.vue:34 and HistoryView.vue:47 then request the literal stream 'main'. On a repo whose default stream is not 'main' that is a wrong request, and a wrong listing or a 404 flashes until default_stream arrives. The server resolves an empty rev to the default stream (api/tree.rs:55, history.rs:69), so the fallback is unnecessary. The 'value.default_stream || 'main'' in board.ts:205 is also dead, since the server always returns default_stream.
findings.refined_fix: Drop the 'main' literals: `const rev = computed(() => qRev.value || board.repo?.default_stream || '')` in FilesView and `effectiveRev` in HistoryView, letting the server resolve an empty rev (or gate the first list/resolve/log call on board.repo being loaded). Also remove the dead `|| 'main'` in stores/board.ts:205, since the server never returns an empty default_stream.

findings.excerpt: description="Queued proposals are integrated one at a time, in order, stopping at the first one that is blocked."  // :50-53 toasts.warn(`Queue stopped at ${shortId(res.stopped_at, 6)}`, `${n} processed before a proposal was blocked or conflicted.`)  // :32-40 TONE has queued/done/integrated/blocked/conflict/failed/skipped
findings.problem: The UI text contradicts the engine: ag-integrate Queue::run_queue documents 'A blocked or conflicting entry does not hold up the ones behind it' and loops over every queued entry. 'processed' therefore contains all entries, and stopped_at is merely the first blocked/rejected one, so 'Queue stopped at ... n processed before' is false. In addition the real queue state set is queued/done/blocked/rejected/failed (OpenAPI QueueEntry.state): 'rejected' (conflict or policy denial) is missing from TONE so it renders neutral, while 'integrated', 'conflict' and 'skipped' are states the server never emits.
findings.proposed_fix: Rewrite the empty-state and toast text to match the engine (entries are processed in order; blocked or rejected ones are marked and skipped, the rest continue) and report counts per outcome from res.processed[].state. Replace TONE with exactly the OpenAPI states (queued, done, blocked, rejected, failed) and derive the type from the generated schema. Fix the OpenAPI description of RunQueueResponse.stopped_at at the same time. Verify with a real queue holding one blocked proposal in front of an integrable one and assert the second is integrated and the first shows state 'blocked'/'rejected' with the correct tone.
reasons: Queue::run_queue (ag-integrate/src/queue.rs:45-83) documents and implements that a blocked or conflicting entry does not hold up later ones, so it loops over all queued entries. In api/integration.rs:200 stopped_at is merely the first blocked/rejected/failed id, and processed holds every entry. QueuePanel.vue:111 and the :50-53 toast are therefore false. The real states are queued/done/blocked/rejected/failed (queue_finish plus the OpenAPI QueueEntry description), so TONE lacks 'rejected' and holds 'integrated'/'conflict'/'skipped', which are never emitted.

Queue::run_queue (ag-integrate/src/queue.rs:45-48) states that a blocked or conflicting entry does not hold up the ones behind it, and it loops over every queued entry. QueuePanel.vue still says 'stopping at the first one that is blocked' and toasts 'n processed before a proposal was blocked'. In fact n is all processed entries and stopped_at is only the first non-integrated one. queue_finish writes done/blocked/rejected/failed (OpenAPI QueueEntry.state). TONE has no 'rejected' (conflict and policy denial), so those render neutral, and it lists states the server never emits (integrated, conflict, skipped).
findings.refined_fix: In QueuePanel.vue set TONE to {queued:'info', done:'ok', blocked:'warn', rejected:'bad', failed:'bad'}. Change the empty-state text to "Queued proposals are integrated in order. A blocked or rejected one is marked and skipped; the rest continue." Build the toast from res.processed[].state counts (e.g. "2 integrated, 1 blocked"), using warn when any non-done entry exists, and drop the "stopped at / processed before" wording. Correct the RunQueueResponse.stopped_at description in the protocol source and regenerate openapi.json and schema.gen.ts.

findings.excerpt: const pass = s(result.outcome) !== 'fail'
findings.problem: A job.complete event is rendered as 'finished validation job (passed)' whenever result.outcome is anything other than the string 'fail'. The server only sets result.outcome when an attestation was submitted; a stale completion stores result {"stale": true} with no outcome, and a non-validate job has none either. Those are shown as green 'passed' in the live feed and proposal timeline, which asserts a verdict the server never gave.
findings.proposed_fix: Tri-state the display: outcome 'pass' -> passed, 'fail' -> failed, result.stale === true -> 'candidate was stale, no attestation', otherwise neutral 'completed' with no tone. Verify with a real worker run against a stale candidate (ag-worker tests already produce {"stale": true}) and with pass and fail runs, asserting the three sentences in the feed.
reasons: events.ts:192 computes pass = outcome !== 'fail'. complete_job (ag-server api/jobs.rs:365-398) sets result.outcome only when an attestation was submitted; a stale completion stores only {"stale":true} and non-validate jobs have no outcome, so both render as green 'passed'.

api/jobs.rs complete_job sets result.outcome only when an attestation was submitted. A stale completion stores {"stale":true} (jobs.rs:365, worker.rs:282), and non-validate jobs have no outcome. events.ts:192 computes `pass = outcome !== 'fail'`, so a stale or outcome-less completion is shown as a green 'finished validation job (passed)'. The server never gave that verdict.
findings.refined_fix: In the job.complete case branch on result: outcome==='pass' -> shield/ok 'finished validation job (passed)'; outcome==='fail' -> x/bad '(failed)'; result.stale===true -> neutral/info 'validation job skipped: candidate was stale (no attestation)'; otherwise neutral 'completed job' with no pass/fail tone.

findings.excerpt: 'The approvals the policy requires are in for the current head.'  // :269-270 'not required', 'The policy requires no approval for this change.'  // :247 const required = typeof d.required === 'number' ? d.required : have + 1
findings.problem: The Approved verdict is inferred from the absence of a blocker even when the prepare result is missing or failed. With prep unavailable (still loading, or prepare errored) and zero reviews, the final else branch states 'not required: The policy requires no approval for this change', a claim with no evidence (ProposalView always passes a non-null reviews array, so this shows during every load). With prep unavailable but one approval it claims the policy's requirement is satisfied. When a blocker has no numeric 'required', the UI invents required = have + 1.
findings.proposed_fix: Only emit 'ok' or 'na' for Approved when prep is present and has no insufficient_approvals/changes_requested blocker; with prep absent or errored return tone 'unknown' ('checking' or 'could not be computed'). Drop the have + 1 invention and show only what the server detail provides. Better: have prepare return a structured approvals verdict (required, have, scope) so no inference is needed. Verify against a real server by forcing a prepare error and asserting the state is 'unknown', and with a policy of min 0 asserting 'not required'.
reasons: fourstate.ts only returns 'unknown' when both prep and summary are missing. ProposalView/useProposalData always passes reviews (`?? []`), so summary is non-null while prepare is loading or failed, and the final else (:266-271) emits tone 'na' 'not required: The policy requires no approval for this change' with no evidence. With one approval and no prep it claims the requirement is met (:258-264). The server's blocker detail does carry have/required/scope, so `have + 1` at :247 is only a defensive invention.

deriveFourStates only emits 'unknown' for Approved when both prep and summary are missing. useProposalData always passes `reviews ?? []`, so summary is non-null while prepare is loading or failed. With zero reviews it falls to the final else and claims 'not required: The policy requires no approval for this change'. With one review it claims 'The approvals the policy requires are in'. Both are verdicts without evidence. The server's insufficient_approvals detail always carries have/required/scope (ag-mcp verdicts.rs fixture), so the `have + 1` invention is an unnecessary guess.
findings.refined_fix: After the changes-requested branch add `else if (!prep) approved = info('approved','Approved','unknown','checking','Waiting for the policy check…')` before the approval-blocker/summary branches, so ok/na are emitted only when prep is present. In the blocker branch, when detail.required is not a number show `${have} approvals` without inventing a required count. Add a spec: prep=null with reviews=[] gives tone 'unknown'.

findings.excerpt: const bases = await api.history.mergeBase(repo, p.stream, p.head).catch(() => [] as string[])  // :30 .reflog(repo, p.stream, 500).catch(() => [])  // :33 .changeset(repo, landed).catch(() => null)  // :121 catch { authorLeases.value = [] }
findings.problem: All failures while computing the diff base are swallowed and turned into base '' (empty tree). A network blip, 403 or timeout then renders the proposal's entire tree as additions with the banner 'Comparing the empty tree with the proposal's head', i.e. a wrong diff presented as correct. For integrated proposals the reflog is capped at a hard 500 entries and falls back to parents[0] of the landed changeset, which is not the pre-integration stream head for merge integrations. loadAuthorLeases (:121) and auth.loadCapabilities (stores/auth.ts:87-93) likewise swallow errors, so IntegrateDialog silently offers no fencing tokens and the sign-in page silently hides the server's auth methods.
findings.proposed_fix: Propagate errors from diffBase into the diff resource so ChangesTab shows its ErrorState with retry; return an empty base only when the server answers that there is no merge base. Obtain the true pre-integration head from a server field on the proposal (e.g. integrated_from or the operation record) instead of searching a 500-entry reflog. Surface lease/capability load failures as a visible warning. Verify with a real server by stopping it mid-load and by integrating a merge-strategy proposal and comparing the shown diff to the changeset's real delta.
reasons: useProposalData.ts:30,33,35 swallow every mergeBase/reflog/changeset failure into base '', and ChangesTab.vue:37 then prints 'the empty tree' as the comparison base, so a network error or 403 shows the whole tree as additions as if correct. loadAuthorLeases (:121) also hides failures, so IntegrateDialog silently lacks fencing tokens. The auth.loadCapabilities and loadAuthConfig fallbacks are documented best-effort ('old server, offline'), which weakens that part, and the merge-integration parents[0] claim is speculative.

diffBase in useProposalData.ts:30 swallows every error from mergeBase (`.catch(() => [])`), so a 5xx, 403 or timeout turns the base into '' and the whole tree is rendered as additions. The reflog and changeset fallbacks swallow too. The banner only says 'empty tree', so the user is not told it is a failure. Swallowing a NotFound is legitimate, because a proposal into a stream with no head has an empty-tree base. The other items are overstated: loadAuthorLeases only drops optional fencing hints, and the server rejects a wrong integrate anyway. auth.ts:150 loadCapabilities holds limits/versions, not auth methods. The sign-in auth config deliberately falls back to token mode (auth.ts:191).
findings.refined_fix: Make diffBase propagate errors: remove the `.catch` on mergeBase/reflog/changeset so the diff useResource sets its error and ChangesTab shows ErrorState with retry; return '' only when mergeBase answers successfully with an empty list. Fall back from reflog to the landed changeset's parents[0] only when the reflog call succeeds without a match. In loadAuthorLeases keep a `leasesError` ref and show a warning in IntegrateDialog instead of silently using [].

findings.excerpt: const value = await guarded('runs', mine, () => api.agents.runs(r, { limit: 100 }))  // :296 api.proposals.list(r, { state: 'open', page_size: 100 }), :297 { state: 'integrated', page_size: 6 }; RunsTable.vue:28 const limit = ref(100)
findings.problem: The board derives 'Agents running' from the newest 100 runs of any status and then filters isActive client-side. The server applies LIMIT before its active_only filter (ag-server list_runs: tx.runs(agent, limit) then retain status == 'running'; runs ordered by started_at DESC), so a long-running agent older than the newest 100 runs silently disappears from the live board, the quiet-run warnings and the lease holder mapping. Open proposals are capped at 100 the same way and BoardSummary shows board.cards.length (BoardSummary.vue:71) as the total with no truncation notice.
findings.proposed_fix: Fix the server to filter by status in SQL before LIMIT (add a runs_active query) and call it with active_only: true from the board; paginate or show 'N+ open proposals' with a link when next_page_token is non-empty (use a count field on the list response). Verify with a real server seeded with more than 100 finished runs plus one old running run and assert it appears on the board.
reasons: ag-server list_runs (api/agents.rs:141-144) runs tx.runs(agent, limit) (ORDER BY started_at DESC LIMIT) before retaining status=='running', and board.ts:296 requests limit 100 without active_only then filters isActive client-side, so a long-running run older than the 100 newest runs vanishes. board.ts:296-297 also caps open proposals at 100 while BoardSummary.vue:71 shows board.cards.length as the total with no truncation notice.

ag-server list_runs applies `tx.runs(agent, limit)` (LIMIT on the newest runs by started_at DESC) before `retain(status == 'running')` (api/agents.rs:138-144). The board calls api.agents.runs with limit 100 and no active_only, then filters isActive client-side (board.ts:229, 141). A long-running agent older than the newest 100 runs vanishes from 'Agents running', the quiet-run warnings and the lease holder mapping. Open proposals are likewise capped at page_size 100 while BoardSummary shows board.cards.length as the total with no truncation notice.
findings.refined_fix: Server: apply the status filter in SQL before LIMIT (e.g. a runs_active query, `WHERE status='running' ORDER BY started_at DESC LIMIT ?`) and have the board call api.agents.runs(r, {active_only:true}). Web: when proposals.list returns a non-empty next_page_token, show "100+" and a link to the Proposals page in BoardSummary, instead of presenting cards.length as the total.

findings.excerpt: const from = Math.max(0, head.latestSeq - 2500)  // :21 limit: 2500  // :62 Showing events from the last ~2,500 in the repository; the audit log has the complete record.
findings.problem: A proposal's timeline is built by downloading the last 2,500 repository events and filtering them in the browser (the server cannot filter by target). In an active repository an older proposal's history falls outside the window and the tab states 'No events for this proposal yet', which is false. The window size is a hard-coded magic number and the whole 2,500-event payload is fetched on every refresh.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a server-side filter (target / ref, or a proposal-scoped events endpoint) to /events/replay or the audit endpoint and page through it; until then, never show the 'No events yet' empty state when the window did not reach seq 0, and offer 'load earlier events'. Verify against a real server with a proposal followed by more than 2,500 unrelated events.
reasons: TimelineTab.vue:20-22 fetches the last 2500 audit events and filters them client-side because /events/replay only filters by topic (api/events.rs:61-72), so an older proposal's events fall outside the window. The EmptyState at :52-56 still says 'No events for this proposal yet'. A footnote at :62 discloses the window, which softens but does not remove the false empty-state claim.

The limit is disclosed in the same view. TimelineTab.vue always renders the note 'Showing events from the last ~2,500 in the repository; the audit log has the complete record', directly under the empty state. The 2,500 window sits inside the server replay cap of 5,000 (api/events.rs:76). The comment in the code explains that the server cannot filter by target. This is an accurately documented limitation, not a misleading claim.
findings.refined_fix: Short term: name the window constant, and when items are empty and from > 0 render "No events in the last N repository events" plus a 'Load earlier' button that replays the previous window instead of the 'No events yet' title. Long term: add a target/proposal filter to /events/replay (or a proposal-scoped endpoint) and page through it.

findings.excerpt: if (isObj(p) && typeof p.min_approvals === 'number' && p.min_approvals < 1) add('warning', `protected_paths[${idx}].min_approvals`, 'A protected path with no required approvals protects nothing.')  // POLICY_SPEC at :35; summarizePolicy defaults at :357 approvalsMinForAgents: 1 and silent `return none` at :376
findings.problem: The policy editor ships a hand-copied schema (POLICY_SPEC) and validator that duplicate ag-policy and already disagree with it: the server rejects protected_paths[].min_approvals == 0 ('needs min_approvals >= 1') while the UI only warns; the server also enforces run.timeout_secs in 1..86400, valid run.env names, argv non-empty and that required_validations[].issuers appear in trusted_issuers, none of which the UI checks, so it reports 'Looks well-formed' for documents the server refuses. summarizePolicy re-implements the evaluator's defaults (approvalsMinForAgents: 1) and swallows a parse failure into a zeroed summary; board.policySummary (stores/board.ts:121) is not consumed by any component, so it is dead code that still claims to stand in for the evaluator.
findings.proposed_fix: Make the server the single source of truth: add a side-effect-free validate/dry-run operation (PUT /policy?dry_run=true or POST /policy/validate) that runs Policy::parse + validate and returns structured issues with JSON paths, and drive the editor's error list from it (debounced) while keeping only the JSON-position helper client-side. Optionally publish the policy JSON Schema generated from ag-policy in docs/protocol and generate POLICY_SPEC from it (checked in CI like check:api). Delete summarizePolicy/policySummary or feed them from a server-provided summary. Verify with a real ag-server by validating a document with min_approvals 0 and a timeout of 0 and asserting the UI shows the server's messages.
reasons: The server's Policy::validate (ag-policy document.rs:76, 228, 245) rejects run.timeout_secs outside 1..86400, protected_paths[].min_approvals==0 and validation issuers missing from trusted_issuers. policy.ts:294 only warns on min_approvals<1 and has no timeout or issuer-membership checks (only a uint kind at :26), so the editor can say 'Looks well-formed' (:318) for documents the server refuses on save (the error is then shown by PolicyEditor.vue:144). board.policySummary (board.ts:121) is consumed only by live-board.spec.ts, so summarizePolicy is dead in production.

policy.ts opens with 'Client-side structure hints ... They are advice, not the authority: the server parses strictly ... and its message is always shown too'. PolicyEditor.vue renders saveError.message from api.admin.setPolicy, so a document the server refuses is rejected with the server's own reason. The message says 'well-formed', not 'valid'. A missing dry-run endpoint is a feature request. The unused summarizePolicy/policySummary is dead-code hygiene with no user impact.
findings.refined_fix: Minimum buildable fix: in analyzePolicy raise protected_paths[].min_approvals<1 to level 'error' with the server's wording, add errors for run.timeout_secs outside 1..86400 and for required_validations[].issuers entries absent from trusted_issuers, and delete summarizePolicy, board.policySummary and their specs. Longer term: add a side-effect-free validate endpoint (Policy::parse + validate returning structured issues) and drive the editor's error list from it.

findings.excerpt: void enrich(items.slice(0, 60), mine)  // :98 watch(visible, (v) => void enrich(v.slice(0, 60), serial))  // :57 mapLimit(todo, 4, ...) and cell fallbacks counts[(row as Repo).name]?.streams ?? '–'
findings.problem: Stream and changeset counts for the repository list come from one GET per repository (N+1) for only the first 60 rows; every repository beyond the 60th (the list loads up to 1000) shows '–' permanently in the Streams and Changesets columns, and errors in the per-row requests are silently ignored. The listing endpoint documents that it leaves both counts at 0, so the UI works around a missing server capability with a placeholder.
findings.proposed_fix: Have the list endpoint return real counts (cheap metadata counts) or add a batch describe endpoint, then drop enrich(); if counts must stay lazy, fetch for rows as they scroll into view (virtualised table) and show an explicit 'unavailable' state on failure. Verify against a real server with more than 60 repositories.
reasons: ReposView.vue:89 and :98 call enrich on only slice(0, 60), one api.repos.get per row via mapLimit, which records failures as rejected results and ignores them. The list endpoint hard-codes stream_count/changeset_count to 0 (api/repository.rs:23-24), and the page loads up to 1000 repos (MAX_REPOS), so unsearched rows 61+ show '–' permanently. This is a UX limitation with a placeholder, not a wrong value.

ReposView.vue documents that the list endpoint leaves counts at 0 and that describe fills them in. The page fetches them lazily for at most 60 rows, re-enriches on search, and shows an honest '–' (unknown), never a fabricated number. A visible Alert already tells the user to use search to narrow the list. A missing optional statistic with a placeholder is a performance trade-off, not a defect.
findings.refined_fix: Return real stream/changeset counts from the list endpoint (or a batch describe) and delete enrich(). Until then, enrich rows lazily as they enter the viewport, and render 'unavailable' with a retry for rows whose request failed instead of a permanent '–'.

findings.excerpt: await api.agents.extendLease(props.repo, l.id, 15 * 60_000)  // :65 toasts.ok('Lease extended by 15 minutes', l.scope)
findings.problem: The Extend action always extends by a fixed 15 minutes; the operator cannot choose a duration or learn the server's maximum lease TTL, and the number is an unnamed magic constant duplicated in the toast text.
findings.proposed_fix: Show a small duration picker (or a dialog) defaulting to the lease's original TTL (expires_at_ms - acquired_at_ms) and bounded by a server-advertised maximum; name the constant and build the toast text from the chosen value. Verify with a real server by extending a lease and checking the new expires_at_ms.
reasons: LeaseTable.vue:64-65 hard-codes 15 * 60_000 and the matching toast text. Server extend (ag-agent lease.rs:130-139) sets expires_at = now + ttl_ms rather than adding to it, so on a lease with more than 15 minutes left 'Lease extended by 15 minutes' actually shortens it. This is worse than the finding states.

LeaseTable's Extend action is a fixed, visible step: the toast says 'Lease extended by 15 minutes', and the server enforces its own limits and returns an error. Nothing misleads the operator, and repeated clicks extend further. A duration picker is an enhancement.
findings.refined_fix: Define `const EXTEND_MS = 15 * 60_000` and compute `ttl = Math.max(EXTEND_MS, (l.expires_at_ms - serverNow()) + EXTEND_MS)` so the lease really gets 15 minutes more. Build the toast from the same value, or add a duration picker bounded by the server's MAX_TTL_MS. Verify against a real server that expires_at_ms grows by the stated amount.

findings.excerpt: api.streams.reflog(repo.value, selected.value, 100)  // :172 subtitle="Append-only record of every head move"
findings.problem: The reflog card is subtitled 'every head move' but silently shows only the newest 100 entries with no paging or truncation notice.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a Load more control driven by a paged reflog (page_token) or at least show '100 most recent' when the limit is reached. Verify against a stream with more than 100 moves.

StreamsView's subtitle 'Append-only record of every head move' describes the reflog as a record, not the table. The table lists newest-first rows with a Version column, so a window of 100 is visible (v250 down to v151). The reflog request has only `limit` and no paging (proto ReflogRequest). findings.excerpt: const blocked = computed(() => board.cards.length - ready.value)  // :78 {{ quiet > 0 ? `${quiet} quiet` : 'all heartbeating' }}
findings.problem: 'held back' is computed as every open proposal that is not provably ready, so proposals whose prepare result is still loading or failed are reported as held back (blocked). 'all heartbeating' is printed whenever no run is over the viewer-side threshold, including when zero agents are running.
findings.proposed_fix: Count held back only from proposals with loaded prep data and show 'checking N' separately; show 'no agents running' when activeRuns is empty. Verify with a real server while prepare is delayed.
reasons: BoardSummary.vue:26 defines blocked = cards.length - ready, where ready requires c.prep?.data, so proposals whose prepare is still loading or failed are counted as 'held back' (:71). Line 78 prints 'all heartbeating' whenever quiet===0, including with zero active runs.

In BoardSummary.vue, `ready` counts only cards whose prep data loaded cleanly, and `blocked = board.cards.length - ready`. Proposals whose prepare result is still loading or errored are therefore reported as 'held back' (blocked). The 'Agents running' tile prints 'all heartbeating' whenever quiet === 0, including with zero active runs. Both state a condition without evidence.
findings.refined_fix: Compute `checking = cards.filter(c => !c.prep?.data).length` and `held = cards.filter(c => c.prep?.data && (blockers.length || conflicts.length)).length`, and render "{ready} ready · {held} held back · {checking} checking". For agents use `activeRuns.length === 0 ? 'no agents running' : quiet > 0 ? ... : 'all heartbeating'`.

findings.excerpt: if (e instanceof ApiError && e.isNotFound && /no changesets yet/.test(e.message)) {  // FilesView.vue:75 same regex, comment 'Servers that predate the empty listing answered 404 "no changesets yet"'
findings.problem: Whether a stream is empty is decided by regex-matching the free-form English text of a 404 message. Any server wording change, localisation or proxy rewrite turns an ordinary empty state into a hard error (or the reverse), and FilesView carries compat code for server versions that no longer exist.
findings.proposed_fix: Make the server return an empty page (history log) or a typed error detail (e.g. code stream_empty) and key the UI on that; delete the legacy branch in FilesView. Verify against a real freshly created repository with no changesets.
reasons: HistoryView.vue:78 and FilesView.vue:75 match /no changesets yet/ against the free-text 404 message. The server still emits that exact English text from ag-integrate history.rs:166 and HistoryView relies on it, so any wording change turns the empty state into an error. The FilesView branch is dead on current servers because tree_at (api/tree.rs:53-60) already returns an empty tree for a stream with no head.

The 404 text 'has no changesets yet' is a stable string emitted by ag-integrate (history.rs:166) and matched the same way by the CLI (ag-cli errors.rs:41). The UI is shipped inside ag-server (web_dir), so UI and server version together. The regex is a pragmatic internal contract, and a mismatch would surface as a visible error, not a silent wrong state. A typed error code would be nicer but this is not a defect that hurts users.
findings.refined_fix: Make history.log for a stream without a head return an empty page (or a typed error code such as stream_empty) and key HistoryView on that. Delete the legacy catch branch and its comment in FilesView.vue:73-78.

findings.excerpt: honouring `Retry-After`, with a cap. `429` is always waited out.
findings.problem: The README says 429 is always waited out, but api/client.ts (lines 223-231) stops after maxRetries (3) and rethrows when the computed wait exceeds maxRetryWaitMs (30 s), so a 429 with a long Retry-After or repeated 429s surfaces as an error.
findings.proposed_fix: Reword to 'retried up to 3 times, waiting at most 30 s per attempt' (and make those two values configurable as proposed above), or implement the unbounded wait. Verify with the existing client spec using a real server rate limit.
reasons: README.md:76 says '429 is always waited out', but client.ts:224-230 rethrows once attempt >= maxRetries (default 3, :106) or when the computed wait exceeds maxRetryWaitMs (30_000, :107), so repeated 429s or a long Retry-After surface as errors. shouldRetry (:236-244) only decides eligibility.

The README sentence reads 'honouring Retry-After, with a cap. 429 is always waited out'. It follows the retry rule directly: shouldRetry in client.ts returns true for 429/503 regardless of method safety, while other errors need a safe or keyed request. The 'with a cap' clause already announces the bound (maxRetries 3, maxRetryWaitMs 30 s). 'Always' is about eligibility, not guaranteed success, so the README is not materially wrong.
findings.refined_fix: Reword README.md:76 to "`429` and `503` are retried (up to 3 times, waiting at most 30 s per attempt, honouring `Retry-After`); beyond that the error is surfaced."

Remove the setStr defaults at config.go:361-362 and the `case "scripted"` at config.go:470-475, so validate only accepts `command`. Make manager.go newExecutor return commandExecutor{cfg: c} only. Turn the check.go:164 `default` branch into an error. Change examples/orchestrator.yaml docs-bot to `type: command`, and update README lines 52, 87, 191, 204, 238 and 260-262.
