findings.excerpt: jitter: func() float64 { return 0.5 }, maxBody: 64 << 20,    // doc at line 270: "backoff is the exponential step ... with ±20% jitter"
findings.problem: The default jitter source is the constant 0.5, so production backoff (HTTP retries, client.go:276) and SSE reconnects (sse.go:128) have no jitter at all although the code and comments promise ±20%. app.go never calls WithJitter. After a server restart every orchestrator client and every repository follower retries in lock-step (thundering herd). maxBody 64 MiB is also fixed and not configurable.
findings.proposed_fix: Default `jitter` to `rand.Float64` (math/rand/v2) and keep WithJitter only for tests; verify with a unit test that two clients produce different delays and that delays stay within ±20%. Expose max response size via config if operators need it.
reasons: client.go:132 sets `jitter: func() float64 { return 0.5 }`. The only non-test reference to WithJitter is its own definition, and app.go:buildClients never passes it. backoff() (client.go:276) therefore multiplies by exactly 1.0. sse.go:128 reconnects with the same jitter, so retries and SSE reconnects have no jitter although the doc comment promises ±20%.

Confirmed in client.go:132: the default jitter is `func() float64 { return 0.5 }`. The factor 0.8+0.4*0.5 is exactly 1.0, so there is no jitter. backoff() (client.go:270-277) and Follower.wait (sse.go:128) both use it, and the comments promise ±20%. grep shows nothing in app/ calls WithJitter. After a server restart, every orchestrator client and per-repository follower retries on the same schedule. The existing tests already accept ±20% (client_test.go:237, sse_test.go within()), so a real random source does not break them.
findings.refined_fix: In client.go import "math/rand/v2" and set `jitter: rand.Float64` in New (the top-level functions are goroutine-safe, which matters because Follower and the client share it). Existing tests rely on the constant 0.5, for example the exact doubling asserted at sse_test.go:215-218 and the timings in client_test.go:228-394. Give those tests `WithJitter(func() float64 { return 0.5 })`. Add one unit test that the delay stays within [0.8,1.2]*step across many calls.

findings.problem: When the reviewer/advisor credential variable is unset the components are still enabled and wired to the orchestrator's own credential, which by design lacks proposal.review (README.md:127-129, requirements.go:21-26). In `run` this only produces a warning; afterwards every review/advice pass is guaranteed to fail with permission_denied and be logged as a reconcile error forever. It is a fallback that cannot work (silently does nothing useful) and the warning text ('posted with the orchestrator's identity') is misleading.
findings.proposed_fix: Make it a startup error (or automatically disable review/advisor for that repo and show `disabled: no credential` in /status and /readyz) instead of falling back; keep the fallback out of the code. Verify with an integration test: start without AG_REVIEWER_TOKEN and assert the documented behaviour against the real server.
reasons: app.go:buildClients runs on every `run`. When the reviewer or advisor variable is unset it logs a Warn and reuses the orchestrator's credential. requirements.go says that credential deliberately lacks proposal.review, and neither review.go nor advisor.go handles permission_denied specially, so with the README's scoped credential every pass fails and is retried. The claim 'guaranteed' is overstated: an unscoped admin credential can post, and `check` already reports the scope error.

Read app.go:158-176, check.go:75-122 and README.md:127-129. The fallback is documented, and `check` reports it as an error with an explicit hint naming the unset variable. It does work when the orchestrator's credential is unrestricted, because the admin role may review, and that case is separately warned about. When scoped, the failures are recorded (rec.Error, reconcile error, /status). Making it fatal or disabling reviews would change a documented design, not fix a stub.
findings.refined_fix: Do not keep a fallback that is known not to work. In Preflight, for each label in a.shared, inspect the Whoami principal. If p.Scope.Operations is non-empty and lacks "proposal.review", log at Error and record a.disabled[label] = "no credential ("+env+" unset)". In Run, check a.disabled after waitReady and do not start rt.review or rt.advisor for it. Show `disabled: <reason>` in /status and make /readyz report it. Reword the Warn to say the orchestrator credential is used only if it carries proposal.review.

findings.problem: If the server's conflict prediction fails (permission, 5xx, timeout) the scheduler silently proceeds as if there were no overlaps (debug log only, no metric, nothing in /status) and starts overlapping work that `placement: avoid` is supposed to defer. A swallowed error that hides lost functionality.
findings.proposed_fix: Log at warn, count it (e.g. orchestrator_prediction_errors_total), expose `prediction_error` in scheduler Status, and make the behaviour explicit and configurable (`placement_on_predict_error: defer|start`, default defer). Test against the real server with a credential lacking `predict`.
reasons: scheduler.go:253-257 (pass, reached from scheduler.Run via app.go) logs a Predict error at Debug and sets overlaps = nil. No metric, no Status field and no warning exist, so `placement: avoid` silently stops deferring overlapping work whenever the prediction call fails.

Confirmed at scheduler.go:253-257. A Predict error is logged only at Debug, then overlaps is set to nil and placement proceeds. Nothing in metrics or /status shows that one of the documented placement signals is down. The README lists the server's overlap prediction as part of conflict-aware placement. A persistent failure (a server without predict, or a scope problem `check` does not catch) silently degrades `placement: avoid`. Fail-open is a defensible design, and the config option and default-defer in the proposed fix are overkill. Being invisible is the defect.
findings.refined_fix: Replace the block with `overlaps, perr := s.o.API.Predict(...)`. On error, take s.mu, set s.predictErr = perr.Error() and clear it on success, then log at Warn "conflict prediction unavailable; placement ignores server overlap this pass" and increment a counter (for example metrics.PredictErrors.With(repo)). Add `PredictError string` to scheduler.Status. Optionally add a `placement_on_predict_error: start|defer` setting, default start to keep today's behaviour.

findings.excerpt:
mu        sync.Mutex
attempts  map[string]int
tempFails map[string]int
retryAt   map[string]time.Time
awaiting  map[string]awaitInfo   // in-memory only; candidates() adopts any in_progress task with attempts==0 (line 349)
findings.problem: The retry budget (`schedule.attempts`, README.md:166), the EX_TEMPFAIL counter and the backoff timers live only in process memory. After an orchestrator restart a task that failed and was waiting for retry is in_progress with no live run, so it is adopted as attempt 1 again: `attempts: N` and the 'at most ten' tempfail limit are not honoured across restarts, and a crash-looping orchestrator or executor can retry a task without bound.
findings.proposed_fix: Derive attempts from server state: count the task's finished failed runs (ListRuns by task/agent, run summaries already record attempt numbers) when rebuilding after restart, and persist retryAt/tempFails in state_dir or as run summaries. Verify with an integration test that restarts the orchestrator between attempts (harness already supports StateDir reuse).
reasons: scheduler.go:104-107 keeps attempts, tempFails, retryAt and awaiting only in memory. candidates() (scheduler.go:341-350) adopts any in_progress task of a managed agent with no live run and no open proposal when hasHistory() is false, and after a restart attempts[id] is 0. startSession then computes attempt = 0+1, so `schedule.attempts` and the ten-EX_TEMPFAIL limit reset on each orchestrator restart.

Confirmed. attempts, tempFails and retryAt are in-memory maps (scheduler.go:104-107). candidates() (line 349) adopts any in_progress task of a managed agent with no live run, no open proposal and no history in this process, as a fresh attempt. After a restart during retry wait, the task is adopted at once with a full budget. That contradicts README.md:245 ('retried within `attempts`, then cancelled') and the `attempts` comment. The blast radius is limited (default attempts is 1, and it needs an orchestrator restart mid-retry). It is not documented, so it is not an accepted limitation.
findings.refined_fix: When a task is adopted and has no entry in s.attempts, seed s.attempts[t.ID] from the server. Call s.o.API.ListRuns(ctx, repo, "agent-name", false, 200) (activeOnly=false), count runs with TaskID == t.ID and Status == "failed", and set the counter to that number. Compare it with Schedule.Attempts before starting, and return session.Cancel semantics (cancel the task) when the budget is already spent. Do the same for tempFails, which is derivable from run summaries. Add an integration test that restarts the orchestrator between attempts, reusing StateDir.

findings.problem: For a proposal into an empty stream only the first 60 files are fetched, files over 128 KiB or that fail to download are skipped with the error swallowed, and the rest are counted as added with 0 lines and no patch. Secret scanning, size and test checks therefore silently never see most of an initial import, and the summary does not say so (Truncated stays false), while the comment claims to have inspected the change. The limits are not configurable.
findings.proposed_fix: Inspect all files (page through the tree; use the server's tree.diff against the empty tree if supported) or, when a limit applies, set Summary.Truncated and name the uninspected files in the comment; surface fetch errors. Move the limits to `review:` config. Test against the real server with an initial import containing a planted secret in file #61.
reasons: review.go:226-240 (rootFiles, used by changes() when the stream head is empty) fetches content for only the first maxRootFiles=60 entries. It silently skips any file whose GetFile fails, including files over 128 KiB, and still counts all entries as added with 0 lines. changes() returns `files, false, err`, so Summary.Truncated stays false and the comment does not mention the gap. Secret, size and test checks never see those files.

Confirmed in review.go:219-241. For a proposal into an empty stream, only the first 60 entries (maxRootFiles) are fetched. Files over 128 KiB or failing GetFile are silently skipped (`if err == nil`), and the rest are counted as added with 0 lines and no patch. changes() returns truncated=false for this path. review() then returns without any comment when `len(findings)==0 && !truncated` (line 272), so a 200-file initial import with a secret in file 61 gets silence that reads as clean. The existing Truncated rendering (line 340) was meant for exactly this kind of partial inspection.
findings.refined_fix: Change `rootFiles` to return `([]agwp.FileDiff, int, error)`, where the int counts entries not inspected: those at i >= maxRootFiles and those whose GetFile returned an error (log the error at Debug). Return it from `changes`, add `Uninspected int` to Summary, set it in `review`, and have Render add "_N file(s) were not inspected (too many or too large)_". Do not reuse Truncated, because its text says the server truncated the diff. Move maxRootFiles and maxRootBytes into `review:` config.

findings.problem: Proposal analysis ignores the documented/configured `index.max_file_bytes` (config.go:137, README.md:185, default 256 KiB) and `index.max_files`, using its own fixed 512 KiB / 30 / 10 instead: a configured argument that is accepted and ignored for half of the semantic index, and an operator cannot tune it.
findings.proposed_fix: Use c.o.Repo.Index.MaxBytes for GetFile and add configurable `index.proposal_max_files` and `index.proposals_per_pass`; mark `Partial` with the reason. Cover by a test that sets a small max_file_bytes and expects the proposal file to be skipped.
reasons: semindex/overlap.go:21-25 uses fixed maxFilesPerProposal=30, maxFileBytes=512<<10 and maxAnalysesPerPass=10, and GetFile at lines 109 and 115 passes the constant. `index.max_file_bytes` (config.go:137, default 256 KiB) is used only for stream indexing at component.go:181, so the documented limit does not govern proposal analysis. The Partial flag already exists, so only the limit source needs changing.

README.md:185 defines `index.max_file_bytes` as the limit for files the stream index holds ('larger files are not indexed'), and component.go:181 honours it. The per-proposal analysis in overlap.go is a separate bounded pass with its own caps. It marks the result `Partial` whenever a file is skipped or the 30-file cap is hit (overlap.go:104-118). So the limits are surfaced, not silent, and no documented setting is ignored.
findings.refined_fix: In analyze(), compute `limit := int64(c.o.Repo.Index.MaxBytes); if limit <= 0 { limit = 512 << 10 }` and use it for both GetFile calls instead of maxFileBytes. Optionally add `index.proposal_max_files` and `index.proposals_per_pass` to config, defaulting to 30 and 10. Add a unit test with a small max_file_bytes that expects the file to be skipped and Partial to be true.

findings.excerpt: rt.review, err = review.New(review.Options{Repo: rc, API: a.reviewer, Reviewer: "service:reviewer", ...
findings.problem: The reviewer identity printed in every posted comment ('<sub>... run by a service identity (service:reviewer)') is a hardcoded string, not the identity the credential really authenticates as (known from Whoami in Preflight). With the fallback credential or a differently named service account the comment states the wrong author.
findings.proposed_fix: Take the identity from a.principals["reviewer"].Identity after preflight (pass a func or set it in Run) and test against the real server with a reviewer credential minted for a different subject name.
reasons: app.go:229 passes the literal "service:reviewer" as review.Options.Reviewer. review.go:291 and :330 render it into every posted comment (`(service:reviewer)`) and into Status. The credential's real identity is known only after Preflight (a.principals["reviewer"].Identity), so with the fallback credential or another subject name the comment names the wrong author.

review.Options.Reviewer is commented 'informational' (review.go:49). The documented convention is the identity `service:reviewer` (README.md:123, guide section 2). The server records the true author of every review, so the audit trail is correct. Only a cosmetic footer in the comment can differ, when an operator uses a non-standard subject name or the credential fallback. It is not a hardcoded credential or fake data, and the effect is negligible.
findings.refined_fix: build() runs before Preflight, so the identity cannot be passed at construction time. Add `func (c *Component) SetReviewer(id string)` guarded by c.mu, with Render reading it under the lock. In App.Preflight, after `a.principals[label] = p`, call `rt.review.SetReviewer(p.Identity)` for each repo whose review is non-nil when label == "reviewer". Keep "service:reviewer" only as the pre-preflight default.

findings.problem: Nothing is redacted or re-checked: `orchestrator config` marshals the whole struct, including `executors[].env` values and `scripted.files`, which may hold secrets pasted by an operator. Validation only checks that *_env names match an identifier regex, which a token like `agt_cred_abc...` also satisfies, and the resulting 'environment variable <token> is empty or unset' error (config.go:407,425) then echoes the pasted token. The 'never carries a token' guarantee is not implemented.
findings.proposed_fix: Implement real redaction in Redacted (mask env values whose keys look secret and all `env` values by default) and reject values of the form of known credentials in the file (agt_ prefix, high-entropy strings in *_env fields) without echoing them in messages; add tests for both.
reasons: main.go:74 prints cfg.Redacted(), which config.go:639 implements as yaml.Marshal(c) with no masking, despite the comment that it 'repeats the check explicitly'. Executor `env` values and `scripted.files` are printed verbatim. envRE (config.go:197) is `^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$`, which a token such as `agt_cred_abc_def` satisfies. config.go:407 then echoes that value as 'environment variable agt_... is empty or unset' under run and check. The 'file can never carry a token' guarantee is therefore not enforced.

Verified. Redacted() (config.go:636-643) is a bare yaml.Marshal and does not 'repeat the check' as its comment claims. It prints executors[].env values and scripted.files verbatim. envRE (`^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$`, line 197) accepts a pasted token such as `agt_x_...`, so the file is not refused as config.go:5-6 and README.md:134 claim. The token is then echoed by the 'environment variable %s is empty or unset' error (lines 407,425) and the `got %q` message. The existing test (config_test.go:275) only covers a token held in the environment. The impact is low but the stated guarantee is false.
findings.refined_fix: In Redacted, marshal a deep copy in which every Executors[i].Env value is replaced by "<redacted>" (keep keys), and blank Script.Files contents or replace them by their byte lengths. In validate, add a helper `looksLikeCredential(v)` that is true for the `agt_` prefix or a length over 64. Use it before the envRE check on every *_token_env field to add a fixed message 'must be the NAME of an environment variable (looks like a credential)' that does not include the value, and never format p.v into the 'empty or unset' errors. Extend TestRedactedOutputHasNoSecrets for both.

findings.problem: `check` re-implements the server's role-binding repo patterns with only exact / `*` / trailing-`*` support, whereas the server matches them with the globset crate (crates/ag-server/src/authz.rs:240 glob_match: `?`, `[..]`, `{a,b}`, inner `*`). A valid binding such as `acme/we?` or `*/web` makes `check` report a false 'no admin role on <repo>' error (check.go:91-93).
findings.proposed_fix: Do not guess: determine access by a real probe per repository (an admin-only dry call or a minting attempt with the exact scope) or at least compile the pattern with the repo's glob package using globset semantics; add a test against the real server with a wildcard binding.
reasons: check.go:197-205 matchPattern supports only `*`, exact match and trailing `*`. The server matches repo patterns in role bindings with the globset crate (authz.rs:240 and :345 `glob_match(&b.repo, repo)`). whoami returns roles as `<b.repo>:<role>` (api/session.rs:57-58). A valid binding like `acme/we?` or `*/web` therefore makes Check report 'no admin role on <repo>' as an error on a correctly configured server.

Confirmed. check.go matchPattern (lines 197-205) supports only `*`, an exact match and a trailing `*`. The server matches repo patterns with globset (authz.rs:240-241 glob_match, used for role bindings at 342-350), which also handles `?`, `[..]`, `{a,b}` and inner `*`. A valid binding such as `*/web:admin` or `acme/we?:admin` makes `check` report a false 'no admin role on acme/web' error (check.go:91-93). The proposed reuse of internal/glob would be wrong. That package uses path-component semantics where `*` stops at `/` (glob.go header), while globset's `*` crosses `/`.
findings.refined_fix: Replace matchPattern with a translation of globset semantics (default `*` crosses `/`) to an anchored regexp. Map `*` to `.*`, `?` to `.`, `[..]` to a class with `!` or `^` negated, `{a,b}` to `(?:a|b)`, and regexp.QuoteMeta for the rest, then match on `^...$`. If the pattern cannot be translated, downgrade the result to a `warn` ('cannot verify role pattern %q locally') instead of an error. Do not reuse internal/glob, whose `*` stops at `/`. Add tests for `acme/we?`, `*/web` and `acme/{web,api}`.

findings.excerpt:
// maxSymbols bounds the derived tables: beyond it, further definitions are not indexed.
const maxSymbols = 200_000   (rebuildLocked: if x.symbols >= maxSymbols { break }, line 132)  |  extract.go:49-51 maxDefsPerFile = 500, maxIdentsPerFile = 512; extract.go:98-100 defs = defs[:maxDefsPerFile]
findings.problem: Definitions beyond 200,000 in total, 500 per file, and identifiers beyond 512 per file are dropped without any counter, log or field in /index/status (Skipped covers only files), so symbol queries and `references` counts are silently incomplete on large repositories; none of the limits can be tuned.
findings.proposed_fix: Count dropped definitions/identifiers in Skipped/Stats and metrics, log once per sync, and move the limits to `index:` config (max_symbols, max_defs_per_file, max_idents_per_file). Test on a generated large file / repository.
reasons: semindex/index.go:132 breaks the definition loop once maxSymbols=200000 is reached. extract.go:98-100 truncates defs to maxDefsPerFile=500 and identCounts caps idents at 512. None of these drops is counted, since Skipped covers whole files only, so queries and `references` are silently incomplete on large repositories and /index/status never says so.

The caps (index.go:117 maxSymbols=200000, extract.go:49-51 per-file limits) are named constants with comments and implement the README's 'bounded memory and disk' promise. The index is documented as a line-based extractor. Dropping definitions beyond a safety bound in a best-effort advisory index is a deliberate resource guard. Files over the limits are already counted in Skipped. It affects only symbol queries and the overlap hints, not correctness of SCM state.
findings.refined_fix: Add `DroppedDefs int` and `DroppedIdents int` to `Skipped` (or to `Stats`). Count them in rebuildLocked when `x.symbols >= maxSymbols`, and have Extract report the number cut, for example by returning it in Symbols. Sum them in Component.Sync, expose them in /index/status, and log one Info line per sync when non-zero. Optionally move the limits to `index:` config.

findings.excerpt:
case errors.Is(err, agwp.ErrResponseTooLarge):
	return &File{Content: make([]byte, max+1)}, nil // reported as "too large" by the rules
findings.problem: A zero-filled placeholder buffer of up to max+1 bytes (1 MiB by default) is fabricated to signal 'too large' to the rules via its length, instead of carrying the condition explicitly; it allocates needlessly and any rule that looks at content would see fake data.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `TooLarge bool` (and Size) to advisor.File, have Rules.Suggest check it, and drop the fabricated buffer; unit-test with the real server returning too_large for an oversized file.
reasons: advisor.go:240 returns `&File{Content: make([]byte, max+1)}` (up to about 1 MiB of zeros per file, three files per conflict, default max 1<<20) as a sentinel for 'too large'. rules.go isText then rejects it only because len > max or because of NUL bytes. This is a fabricated buffer on the production path used instead of a flag. The effect is small.

advisor.go:240 builds a max+1-byte zero buffer only so the rules see len>max and report 'too large'. It is an internal encoding choice with no operator-visible effect: nothing posts the buffer, and the size is checked before content. At most 1 MiB is allocated per oversized file. It is a code-style nit, not a stub or fake data.
findings.refined_fix: In advisor/rules.go change `type File struct { Content []byte }` to `type File struct { Content []byte; TooLarge bool }`. In load() return `&File{TooLarge: true}` for ErrResponseTooLarge. In Rules.Suggest the loop becomes `if f != nil && (f.TooLarge || !isText(f.Content, max))`. Update the note to say 'larger than N bytes' when TooLarge is set. Add a unit test for the TooLarge input.

findings.problem: Refresh (15s) and Recent (20) are never wired to config (app.go:209 does not set them), ListJobs is capped at a fixed 200, and errors from ListJobs/ListQueue are swallowed so /status shows a stale or empty validation/integration queue without any error indication.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `validations.refresh`, `validations.recent` and `validations.jobs_limit` to config, and record job/queue listing errors in Status.LastError (or separate fields). Test with a credential lacking jobs.read/queue.read against the real server.
reasons: app.go:209 builds execsched.Options without Refresh or Recent, so the 15s and 20 defaults are fixed. execsched.go:292-301 calls ListJobs(…, 200) and ListQueue and drops the error (`jerr == nil`, `qerr == nil`), so a failing or permission-denied listing leaves /status with a stale or empty validation or integration queue and no error indication.

Refresh (15s) and Recent (20) are documented Options fields with stated defaults (execsched.go:123-127), and the reconcile cadence is configurable through `loop:`. The swallowed ListJobs/ListQueue errors at lines 292-304 only affect the display view in /status, which is refreshed on the next pass. They do not affect scheduling or safety, so this is an unconfigured tunable, not a defect.
findings.refined_fix: Capture the errors: `var listErr error`; on `jerr != nil` or `qerr != nil` set listErr, and after the block store it in s.listErr under s.mu. In Status(), if LastError is empty, set it to "listing validation jobs/integration queue: "+err. Add `validations.refresh` and `validations.recent` to config and pass them in app.go:209, keeping the defaults of 15s and 20. Test with a credential lacking jobs.read or queue.read.

findings.excerpt:
# NOTE: this Dockerfile has not been built by its authors (the machine it was
# written on has a Docker client but no daemon). ...  ARG VERSION=dev   (app.go:37: var Version = "dev")
findings.problem: The only packaging of the service is unbuilt and untested; neither .github/workflows/ci.yml nor release.yml nor deploy/ builds or references the orchestrator image, so no shipped artifact carries a real version (Version stays "dev", User-Agent `agentgit-orchestrator/dev`). README.md:354-356 admits it.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a CI job that `docker build`s the image, runs `orchestrator version`, `check` and a smoke `run` against a real ag-server container (compose), and wire release.yml to pass VERSION=${tag}; then remove the NOTE and the README caveat.
reasons: The Dockerfile header says it has never been built. Greps of .github/workflows and deploy/ found no docker build of the orchestrator and no VERSION wiring. ci.yml:197-214 only runs go vet and tests, and README admits it (354-356). So the packaged artifact is untested and its version stays "dev" (app.go Version).

The Dockerfile NOTE and README.md:354-356 / docs/guides/orchestrator.md:377 openly state the image has not been built. There is no false claim, only a missing CI job, which is a roadmap item. Version staying `dev` for source builds is normal until a release is cut. The disclosure makes this an accurate documented limitation.
findings.refined_fix: Add a ci.yml job or step (needs only docker, no ag-server) that runs `docker build --build-arg VERSION=ci -t agentgit/agent-orchestrator:ci services/agent-orchestrator` and then `docker run --rm agentgit/agent-orchestrator:ci version`. Pass `--build-arg VERSION=${{ github.ref_name }}` in release.yml. Check that the `golang:1.27` base tag in the Dockerfile exists and matches go.mod, for example by pinning it to the toolchain CI uses. Remove the NOTE and the README caveat once the job is green.

findings.excerpt:
- The OpenAPI document lists `application/octet-stream` for the `200` of `objects.put`, which answers JSON
  (`{"object_id": ..., ...}`). `sdk/api-policy.json` overrides that one response; everything else about request and
  response bodies (`tree.file`, `objects.get`, `objects.put`, `events.subscribe`) comes from the document.
findings.problem: The claim is false today. openapi.json now lists `application/json` for the 200 of objects.put (`test/server-gaps.test.ts` line 140 asserts exactly that). `sdk/api-policy.json` has an empty `bodies` section (lines 62-64: "none today"), so nothing overrides the response. The README describes a workaround that no longer exists and a spec defect that has since been partly fixed. The same text is in the Python README.
findings.proposed_fix: Delete or rewrite the bullet in both READMEs (and docs/guides/sdks.md if it repeats it) to state what is true: the document lists JSON for objects.put, but its schema is still `{type: string, format: binary}` (see the PutObjectResult finding). Add a doc test, like the existing sdk/tools/sync_doc_samples.py check, that fails when a README claims an override that api-policy.json does not contain.
reasons: README.md:419 says api-policy.json overrides the objects.put 200, but api-policy.json `bodies` holds only a $comment ('none today') and docs/protocol/openapi.json already lists application/json for that 200 (emitted by http.rs:402 `.response_body("application/json")`, pinned by server-gaps.test.ts:139-147). The same stale text is in python/README.md:450 and docs/guides/sdks.md:519.

Confirmed stale. openapi.json objects.put 200 lists only application/json (commit 30d4c1f; server-gaps.test.ts:140 pins it). api-policy.json `bodies` holds only a $comment, and both generators read `bodies[id]` with nothing to find, so no override exists. README lines 419-421 describe an octet-stream entry and an override that are gone, and docs/guides/sdks.md:519-520 repeats the claim.
findings.refined_fix: Delete the objects.put bullet from sdk/typescript/README.md (419-421), sdk/python/README.md (450-452) and docs/guides/sdks.md (519-520). Also drop the 'one override in sdk/api-policy.json' phrase there and 'which bodies are binary' in python/README.md ~433, since `bodies` is empty. Optionally extend sdk/tools/sync_doc_samples.py or the generators' tests to fail if a README mentions an override that api-policy.json does not contain.

findings.excerpt:
* The OpenAPI document lists `application/octet-stream` for the `200` of `objects.put`, which answers JSON
  (`{"object_id": ..., ...}`). `sdk/api-policy.json` overrides that one response;
findings.problem: Same stale claim as in the TypeScript README. api-policy.json `bodies` is empty and openapi.json already lists application/json for objects.put, so no override exists.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove or correct the bullet and cover it with the same doc-consistency test as the TypeScript README.

Same stale claim at sdk/python/README.md:450-452. `bodies` in api-policy.json is empty and openapi.json already lists application/json for objects.put, so the stated override does not exist.

findings.problem: The response model of objects.put is hand-written in each SDK (types.ts:38-43, sdk/python/scripts/generate.py:148-154, plus the SPECIAL signature at generate.mjs:141-142). The OpenAPI schema for that 200 is `{"type":"string","format":"binary"}` while the media type is application/json, so the wire message has no schema. The SDK types can drift from the server without any generator check. The comment also contradicts the READMEs.
findings.proposed_fix: Define a real `PutObjectResponse {object_id, stored}` message in proto/agwp and openapi.json on the server side. Point objects.put's 200 at it. Regenerate both SDKs and delete the three hand-written copies. The generators can then drop the 'objects.put' special case for the result type. Verify with test/server-gaps and test_server_gaps against a real ag-server.
reasons: routes.rs:231-243 emits `{type:string, format:binary}` for every non-SSE raw response, so objects.put's application/json 200 has no real schema (http.rs:441 builds json!({object_id, stored}) by hand). PutObjectResult is hand-written in types.ts:38, python generate.py:148-154 and generate.mjs:141-142. Real-server tests (lifecycle.test.ts:217, retries.test.ts:259) do assert `stored`, so drift would be caught later, not by the generator.

The comment 'not described by the OpenAPI document' is accurate: the schema is {string, binary}. The hand-written PutObjectResult is a deliberate, documented gap, and real-server tests pin the shape (lifecycle.test.ts:217 and retries.test.ts:259 assert `stored`, server-gaps.test.ts:140 asserts `object_id`). The proposed fix is a server proto change outside the sdks area. The stale README text is already covered by findings 0/1.
findings.refined_fix: Add a `PutObjectResponse {string object_id; bool stored}` message to proto/agwp/v1, make the handler in crates/ag-server/src/http.rs:441 return it, and let RouteMeta::raw routes carry an optional JSON response schema ref so routes.rs:234-243 emits `$ref: #/components/schemas/PutObjectResponse` for objects.put. Regenerate openapi.json and both SDKs, delete the three hand-written PutObjectResult definitions, and make the generators map objects.put to the generated type.

findings.excerpt: timeout = httpx.Timeout(connect=30.0, read=idle_timeout_s, write=30.0, pool=30.0)
findings.problem: The event-stream connection uses fixed 30 s connect, write and pool timeouts that no client argument or CallOptions can change. They are not tied to `request_timeout_ms`. An operator behind a slow proxy, or one who wants fast failover, cannot tune them. The same line is in `_async.py:167`. The TypeScript client has no connect timeout at all for streams (transport.ts:234 `fetch(... signal: options.signal)`), so a blackholed host blocks until the OS TCP timeout. The two SDKs therefore disagree.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a `connect_timeout_ms` option (Python) and `connectTimeoutMs` (TypeScript) to the subscription options or the client config, defaulting to `request_timeout_ms`. Use it in both open_stream implementations; in TypeScript, arm an AbortController timer until the response headers arrive. Test against a real ag-server plus a listening-but-silent socket, as retries.test.ts already does for the unary path.
reasons: _sync.py:161 and _async.py:167 hard-code `httpx.Timeout(connect=30.0, write=30.0, pool=30.0)` and pass it explicitly to http.stream, so neither config.request_timeout_ms nor the injected http client can change it. TS transport.ts:234 calls fetch with only `signal`, so it has no connect timeout for streams; the two SDKs disagree.

A 30 s connect/write/pool timeout is a sane fixed default for a stream open. The idle (read) timeout is configurable via idle_timeout_ms, and a TS caller can always abort through `signal`. The TS stream is bounded by the runtime's own connect and header timeouts, not unbounded. This is a minor tuning/parity gap, and nobody is misled or hurt.
findings.refined_fix: Python (both files): `rt = self.config.request_timeout_ms / 1000; timeout = httpx.Timeout(connect=rt, write=rt, pool=rt, read=idle_timeout_s)`. TypeScript openStream: arm `setTimeout(() => connectCtl.abort(), this.config.requestTimeoutMs)` on a controller that is also aborted when `options.signal` aborts (keep that link for the life of the body), clear the timer once `fetch` resolves, and if the timer fired throw the same network/deadline error `wrapNetworkError` produces. Add a test with a listening-but-silent socket, like retries.test.ts does for unary calls.

findings.excerpt: idle_s = (idle_timeout_ms or DEFAULT_IDLE_MS) / 1000
findings.problem: `idle_timeout_ms=0` is silently replaced by the 90 s default in Python (also line 130). In TypeScript `idleTimeoutMs: 0` disables the watchdog (sse.ts:136 `?? DEFAULT_IDLE_MS`, readSse `idleTimeoutMs > 0`). The Python argument is accepted but ignored for 0, and the watchdog can never be turned off. Python also has no equivalent of TypeScript's `reconnect: false`; `ReconnectPolicy(max_attempts=0)` still reconnects forever after a clean close that delivered events, because `failures` resets to 0.
findings.proposed_fix: Use `DEFAULT_IDLE_MS if idle_timeout_ms is None else idle_timeout_ms`. Treat 0 as 'no watchdog' by passing `read=None` to httpx. Accept `reconnect=False` and return after the first drop. Add real-server tests for both, mirroring events.test.ts.
reasons: _events.py:68 and :130 use `(idle_timeout_ms or DEFAULT_IDLE_MS)`, so 0 becomes 90 s, while sse.ts:136 uses `??` and readSse treats 0 as no watchdog. Python's `reconnect` is `ReconnectPolicy | None` with no off switch, and `failures` resets to 0 on delivery, so max_attempts=0 still reconnects after a clean close that delivered events.

Neither README nor the TS doc comment (types.ts:108, 'default 90 000 ms') says that 0 disables the watchdog, so no documented contract is broken. Python's `or` also keeps httpx from receiving read=0 (an immediate timeout). `ReconnectPolicy.max_attempts` is documented as 'consecutive failed reconnects', which matches the behaviour. A missing `reconnect=False` is a feature-parity wish, not a defect.
findings.refined_fix: In subscribe_sync/subscribe_async: `ms = DEFAULT_IDLE_MS if idle_timeout_ms is None else idle_timeout_ms; idle_s = None if ms == 0 else ms / 1000` (open_stream already accepts None and passes it as httpx read=). Widen the `reconnect` parameter in client.py to `ReconnectPolicy | Literal[False] | None`. When it is False, return after the first drop and re-raise transient errors instead of retrying (mirror the `!reconnect` branches in sse.ts). Add real-server tests like events.test.ts.

findings.excerpt: return Number.isFinite(wait) && wait > 0 ? Math.max(base, wait + 10_000) : base;
findings.problem: The 10 s headroom added to a long-poll's `wait_ms` is an unnamed, non-configurable magic number. So is the local grace added to the deadline (line 343: `Math.min(1000, Math.max(100, Math.round(ctx.timeoutMs * 0.1)))`). The same values are duplicated in Python (_core.py:176 `wait + 10_000`, _core.py:181 `min(1000, max(100, round(timeout_ms * 0.1)))`). An operator on a high-latency link cannot tune them, and the server's `Request-Timeout` handling is not documented against them.
findings.proposed_fix: Introduce named, documented constants (`LONG_POLL_HEADROOM_MS`, `LOCAL_DEADLINE_GRACE_*`) and expose them through the existing client options (for example `longPollHeadroomMs`). Add one test that a configured value reaches the `Request-Timeout` header, against a real ag-server.
reasons: The 10_000 ms long-poll headroom (transport.ts:261, _core.py:176) and the 100..1000 ms / 10 % local grace (transport.ts:343, _core.py:181) are unnamed and duplicated in both SDKs. The finding overstates the tuning problem, because a per-call `timeoutMs`/`timeout_ms` overrides the headroom entirely. It is a naming and duplication issue only.

timeoutFor (transport.ts:257) and timeout_ms_for (_core.py:173) return the per-call `timeoutMs`/`timeout_ms` first, and `requestTimeoutMs` is a client option. A high-latency operator therefore already has an override. The +10 s headroom and the 10% grace are small deterministic heuristics, and the code states what they do. Naming the constants would be a style nit.
findings.refined_fix: Name the values in both SDKs: `LONG_POLL_HEADROOM_MS = 10_000`, `DEADLINE_GRACE_MIN_MS = 100`, `DEADLINE_GRACE_MAX_MS = 1000`, `DEADLINE_GRACE_FRACTION = 0.1`, each with a comment. Mention in the README's deadline section that wait_ms calls get wait_ms + 10 s unless `timeoutMs`/`timeout_ms` is given. No new client option is needed.

findings.excerpt: const QUERY_CSV = new Set(['topics']);
findings.problem: Query-array serialisation is chosen by the parameter name, in the generic transport (Python: _core.py:28 `_QUERY_CSV = frozenset({"topics"})`). openapi.json declares events.replay's `topics` as an array with no `style`/`explode` (OpenAPI default is repeated keys) and events.subscribe's `topics` as a comma-separated string. The server really wants commas for both. Operation-specific knowledge is therefore buried in transport code, and any future array parameter named `topics` would be mis-encoded.
findings.proposed_fix: Fix openapi.json (`style: form, explode: false` for events.replay `topics`, array type for subscribe) or add a per-operation `csvQuery` entry to api-policy.json. Have both generators emit the list into OPERATIONS, and make buildRequest/build_request use it instead of a global name set. Verify against a real ag-server with the existing events.replay topic-filter tests.
reasons: transport.ts:80 (`QUERY_CSV = new Set(['topics'])`) and _core.py:28 key array encoding on the parameter name. openapi.json declares events.replay `topics` as an array with no style/explode, while the server (http.rs:1261/1309) splits on commas for both routes, so the spec and the wire format disagree and the SDK compensates by name in generic transport code.

The server really parses `topics` as a comma-separated string (http.rs:1261-1264, 1309). OpenAPI's array declaration for events.replay is the spec's imprecision, and the SDK's name-based CSV rule is a tested workaround for it (real-server topic-filter tests). A future second array parameter named `topics` is speculative. No user is hurt.
findings.refined_fix: In routes.rs, emit `"style":"form","explode":false` for array-typed query parameters of GET JSON routes, so events.replay `topics` carries it. Have both generators read `explode === false` and emit a per-operation `csvQuery: ['topics']` in OPERATIONS. Make buildRequest/build_request use `op.csvQuery` instead of the global set and delete QUERY_CSV/_QUERY_CSV. The existing events.replay topic-filter tests against ag-server stay as the guard.

findings.problem: The `objects.upload` batch size 1000 is an unnamed constant, duplicated in Python (client.py:170-171 and 201-202). The server publishes its real limit in `NegotiateResponse.limits.max_batch` (10 000 today, crates/ag-protocol/src/lib.rs:58), but the SDK never reads it. If the limit changes, upload either under-uses it or breaks.
findings.proposed_fix: Define a named constant. Better, cache `limits.max_batch` from `negotiate()` (or fetch it lazily with `session.negotiate`) and use `min(limit, default)` as the chunk size. Test against a real ag-server by uploading more objects than the batch size.
reasons: client.ts:149 and client.py:170-171/201-202 use an unnamed, duplicated 1000 chunk size for objects.missing. The server limit is the compile-time MAX_BATCH = 10_000 (ag-protocol/src/lib.rs:58, advertised in negotiate), so 1000 is safe today and merely under-uses it. This is a magic-number and duplication issue, not a bug.

1000 is well below the server limit MAX_BATCH = 10 000 (ag-protocol/src/lib.rs:58, enforced at ag-server/src/api/objects.rs:153), so it is a safe conservative chunk size and can neither break nor mis-upload. Reading negotiate limits would add a round trip for no practical gain. At worst this is a cosmetic duplicated constant.
findings.refined_fix: Add `const MISSING_BATCH = 1000` in client.ts and `_MISSING_BATCH = 1000` in client.py with a comment that it must stay <= limits.max_batch (10_000), and use it in the loops. Reading negotiate's limits.max_batch is optional.

findings.excerpt: if (connectedAt > 0 && Date.now() - connectedAt > 5000) failures = 0;
findings.problem: The 5 s 'connection was stable' window that resets the reconnect failure counter is an undocumented magic number (Python: _events.py:104 and 164 `> 5`). It cannot be changed through `ReconnectOptions` or `ReconnectPolicy`.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `stableAfterMs` to ReconnectOptions and `stable_after_ms` to ReconnectPolicy, default 5000, documented in both READMEs.
reasons: sse.ts:198 (`> 5000`) and _events.py:104/164 (`> 5`) are a hard-coded, undocumented 'stable connection' window. ReconnectOptions and ReconnectPolicy do not expose it. It is on the production reconnect path.

The 5 s 'stable connection' window only decides when the consecutive-failure counter resets in a deterministic backoff algorithm (sse.ts:198, _events.py:104/164). Base and max delay and max attempts are configurable. The window is an internal tuning detail whose absence harms no operator.
findings.refined_fix: Add `stableAfterMs?: number` (default 5000) to ReconnectOptions/DEFAULT_RECONNECT and `stable_after_ms: int = 5000` to ReconnectPolicy. Use `reconnect.stableAfterMs` / `policy.stable_after_ms / 1000` in the comparisons, and document it in the Events sections of both READMEs.

findings.problem: `headers()` takes a `hasBody` parameter, and all three callers compute and pass it (lines 229, 299, 329). The function never reads it. This is a dead argument that suggests behaviour, such as Content-Length or Expect handling, that does not exist.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove the parameter and the computations at 229 and 329, or implement what it was meant for.
reasons: Transport.headers() declares `hasBody: boolean` (transport.ts:299), and the three callers compute it (:229 false, :329 `built.hasJsonBody || op.body === 'bytes'`), but the function body never reads `h.hasBody`. It is a dead argument on a path every request takes.

Confirmed that `hasBody` is never read in headers() (transport.ts: only the type at 299 and the two callers at 229/329; line 299 is the declaration, not a third caller). It is a private method, so no user-facing behaviour is implied or misreported. This is a trivial dead-field cleanup with no operator impact.
findings.refined_fix: Remove `hasBody: boolean;` from the parameter type of headers() (transport.ts:299) and delete the `hasBody:` property at the call sites at :229 and :329. `built.hasJsonBody` is still used at :180 and :332, so nothing else changes.

findings.excerpt:
if event is None or event.seq <= last:
                            continue  # already delivered
findings.problem: `_event()` is annotated `Event | None` but never returns None (an `error` frame raises, everything else is decoded). The `event is None` branch in subscribe_sync (line 93) and subscribe_async (line 153) is dead, so a malformed frame can never be skipped as the code suggests.
findings.proposed_fix: Change the return type to `Event` and drop the dead check. If heartbeat-like frames without data should be skipped, handle that explicitly in the parser and test it against the real server's heartbeat_ms mode.
reasons: _events.py:42 `_event()` is annotated `Event | None`, but it either raises on an error frame or returns `decode_as(Event, ...)`, which returns T and is never None. The `event is None` checks at :93 and :153 are dead branches on the live subscription path.

_event() is annotated `Event | None` but never returns None, so the `event is None` guard is harmless dead code. It cannot change behaviour, and no malformed frame is mishandled (json.loads and decode_as raise). This is a typing nit, not a defect.
findings.refined_fix: Change the signature to `def _event(frame: SseFrame) -> Event:` and the checks at :93 and :153 to `if event.seq <= last: continue`.

findings.excerpt: Uint8Array.of(a.result === 'pass' ? 1 : 2),
findings.problem: Any `result` other than the exact string 'pass' is signed as 'fail' (Python signing.py:184 `bytes([1 if _get(a, "result") == "pass" else 2])`, where a missing key also becomes 'fail'). Likewise any file type other than 'symlink' is encoded as regular (changeset.ts:124, changeset.py:159). Only the TypeScript types guard this; runtime and Python callers get a silently wrong signature or changeset instead of an error.
findings.proposed_fix: Validate explicitly and throw `TypeError`/`ValueError` for any value outside {'pass','fail'} and {'regular','symlink'} (and for a missing `result`). Add unit tests plus a real-server upload of a symlink and an attestation.
reasons: signing.ts:187 encodes `a.result === 'pass' ? 1 : 2` and signing.py:184 does the same, where a missing key reads as None via _get and becomes 2. changeset.ts:124 and changeset.py:159 treat anything other than 'symlink' as regular. Neighbouring code in changeset.ts throws TypeError for other bad inputs, so unchecked JS/Python callers get a wrong signature or changeset instead of an error. These are public SDK functions.

The encoding mirrors the server's two-valued enum (ag-policy/src/attestation.rs:86 `Pass => 1, Fail => 2`). `result` is typed 'pass'|'fail' in TS, and `file_type` is `Literal['regular','symlink']` in Python (changeset.py:26). A wrong value in an attestation still fails loudly, because the server's strict enum or signature check rejects it. Extra runtime validation would be nice-to-have, but nothing misleads an operator.
findings.refined_fix: TS: `if (a.result !== 'pass' && a.result !== 'fail') throw new TypeError(...)` in attestationSigningBytes, and in changeset.ts after `const fileType = op.fileType ?? 'regular'` add `if (fileType !== 'regular' && fileType !== 'symlink') throw new TypeError(...)`. Python: the same checks raising ValueError, using `_get(a, "result")` before building the byte. Add unit tests for the rejections.

findings.problem: The package version is duplicated by hand: pyproject.toml:7, sdk/typescript/package.json:3 and this line. Nothing checks that they agree, and the SDK never reports its version to the server (`negotiate()` sends client_name/client_version only if the caller supplies them).
findings.proposed_fix: Read the version at runtime from `importlib.metadata.version('agentgit-client')`, or generate the module from pyproject. Add a CI check that the Python and npm versions match, and send `client_name`/`client_version` by default in `negotiate()`.
reasons: Partly refuted: scripts/check_publish_metadata.py:117/129 already checks package.json and pyproject.toml against the workspace version, in packaging.yml:88 and publish-sdks.yml:41. What is unchecked is `agentgit.__version__ = "0.1.0"` (__init__.py:80), a third hand-copied literal that no test or script compares. negotiate() sends client_name/client_version only when the caller supplies them (client.py:139-145).

Three copies of '0.1.0' (pyproject.toml:7, package.json:3, __init__.py:80) in an alpha SDK are routine release bookkeeping. No operator is misled, since the SDKs are unpublished. Passing client_name/client_version to negotiate is an optional parameter by design.
findings.refined_fix: In check_pypi() of scripts/check_publish_metadata.py, read sdk/python/src/agentgit/__init__.py, `m = re.search(r'^__version__ = "([^"]+)"', text, re.M)`, and call bad() unless m and m.group(1) == proj['version'] (add `import re` if absent). Alternatively define `__version__` with `importlib.metadata.version('agentgit-client')`.

findings.excerpt: check(Object.keys(m.OPERATIONS).length === 91, `${name}: 91 operations`);
findings.problem: The package check hardcodes the operation count (the READMEs say '91 operations' too: typescript/README.md:7, python/README.md:8). It fails on every legitimate API addition, and the READMEs go stale silently.
findings.proposed_fix: Compare with the number of operations in docs/protocol/openapi.json read at check time. Generate the number in the READMEs, or drop it from the prose.
reasons: verify-package.mjs:40 hard-codes `=== 91`, and the 91 is repeated in the READMEs (typescript:7, python:8) and docs/guides/sdks.md:5. docs/protocol/openapi.json now has 92 operations (session.auth_config, added by commit fbdabd4) while the generated SDK has 91, so the check will fail on the next regeneration.

The hard-coded 91 in verify-package.mjs is a tripwire for the package smoke test. Real consistency with the spec is already enforced dynamically (all-operations.test.ts:311-334 compares OPERATIONS with the ids in openapi.json and requires every operation to be reached). The READMEs' '91' is prose that goes stale at worst by a number, so nobody is misled.
findings.refined_fix: In verify-package.mjs read the spec: `const spec = JSON.parse(readFileSync(path.resolve(root, '../../docs/protocol/openapi.json'), 'utf8')); const expected = Object.values(spec.paths).flatMap(p => Object.values(p)).filter(o => o && o.operationId).length;` then `check(Object.keys(m.OPERATIONS).length === expected, `${name}: ${expected} operations`)`. Reword the READMEs and docs/guides/sdks.md to 'every operation' or add the count to the doc-sync check.

findings.excerpt: - **No runtime dependencies.** `fetch`, `AbortSignal` and `ReadableStream` are the only platform APIs used.
findings.problem: The code also uses `globalThis.crypto.getRandomValues` (encoding.ts:128), `TextEncoder`/`TextDecoder`, `Headers`, `Response`, `URLSearchParams`, `AbortController`, `DOMException` and timers. The sentence understates the platform requirements, and the README itself says the package 'has not been run in a browser'.
findings.proposed_fix: List the real requirements (Web Crypto `getRandomValues`, Fetch API, Streams, TextEncoder) or drop the 'only' claim. Add a smoke test that loads the built package under a minimal global surface, or run the suite in a browser-like runtime.
reasons: typescript/README.md:11 says fetch, AbortSignal and ReadableStream 'are the only platform APIs used', but the source also uses globalThis.crypto.getRandomValues (encoding.ts:128), TextEncoder/TextDecoder (encoding.ts:5-6, sse.ts:33), Headers, URLSearchParams, AbortController, DOMException (transport.ts:50) and timers. The claim is inaccurate.

The sentence is loose shorthand: encoding.ts uses globalThis.crypto.getRandomValues, and sse.ts/encoding.ts use TextEncoder/TextDecoder. But the same README states 'Node 20 or newer' and that it 'has not been run in a browser', and Node 20 provides all of these, so no supported user is misled. This is at most a wording nit.
findings.refined_fix: Reword to: '**No runtime dependencies.** It uses only standard platform APIs: fetch/Headers/URLSearchParams, AbortController/AbortSignal, ReadableStream, TextEncoder/TextDecoder, DOMException and Web Crypto `getRandomValues`.' Do not add a browser smoke test, since the README already says it has not been run in a browser.

findings.excerpt: * **Python 3.10 or newer.** The test suite passes on 3.10, 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13; newer versions are not run here.
findings.problem: CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml, `sdk` job, lines 168-195) runs the Python SDK on a single interpreter (`uv sync` default) and the TypeScript SDK on Node 22 only. The claims 'passes on 3.10-3.13' (and the TypeScript README line 13, 'tests were run on 20.20 and 22.22', with `engines.node >=20`) are not backed by any automated matrix.
findings.proposed_fix: Add matrix jobs: python-version [3.10, 3.11, 3.12, 3.13] with `uv run --python`, and node [20, 22], each running the real-server suite. Otherwise narrow the claim to what CI actually runs.
reasons: The `sdk` job in ci.yml:168-195 runs Node 22 and a single default Python (`uv sync`, no .python-version or matrix), and publish-sdks.yml and packaging.yml also use Node 22 only. python/README.md:14 says the suite 'passes on 3.10, 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13' and package.json declares node >=20, so no automation backs the multi-version claim. The TypeScript line is a past-tense statement and is not false.

The README sentences are accurate statements of what was run ('the tests were run on 20.20 and 22.22'; 'newer versions are not run here'). pyproject pins requires-python >=3.10, and ruff target-version py310 and mypy python_version 3.10 statically enforce 3.10 syntax. I found no 3.11+-only features in src. A CI matrix would be good hygiene but nothing is misrepresented.
findings.refined_fix: In ci.yml, give the sdk job `strategy.matrix: { python: ['3.10','3.11','3.12','3.13'], node: [20, 22] }`, set `node-version: ${{ matrix.node }}`, and run `uv sync --python ${{ matrix.python }}` and `uv run --python ${{ matrix.python }} pytest`. Or, to avoid a 4x server build, narrow the README sentences to the versions CI runs.

findings.excerpt: cargo build --release --locked -p ag-server -p ag-cli  (no Node stage; deploy/docker/ag-server.toml and deploy/*/ag-server.toml never set `web_dir`)
findings.problem: docs/guides/web-ui.md:22-27 and README ("Clients: a Web UI") describe a Web UI served by ag-server, but the image has no UI build and none of the shipped configs set `server.web_dir`. A Compose or Kubernetes deployment has no Web UI; the operator must run `npm ci && npm run build` by hand and mount the dist directory. The roadmap task 'embed UI in ag-server' is still open.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a Node build stage to the Dockerfile (apps/web `npm ci && npm run build`), copy dist to /usr/share/agentgit/web and set `web_dir` in deploy/docker/ag-server.toml; or embed the dist in the binary (include_dir / rust-embed). Verify in the CI `images` job by `curl`ing `/` and asserting the app's index.html and the CSP headers from the running container.
reasons: The embedding mechanism now exists (cargo feature `ui` on by default, crates/ag-ui-assets/build.rs). But deploy/docker/Dockerfile has no Node stage, .dockerignore excludes apps/web, and neither release.yml nor containers.yml runs scripts/build_ui.sh or sets AG_UI_DIST (only web.yml does). So the shipped image and the release binaries embed an empty asset table and serve the 'UI not built' page, despite scripts/build_ui.sh and docs/guides/web-ui.md saying 'Release and CI builds run this first'.

Still true, though the web_dir part is obsolete. ag-server now embeds the UI through the default-on `ui` feature and the ag-ui-assets crate, but deploy/docker/Dockerfile has no Node stage and neither does release.yml (`grep -i node` finds nothing). .dockerignore also excludes apps/web. A Docker image or release binary therefore gets the empty 'UI not built' stub. docs/guides/web-ui.md says 'Release and CI builds run scripts/build_ui.sh', which is false for both. dev/handoff/web.md lists the Dockerfile stage as an open to-do.
findings.refined_fix: 1) Dockerfile: add `FROM node:22-bookworm-slim AS ui` (Node must be >=22.18, so pin a node:22.x tag that satisfies it), `WORKDIR /src/apps/web`, `COPY apps/web/ ./`, `RUN npm ci && npm run build`. Run npm directly and not scripts/build_ui.sh, whose final `touch crates/ag-ui-assets/build.rs` fails inside this stage because crates/ is absent. 2) In the `build` stage, after `cargo chef cook` and the `COPY . .`, add `COPY --from=ui /src/apps/web/dist apps/web/dist` and `RUN touch crates/ag-ui-assets/build.rs` before the final `cargo build`. 3) .dockerignore: add `!apps/web` plus `apps/web/dist` and `apps/web/test-results` to the exclusions. 4) release.yml `binaries` job: add `actions/setup-node@v4` (node 22) and `run: scripts/build_ui.sh` before the Build step. 5) Assert the result: in containers.yml (image job) and in the release smoke, `curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:PORT/ | grep -q '<div id="app"'` and `! grep -q 'Web UI is not built'`.

findings.excerpt: expr: up{job="agentgit"} == 0   (source: alerts.yml:7; servicemonitor.yaml:10-21 sets neither `jobLabel` nor a relabeling)
findings.problem: The generated PrometheusRule hardcodes `job="agentgit"`, which is the `job_name` of the two plain Prometheus scrape configs. A ServiceMonitor without `jobLabel` labels the series with the Service name, i.e. `job="ag-server"`. In the Operator overlay `up{job="agentgit"}` therefore matches no series and AgentGitDown can never fire: the most important alert is dead exactly in the deployment mode that ships it. promtool/kubeconform cannot detect this.
findings.proposed_fix: Make the label deterministic: add `jobLabel: app.kubernetes.io/part-of` (value `agentgit`) or a `relabelings` rule setting `job=agentgit` in servicemonitor.yaml, or select the alert on `up{service="ag-server"}`/a label both modes share. Add `promtool test rules` unit tests for every alert (including a case that proves AgentGitDown fires when the target disappears) and verify in the kind CI job by killing the pod and waiting for the alert in Prometheus.
reasons: deploy/kubernetes/overlays/prometheus-operator/servicemonitor.yaml sets no `jobLabel` or relabelings, so the Operator labels series `job="ag-server"` (the Service name). prometheusrule.yaml, generated from alerts.yml, uses `up{job="agentgit"} == 0`, which matches nothing in this overlay. `job="agentgit"` exists only as the job_name in prometheus.yml and prometheus.compose.yml.

Confirmed. The generated prometheusrule.yaml has `up{job="agentgit"} == 0`. The ServiceMonitor sets no `jobLabel`, so the Operator names the job after the Service, `ag-server`. `agentgit` is only the job_name of the two static Prometheus configs. In the Operator overlay AgentGitDown therefore matches no series and can never fire. The Service already carries the label `app.kubernetes.io/part-of: agentgit`.
findings.refined_fix: In overlays/prometheus-operator/servicemonitor.yaml add `spec.jobLabel: app.kubernetes.io/part-of`. base/service.yaml already carries `app.kubernetes.io/part-of: agentgit`, so the series become `job="agentgit"` and the generated rule works unchanged. Add a check to scripts/check_deploy.py that the ServiceMonitor's jobLabel resolves to the `job` value used in alerts.yml. Optionally add a promtool unit test showing AgentGitDown fires when `up{job="agentgit"}` is 0.

findings.excerpt:
ingress:
    - from:
        - podSelector: {}
      ports: [{protocol: TCP, port: 8080}]   (ingress-nginx rule is commented out, lines 18-21)
findings.problem: The only shipped ingress rule admits pods of the same namespace. The Prometheus Operator overlay adds a ServiceMonitor, but Prometheus normally runs in another namespace (e.g. monitoring), so its scrapes of /metrics are dropped by the shipped policy, as is traffic from any ingress controller. The base+overlay combination is internally inconsistent and the user must discover and edit it.
findings.proposed_fix: Ship the overlay with a NetworkPolicy patch admitting the Prometheus namespace (configurable via a kustomize patch/replacement, default `monitoring`) and document or provide an ingress overlay. Verify in the kind job by scraping from a pod in a different namespace.
reasons: base/networkpolicy.yaml admits only `podSelector: {}` (same namespace), and its only cross-namespace example is a commented ingress-nginx rule. The prometheus-operator overlay adds a ServiceMonitor and no NetworkPolicy change, so a Prometheus in another namespace (the usual kube-prometheus-stack layout) cannot reach :8080 and every scrape fails until the user edits the policy.

The base NetworkPolicy admits only `podSelector: {}` (same namespace). Its comment says to add a rule for Prometheus if it runs elsewhere, but the 'examples below' only show ingress-nginx. The prometheus-operator overlay adds a ServiceMonitor and a PrometheusRule but no matching ingress rule, and deployment.md/observability.md do not mention this. With the usual cross-namespace Prometheus, scrapes are silently dropped on an enforcing CNI, and with the job-label bug (finding 5) no alert fires either.
findings.refined_fix: In overlays/prometheus-operator/kustomization.yaml add a patch targeting NetworkPolicy/ag-server: `- op: add`, `path: /spec/ingress/-`, `value: {from: [{namespaceSelector: {matchLabels: {kubernetes.io/metadata.name: monitoring}}}], ports: [{protocol: TCP, port: 8080}]}`. Comment that `monitoring` must be changed to Prometheus's namespace. Mention it in docs/operations/deployment.md and in the ServiceMonitor header comment.

findings.excerpt:
alert: AgentGitSlowRequests
 expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(agwp_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m]))) > 5   (same query shape in dashboard panels 'Latency (all operations)' agentgit-overview.json:104 and 'Slowest operations (p95)' :164)
findings.problem: agwp_request_duration_seconds is observed for every operation (crates/ag-server/src/app.rs:229 `started.elapsed()`), including long-poll operations by design: `jobs.claim` and `streams.head` wait up to 30 s (api/jobs.rs:37, api/streams.rs:14) and `events.subscribe` is a stream. Idle execution-plane workers poll continuously, so p99 sits at multiple seconds and the 5 s alert flaps or is permanently firing, and the description ('check storage latency') is misleading; the dashboard panels are skewed the same way.
findings.proposed_fix: Exclude long-poll/streaming operations from the SLO latency query (`operation!~"jobs.claim|streams.head|events.subscribe"`) or record them in a separate histogram/with a `long_poll` label; derive the exclusion list from the server's route table instead of hand-typing it. Add `promtool test rules` cases with idle-worker-shaped series, and check the dashboard against a real server with an idle ag-worker.
reasons: App::dispatch (app.rs) observes agwp_request_duration_seconds for every operation, including jobs.claim, which long-polls up to MAX_WAIT_MS=30 s (ag-worker default wait is 20 s). stream.head also long-polls, and events.subscribe goes through dispatch as well. alerts.yml AgentGitSlowRequests and the dashboard 'Latency (all operations)' and 'Slowest operations (p95)' panels aggregate all operations without excluding them. On a quiet server with idle workers p99 sits near 20 s, so the 5 s alert fires. Note the HTTP op name is `stream.head`, not `streams.head`.

Confirmed. app.rs:279 observes `agwp_request_duration_seconds` for every dispatched operation, and jobs.claim and events.subscribe are dispatched through the same path. ag-worker claims with wait_ms=20 s by default (capped at 30 s by the server). The alert and three dashboard queries aggregate over all operations (`sum by (le)` or `by (le, operation)`). On a quiet server a few idle workers make long polls more than 1% of samples, so p99 sits at about 20 s and AgentGitSlowRequests fires permanently. Its description ('check storage latency') then points the wrong way.
findings.refined_fix: In deploy/observability/alerts.yml change the AgentGitSlowRequests selector to `rate(agwp_request_duration_seconds_bucket{operation!~"jobs.claim|stream.head|events.subscribe"}[5m])` and fix the description (it should not blame storage only). Apply the same matcher to the three quantile queries in the 'Latency (all operations)' panel and the 'Slowest operations (p95)' topk panel in grafana/dashboards/agentgit-overview.json. Regenerate kubernetes/overlays/prometheus-operator/prometheusrule.yaml with scripts/gen_prometheusrule.py. Add a promtool rule test with idle-worker-shaped series.

findings.excerpt:
debug:
    verbosity: basic ... exporters: [debug]   (comment line 16: "Prints a summary of what arrives. Replace or extend with a real backend")
findings.problem: The collector wired up by `docker compose --profile observability` (compose.yaml:87-93) terminates every trace in a `debug` exporter that only prints counts. No trace backend exists in the profile and Grafana has no tracing datasource, so 'OpenTelemetry traces' (README, observability.md) are collected and discarded; the Compose server config even leaves `otlp_endpoint` commented out (ag-server.toml:21-22), so with the shipped defaults no spans are ever produced.
findings.proposed_fix: Add Grafana Tempo (or Jaeger) to the observability profile, export through `otlphttp` to it, provision a Tempo datasource in Grafana and enable `otlp_endpoint = "http://otel-collector:4318"` in the compose server config when the profile is active (env-substituted). Verify in the Compose CI job by creating a proposal and querying Tempo's search API for the span `proposals.create`.
reasons: deploy/observability/otel-collector.yaml has a single `debug` exporter (verbosity basic) and the traces pipeline exports only to it. The observability profile in compose.yaml has no Tempo or Jaeger service and Grafana has no tracing datasource. deploy/compose/ag-server.toml leaves `otlp_endpoint` commented out, so with the shipped Compose defaults no spans are produced, and any that arrived would be discarded.

A placeholder sink that is openly labelled. otel-collector.yaml says in a comment that the `debug` exporter 'prints a summary ... replace or extend with a real backend' and shows an otlphttp example. The Compose server config also comments `otlp_endpoint` with the instruction to enable it with the profile. The server's exporter is real and covered by tests; the choice of trace backend is left to the deployer. That is an accurate, documented demo default, not a hidden stub.
findings.refined_fix: Add a `tempo` service (profile observability) to compose.yaml. Add an `otlphttp/tempo` exporter to otel-collector.yaml pointing at it and use it in the traces pipeline. Provision a Tempo datasource under grafana/provisioning/datasources. Ship a compose override or second server config enabling `otlp_endpoint = "http://otel-collector:4318"` when the profile is on. Extend scripts/e2e_observability.py to run an operation and query Tempo's search API for the `proposals.create` span.

findings.excerpt:
/// Externally visible base URL (for links in responses and OIDC redirects).
    pub public_url: Option<String>,
findings.problem: The configuration key is parsed, stored and documented as driving links and OIDC redirects, but nothing in the server reads it (zero uses outside config.rs). Operators who set it behind a proxy get no effect and no warning.
findings.proposed_fix: Either implement it (use it for absolute URLs in responses/`capabilities` and for any OIDC redirect/discovery logic, validate it is an http(s) URL) with a server test asserting the emitted URLs, or remove the key and its documentation so that `deny_unknown_fields` rejects it.
reasons: crates/ag-server/src/config.rs:66-70 declares `pub public_url: Option<String>` with the doc comment 'for links in responses and OIDC redirects'. It is set to None in Default and referenced nowhere else under crates/ (grep finds only these two lines), and no docs or deploy files mention it. ServerSection has `deny_unknown_fields`, so the key is accepted but does nothing, with no warning.

Confirmed. `public_url` exists only in config.rs (field, doc comment, default `None`). `grep -rn public_url` finds no reader in crates/, no docs and no deploy configs. The comment promises it drives response links and OIDC redirects. ServerSection uses `deny_unknown_fields`, so the key is accepted silently and does nothing. An operator behind a proxy who sets it is misled.
findings.refined_fix: Remove the `public_url` field and its `public_url: None` initializer from ServerSection in crates/ag-server/src/config.rs. `deny_unknown_fields` then rejects configs that set it. Add a config test asserting that `[server] public_url = "..."` is rejected. If a feature is wanted instead, implement and test it, validating that the value is an http(s) URL.

findings.excerpt: "Checks (all must pass; used by CI)"; README.md:359-362: "test names and commands mentioned in docs are verified against the code (`scripts/check_docs.py`)" (README.ru.md:365-367 same)

The README's and docs/README.md's 'the docs are checked' claim is false for link rot, renamed tests and non-existent commands; the script's command check is also silently skipped when no `ag` binary is found (line 128).
